title: TG-04c: Voice handler error-reply mapper (TranscriptionError + TelegramDownloadError -> PRD §13 strings)
description:
## Goal
Pure function that converts the failure modes from the voice pipeline into the user-facing reply strings the bot will send back. Per PRD §13, each error tells the user (a) what happened, (b) what they can do, (c) whether anything is lost. Splitting this out lets it land independently of the inbox writer (calmly-unr / TG-03b lives on a separate branch in flight).

## Scope
- `server/src/telegram/handlers/voiceReplies.ts`
  - export `voiceReplyForDownloadError(err: TelegramDownloadError): string` — covers too_large, not_found, auth, network, timeout, unsupported
  - export `voiceReplyForTranscriptionError(err: TranscriptionError): string` — covers provider_error, audio_too_long, unsupported_format, auth, quota, timeout
  - export `voiceReplyForTooLongDuration(durationSec: number, limitSec: number): string` — for the 5-min cap
  - export `voiceReplySuccess(transcript: string): string` — "Saved to inbox: <first 80 chars of transcript>…" with truncation marker
  - All replies are short (ADHD principle); no PII echoed (transcript echoed only in success ack and only first 80 chars)
- Tests: `server/src/telegram/handlers/__tests__/voiceReplies.test.ts`
  - one test per error code per type, asserting the reply string matches the expected copy
  - success ack: short transcript echoed verbatim; long transcript truncated at 80 chars + ellipsis; empty transcript edge case (handler should never call with empty, but guard)

## Acceptance
- pnpm typecheck:gated passes (no new errors vs baseline)
- vitest run passes for the new suite (>= 14 tests covering all branches)
- voiceReplies.ts < 150 LOC
- No imports from telegram dispatcher / handlers / inbox (pure function)

## Out of scope (TG-04 final assembly will pick up)
- Voice handler orchestration (dispatcher route + 5-min check + retry retention + ack send)
- InboxItem creation
- Calling getFile / transcribe

## Notes
- Copy follows PRD §13 principle: "Each state must tell the user: what happened, what they can do next, whether anything is lost." Keep replies under ~140 chars where possible; one sentence preferred.
- Transcript echo in success ack: 80 chars max + ellipsis. Use grapheme-naive substring (server only, audit for unicode safety later if needed).
- Do NOT log the transcript at info level (PII).
notes:
Approach: pure module — three error → reply functions (download, transcription, too-long-duration), plus a success-ack helper. No imports beyond TG-04a/4b error types. Tests use plain TranscriptionError / TelegramDownloadError instances and assert returned strings.

Tradeoffs: hard-coding copy here vs. a copy-strings table or i18n system. PRD has no mention of i18n in MVP, so inline literals are fine; a future i18n pass would replace these.

Not doing: logger calls (handler logs), retry-state strings ("I'll retry within an hour" requires the handler to actually be retrying — keep this module stateless and have the handler choose between immediate-failure vs. queued-retry copy).
close_reason: Closed

title: Self-hostable sync server: OSS release packaging
description:
## Goal
Package the sync server as a clean OSS release so users can self-host instead of using hosted sync. Hosted sync remains included with the license; this is the open-source path.

## Build order
PRD §23 step 10 — explicitly deferred per PRD §26 (tension: cloud-first vs self-host).

## Scope
- Extract sync server to a standalone repo (or workspace) with permissive OSS license
- Dockerfile + docker-compose for one-command self-host
- Configuration docs (DB, secrets, OAuth callback URLs, Telegram webhook, magic-link email provider)
- Migration tooling
- Desktop client config: point at custom sync server URL
- Release pipeline: tagged releases, checksums

## Out of scope
- Migrating users between hosted and self-host (manual export/import is enough at MVP)

## Done when
A new operator can clone the OSS sync repo, run `docker compose up`, point a fresh desktop client at it, sign in via magic link, and complete a capture-to-review loop.

## References
PRD §19 Pricing/Packaging, §20 Architecture, §22 Risks (cloud-first vs self-host), §26 Tensions Carried Forward.
close_reason: All children closed

title: OSS-01: Extract sync server as OSS-ready package (LICENSE, README, CONTRIBUTING, COC, SECURITY)
description:
## Goal
Extract the sync server into a clean, OSS-ready package — license, README, CONTRIBUTING, code of conduct — so external operators can self-host without inheriting any of the desktop / Telegram-bot / hosted-only assumptions.

## Scope
- Confirm `server/` workspace is a self-contained, importable-on-its-own deployable; remove or guard any internal-only dependencies (private utilities, hosted-only env vars)
- Add `server/LICENSE` (Apache-2.0 or MIT — pick one explicitly; document why in CONTRIBUTING)
- Add `server/README.md`: project description, what it does, what it doesn't do, quickstart link to docker-compose, links to config docs
- Add `server/CONTRIBUTING.md`: dev setup, test commands, PR process, issue triage labels
- Add `server/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md` (Contributor Covenant 2.1 standard)
- Add `server/SECURITY.md` (private security disclosure email + response SLA)
- `server/package.json` `name` becomes a publishable name (e.g., `calmly-sync-server`); set `repository`, `homepage`, `bugs`
- Strip references to the hosted-only telemetry/crash endpoints — those endpoints should still exist but be optional / disable-by-default in self-host
- Add a `SELF_HOSTING.md` index pointing to the dedicated docs (built in `oss_config_docs`)

## Files
- `server/LICENSE`
- `server/README.md`
- `server/CONTRIBUTING.md`
- `server/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md`
- `server/SECURITY.md`
- `server/SELF_HOSTING.md` (skeleton — fleshed out in `oss_config_docs`)
- `server/package.json` (metadata fields)

## Acceptance
- A reviewer can clone only `server/` (no other workspace) and read README + CONTRIBUTING and understand how to start
- License is unambiguously chosen and present
- `pnpm --filter @calmly/server build` still passes after metadata + dependency cleanup
- No internal-only env var is required to start the server in OSS mode (verify by booting with the documented minimum env set)

## Notes
- This task does NOT split the repo into a separate Git repo; it makes the workspace OSS-ready in place. Repo split is a logistics step at release time.
- Dockerfile + compose is the next task (`oss_dockerfile_compose`).

## References
PRD §19 Pricing/Packaging ("Optional self-hostable sync server — published as open source"), §20 Architecture (optional self-host build), §22 (cloud-first vs self-host risk), §26 (tension carried forward), §23 step 10.
close_reason: Closed

title: OSS-02: Dockerfile + docker-compose for one-command self-host (Postgres included)
description:
## Goal
Ship a production-grade `Dockerfile` and `docker-compose.yml` so a new operator can run `docker compose up` and have a working sync server (with Postgres) reachable on a known port.

## Scope
- Multi-stage `server/Dockerfile`:
  - Stage 1: build with pnpm + node 20; install deps, run `pnpm --filter @calmly/server build`
  - Stage 2: minimal `node:20-slim` runtime; copy build output + production node_modules; runs as non-root user `node`
  - Healthcheck pinging `/health`
  - Image labels: `org.opencontainers.image.source`, `version`, `licenses`
- `deploy/docker-compose.yml` (separate from the dev compose at repo root):
  - `sync` service built from `server/Dockerfile`
  - `postgres:16` service with named volume `calmly_pg_data`
  - Healthcheck-aware `depends_on` so `sync` waits for Postgres
  - Env-driven config via `.env` (template `deploy/.env.example`)
  - Default ports: sync `:3001`, Postgres internal-only
  - Migration job runs once on startup (entrypoint or separate one-shot service)
- `deploy/README.md`: quickstart (clone, copy `.env.example`, generate secrets, `docker compose up`)

## Files
- `server/Dockerfile`
- `server/.dockerignore`
- `deploy/docker-compose.yml`
- `deploy/.env.example`
- `deploy/README.md`

## Acceptance
- `docker compose -f deploy/docker-compose.yml up -d` results in a healthy sync server reachable at `http://localhost:3001/health`
- Migrations run automatically on first up; subsequent `up` is idempotent (no re-running of completed migrations)
- Container runs as non-root; image size is reasonable (target < 300 MB)
- Stopping and restarting preserves data via the named Postgres volume
- Image builds on linux/amd64 and linux/arm64

## Notes
- Configuration docs (env var reference, OAuth callback URLs, Telegram webhook, magic-link email) are written in `oss_config_docs`.
- Migration tooling polish (rollback notes, backups) is `oss_migrations_polish`.

## References
PRD §19 Pricing/Packaging (self-hostable), §20 Architecture (optional self-host build), §23 step 10.
close_reason: Closed

title: OSS-03: Self-hosting configuration docs (env vars, OAuth callbacks, Telegram webhook, email)
description:
## Goal
Write the configuration documentation an operator needs to take a self-hosted sync server from "container running" to "fully wired with auth, calendars, and Telegram" — covering every required env var, every external callback URL, and every secret-generation step.

## Scope
- Document every env var consumed by the server, grouped by domain:
  - Core: `DATABASE_URL`, `PORT`, `LOG_LEVEL`, `NODE_ENV`
  - Secrets: `SESSION_SECRET`, `MAGIC_LINK_SIGNING_SECRET` (with `openssl rand -base64 32` snippets)
  - Auth: `BASE_URL` (used to construct callback URLs)
  - Email: `EMAIL_PROVIDER` (resend|console|smtp), `RESEND_API_KEY`, SMTP fields if relevant, `EMAIL_FROM`
  - Calendar OAuth: `GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID`, `GOOGLE_CLIENT_SECRET`, `MS_CLIENT_ID`, `MS_CLIENT_SECRET`, callback paths
  - Telegram: `TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN`, `TELEGRAM_WEBHOOK_SECRET`, webhook URL (`{BASE_URL}/telegram/webhook`)
- For each external service, exact step-by-step setup:
  - Google Cloud Console: create OAuth client, add redirect URI `{BASE_URL}/auth/google/callback`, scopes
  - Microsoft Entra ID: app registration, redirect URI, delegated permissions for Calendar.Read
  - Resend: API key, verified sender domain
  - Telegram BotFather: create bot, get token, set webhook command
- TLS / reverse proxy guidance: a brief section on running behind nginx / Caddy / Traefik with HTTPS (required for OAuth callbacks)
- Desktop client config: how to point a client at a custom server URL (cross-references `oss_desktop_custom_server`)
- Troubleshooting section: common boot failures (bad DATABASE_URL, missing secrets, callback URL mismatch)

## Files
- `server/SELF_HOSTING.md` (full guide — was a skeleton from `oss_extract_package`)
- `server/docs/env-reference.md` (table of every env var: name, required?, default, description)
- `server/docs/oauth-google.md`
- `server/docs/oauth-microsoft.md`
- `server/docs/email-magic-link.md`
- `server/docs/telegram-webhook.md`
- `server/docs/reverse-proxy.md`

## Acceptance
- Env-reference table matches the actual config schema in `server/src/config.ts` exactly (verified by a generation/check script)
- A first-time operator following SELF_HOSTING.md end-to-end reaches a working sync + magic-link auth + at least one calendar OAuth flow
- Every callback URL is shown with a `BASE_URL` placeholder so copy-paste works after substitution
- Secret-generation snippets work on macOS, Linux, and Windows (PowerShell variant)

## Notes
- Documentation is OSS surface; keep tone neutral and operator-focused, not marketing-y.
- Don't document hosted-only secrets / endpoints in this self-host guide.

## References
PRD §19 Pricing/Packaging, §20 Architecture, §15 Calendar Integration (Google + Microsoft 365), §23 step 10.
close_reason: Closed

title: OSS-04: Migration tooling polish — idempotency, rollback notes, backup procedure
description:
## Goal
Polish the database migration tooling for self-hosters — idempotent migrations, documented rollback, and clear backup recommendations — so operators can upgrade Calmly versions without data loss.

## Scope
- Audit all existing migrations under `server/migrations/` for idempotency: every migration must be safely re-runnable (use `IF NOT EXISTS`, guarded `DO $$ BEGIN ... EXCEPTION ...`, etc., or rely on the migration runner's tracking table)
- Verify the migration runner records every applied migration in a tracking table and refuses to re-apply a completed one
- Add a migration template + brief authoring guide: forward-only style, no destructive statements without a documented rollback path, additive changes preferred
- Rollback notes: for each existing migration, document in a comment whether/how to reverse it; ship a `MIGRATIONS.md` summarizing
- Backup recommendations: documented procedure using `pg_dump` for self-hosters; suggested cadence; restore drill
- `bin/calmly-server migrate up` and `bin/calmly-server migrate status` CLI subcommands (status shows applied + pending)
- Pre-flight: server refuses to start if pending migrations exist AND `AUTO_MIGRATE=false` (operator opt-in to auto-apply)

## Files
- Audit + minor edits across `server/migrations/*.sql`
- `server/migrations/_template.sql.tmpl`
- `server/MIGRATIONS.md` (authoring guide + per-migration rollback notes)
- `server/docs/backups.md` (pg_dump procedure, restore drill)
- `server/src/cli/migrate.ts` (CLI entry)
- `server/src/db/migrationRunner.ts` (idempotency + status check)

## Acceptance
- Running `migrate up` twice in a row is a no-op the second time (idempotent)
- Running `migrate status` lists applied + pending with timestamps
- Boot with `AUTO_MIGRATE=false` and pending migrations exits non-zero with a clear message
- Backup doc procedure is verified end-to-end on a sample dataset (dump → drop schema → restore → row counts match)

## Notes
- This is polish on top of the existing migration setup from F-07; do not redesign the runner unless the audit reveals a hard issue.
- Fully automated downward rollback ("migrate down") is OUT of scope — documented manual rollback notes are sufficient at MVP self-host.

## References
PRD §19 Pricing/Packaging, §22 Risks, §23 step 10.
close_reason: Closed

title: OSS-05: Desktop client — custom sync server URL setting (Settings → Account)
description:
## Goal
Allow the desktop client to connect to a self-hosted sync server by exposing a "Custom server URL" setting under Settings → Account, so users running their own infra can swap away from the hosted endpoint.

## Scope
- Settings → Account → Sync server section:
  - Default option: "Calmly hosted (recommended)" — uses the bundled hosted URL
  - Alternative: "Custom server URL" — text input accepting a full HTTPS URL
  - Validation: HTTPS only (refuse `http://` except `localhost` for development), URL format, trailing-slash normalization
  - "Test connection" button: hits `{url}/health` and `{url}/version`; shows pass/fail with a clear error if version mismatch with desktop client
- Switching the URL signs the user out (sessions are server-bound) and clears local sync state; warn clearly before switching
- Sync state cleared on switch: cached items remain in SQLite (read-only) until next sign-in repopulates from the new server; no data loss, just sync direction reset
- Persist setting in `UserSettings` (encrypted store not required — URL is not a secret)
- Surface the active server URL on the Sign-In screen subtly ("Connecting to: <url>") so users know which server they're authenticating against

## Files
- `desktop/src/renderer/pages/Settings/Account/SyncServerSection.tsx`
- `desktop/src/main/sync/serverConfig.ts` (URL resolver: env override > user setting > bundled default)
- `desktop/src/renderer/pages/SignIn/SignIn.tsx` (show active server URL)
- `shared/src/config/serverUrl.ts` (validation + normalization)
- Migration: add `sync_server_url` field to user settings storage

## Acceptance
- Setting a valid custom URL + Test connection succeeds against a locally-running self-host (verified manually + e2e test against a stub server)
- HTTP URLs (non-localhost) are rejected with a clear error
- Switching URL warns about sign-out + sync reset; confirming clears session and reroutes to Sign In; cancelling leaves state unchanged
- Desktop with custom URL completes magic-link sign-in + a capture-to-review loop end-to-end against the self-hosted server
- Sign-In screen shows the active URL when it differs from the default

## Notes
- API version compatibility: client sends its `client-version`; server's `/version` is checked; mismatched majors show a friendly "Update Calmly or self-host server" message.
- This task pairs with `oss_dockerfile_compose` for the operator side.

## References
PRD §19 Pricing/Packaging (optional self-host), §20 Architecture, §23 step 10.
close_reason: Closed

title: OSS-06: Release pipeline — tagged GitHub releases, GHCR images, checksums
description:
## Goal
Stand up the release pipeline for the OSS sync server — tagged GitHub releases, container images published to GHCR, and SHA256 checksums — so operators can pin to a known-good version with verifiable artifacts.

## Scope
- GitHub Actions workflow `release.yml` triggered on tags matching `sync-v*`:
  - Build multi-arch container image (linux/amd64, linux/arm64) via `docker/build-push-action`
  - Push to `ghcr.io/<org>/calmly-sync:<version>` and `:latest`
  - Generate SHA256 checksums for the image digest + any tarball artifacts
  - Create a GitHub Release with notes templated from a `CHANGELOG.md` section
  - Attach checksum file to the release
- Tag convention documented: `sync-v<semver>` (separate from desktop release tags)
- `CHANGELOG.md` at `server/CHANGELOG.md` follows Keep-a-Changelog; PRs that touch `server/` must update an "Unreleased" entry (lint check)
- Image signing via `cosign` (keyless OIDC) — optional for MVP; document the verification command if signing is enabled
- Release checklist `server/RELEASING.md`: bump version, update CHANGELOG, tag, monitor workflow, smoke-test pulled image
- Pre-release smoke test: a workflow job that pulls the freshly-pushed image and runs the docker-compose against it for `/health` and one migration cycle

## Files
- `.github/workflows/release.yml`
- `server/CHANGELOG.md`
- `server/RELEASING.md`
- `.github/release-notes-template.md`
- `.github/workflows/changelog-lint.yml` (PR check that flags missing CHANGELOG entries)

## Acceptance
- Pushing a `sync-v0.1.0-test` tag triggers the workflow, produces a GHCR image, and creates a draft release with notes + checksums attached
- Pulling the published image and running `docker compose up` succeeds end-to-end
- CHANGELOG-lint check fails on a PR touching `server/` without an Unreleased entry
- `RELEASING.md` walks through a real release end-to-end (rehearsed once before close)

## Notes
- This task assumes the GitHub repo + GHCR org are set up; org-level config is operator concern, not coded here.
- Image signing is documented as a follow-up if cosign setup blocks the initial release.

## References
PRD §19 Pricing/Packaging (open source release), §23 step 10, §26 (tension: cloud-first vs self-host).
close_reason: Closed

title: OSS-07: Self-host smoke test (docker compose + AppImage + loop)
description:
## Goal
Self-host smoke test — clone OSS repo, `docker compose up`, point a fresh desktop client at it, sign in, and complete the daily loop. Validates the entire OSS-sync release path before tagging a release.

## Scope
- CI workflow `.github/workflows/oss-self-host.yml` (runs on tag pushes only)
- Steps:
  1. Spin up `docker-compose.yml` from the OSS sync repo (Postgres + sync server + Telegram bot stub) on a Linux GitHub runner
  2. Wait for `/health` → 200
  3. Configure a built desktop client (Linux AppImage from a recent main build) to point at `http://localhost:3001`
  4. Drive the client via Playwright: sign in (ConsoleEmailSender prints link → script reads it), capture an item, plan it, focus, mark done, review
  5. Tear down docker compose; assert clean shutdown
- Local dev script: `scripts/oss-smoke-test.sh` runs the same flow on a developer's machine
- Documentation: `docs/SELF_HOSTING.md` step-by-step matches what the smoke test exercises

## Files
- `.github/workflows/oss-self-host.yml`
- `scripts/oss-smoke-test.sh`
- `docs/SELF_HOSTING.md`
- `oss-sync/test/e2e/full-loop.spec.ts` (Playwright)

## Acceptance
- Workflow passes on the OSS-sync release tag
- Local script reproduces the workflow with `bash scripts/oss-smoke-test.sh`
- Docs walk a new operator from `git clone` to "loop completed" in under 10 minutes
- Tear-down leaves no orphan containers or volumes

## Skills
**Invoke `playwright-electron-debugger`** for the Playwright spec running against the AppImage on Linux — sandbox flags + display server (xvfb) configuration are skill-specific.

## Notes
- This task lives in the OSS-sync repo (extracted in OSS-01).
- It's the gate test before tagging an OSS release; ship-blocker.

## References
PRD §19 Pricing/Packaging, §20 Architecture, §26 Tensions Carried Forward.
close_reason: Decomposed into three sub-tasks: calmly-soc (Dockerfile + docker-compose + SELF_HOSTING.md), calmly-ss5 (smoke script), calmly-az5 (CI workflow + e2e spec). Dependencies chained in order.

title: Ralph permission halt: switch to bypassPermissions mode
description: Opus halted on Loop #178 with 'Permission denied for: Bash(mkdir -p .husky .github/workflows 2>&1), Write'. ALLOWED_TOOLS in .ralphrc had Bash(mkdir *) and Write but claude's permission matcher didn't accept them — likely the shell redirect (2>&1) and Write-to-new-directory cases. Switched both wrapper scripts to pass --permission-mode bypassPermissions. Safety still comes from worktree isolation + PR-mode merge gating.

title: CAL-04b: Google Calendar provider — listEvents + delta sync (singleEvents=true)
description:
## Goal
Implement Google Calendar provider for the import worker. Server-expanded recurring instances via singleEvents=true, sync token for incremental delta.

## Scope
- desktop/src/main/calendar/providers/google.ts: listEvents(account, { timeMin, timeMax }) and delta(account, syncToken)
- Use singleEvents=true&timeMin=&timeMax= so the API returns expanded instances; never expand RRULE locally
- Cancellations: rows with status='cancelled' returned by API are forwarded to caller (worker does the soft-delete)
- Persist nextSyncToken from each call so the next call uses delta endpoint
- Use access-token refresh helper from CAL-03 (calendar/refresh.ts) for 401 retry
- Tests: mock the Google API HTTP client and verify pagination, delta token round-trip, cancellation forwarding

## Acceptance
- Provider returns normalized event objects ready for upsert
- Delta call correctly uses syncToken when present
- Tests cover: first sync (no token), incremental (with token), cancellation, all-day event, recurring expansion

## Depends on
- CAL-04a (schema)
close_reason: Closed

title: AI v1.1: Ollama + OpenAI + hybrid + stuck rescue + daily planning
description:
## Goal
Expand AI to hybrid mode: add Ollama local provider, OpenAI as second cloud provider, hybrid routing UI, plus the two more demanding feature classes (stuck rescue, daily planning + replan suggestions).

## Build order
PRD §23 step 8 (AI v1.1).

## Scope
- Ollama local integration: detect Ollama running, list installed models, model picker in Settings
- OpenAI provider integration alongside Anthropic; key entry per provider
- Hybrid routing: per-action class default (triage=local, planning=cloud, etc.); user override; routing-rules editor
- Privacy mode toggle (Local-only / Allow cloud for selected actions)
- Suggestion behavior toggle (Automatic inline / On-demand only)
- "Speed vs quality" preference and "Show brief reason" toggle
- Stuck rescue AI suggestions in Focus
- Daily planning suggestions in Quick Plan / Plan
- Replan suggestions from Replan UI
- End-of-day / next-day suggestions in Review

## Out of scope
- Silent auto-rescheduling (PRD §8 explicitly out)
- Adaptive reminder AI (PRD §8)

## Done when
A user can pick Hybrid mode, configure both providers + Ollama, customize routing, and use all five higher-order AI actions (triage cleanup, Make Startable, brain-dump split, stuck rescue, daily planning) with inline failure paths.

## References
PRD §6 AI sub-modes, §16 AI Settings (full), §17 AI Technical Posture (Local Ollama + Hybrid + Fallback), §22 Risks (model variance, latency).
close_reason: Closed

title: AI11-01: Ollama integration (detect daemon, list models, picker in Settings, provider impl)
description:
## Goal
Integrate Ollama as a local AI provider: detect a running Ollama daemon, list installed models, expose a model picker in Settings, and ship a concrete `AIProvider` implementation that plugs into the orchestration layer from Epic 7.

## Scope
- Detection: HTTP probe to `http://127.0.0.1:11434/api/tags` with a 1s timeout; cached for 30s
- Model list: parse `/api/tags` response into `{ name, size, family }[]`
- Generation: implement `OllamaProvider` against `/api/generate` (or `/api/chat`); JSON-mode for structured prompts
- Settings → AI page additions:
  - Status row: "Ollama detected" / "Ollama not running [How to install]"
  - Model picker (dropdown of installed models) — persists to `user_settings.ai.localModel`
  - "Refresh" button forces re-detection
  - Disabled options from Epic 7 (`Local only`, `Hybrid`) are now enabled
- Failure cases mapped to existing `AIError` shape:
  - Ollama not running → `network` with copy "Start Ollama to use Local AI"
  - No models installed → `invalid_response` with copy "Pull a model with `ollama pull <name>`"
  - Generation timeout → `timeout`

title: AI11-03: Hybrid routing config (per-action defaults + user override + Settings editor)
description:
## Goal
Implement hybrid routing: a per-action-class mapping of where each AI prompt class runs (Local / Cloud / specific provider), with shipped defaults and a Settings UI to edit the rules.

## Scope
- Routing config shape:
  ```ts
  type ActionClass =
    | 'triage_cleanup' | 'make_startable' | 'brain_dump_split'
    | 'stuck_rescue' | 'daily_planning' | 'replan' | 'end_of_day'
  type Destination = 'local' | 'cloud:anthropic' | 'cloud:openai'
  type RoutingRules = Record<ActionClass, Destination>
  ```
- Shipped defaults (per PRD §17 hybrid intent):
  - `triage_cleanup` → local
  - `make_startable` → local
  - `brain_dump_split` → local
  - `stuck_rescue` → cloud (default cloud provider)
  - `daily_planning` → cloud
  - `replan` → cloud
  - `end_of_day` → cloud
- Resolves `cloud:anthropic` / `cloud:openai` literally; resolves bare `cloud` to user's default cloud provider
- `runAI` consults `RoutingRules` first, then mode (Off / Local only / Cloud only / Hybrid):
  - Local only forces destination to local regardless of rule
  - Cloud only forces destination to default cloud
  - Hybrid honors the rule
- Settings UI: routing-rules editor with one dropdown per ActionClass listing valid destinations (limited by what's configured: hide local options if no Ollama model picked, hide cloud options if no key)
- Per-rule "Reset to default" and a top-level "Reset all" affordance

## Files
- `desktop/src/main/ai/routing.ts` — defaults + resolver
- `desktop/src/main/ai/index.ts` — integrate resolver into `runAI` dispatch
- `shared/src/model/settings.ts` — extend AI settings with `routing`
- `desktop/src/renderer/pages/settings/RoutingRulesEditor.tsx`
- `desktop/src/renderer/pages/settings/AIPage.tsx` — mount editor under Hybrid mode
- Unit tests: `desktop/src/main/ai/__tests__/routing.test.ts`

## Acceptance

- Switching mode to "Local only" forces all classes to Ollama irrespective of rules
- Editing a rule and saving persists across restart
- "Reset to default" on `daily_planning` returns it to `cloud`
- Editor disables destinations that are not currently configured (e.g., no Ollama → local options grayed)

## Notes
- Mode switch overrides rules — do not let the user end up in a state where Local-only routes to a cloud provider.
- Document the precedence (mode > rules) in the editor copy.
- Editor is only mounted when mode = Hybrid; in Off / Local only / Cloud only, it's hidden.

title: TG-04b: Telegram file download helper (getFile + fetch + size cap)
description:
## Goal
Foundation helper for TG-04 (calmly-d0p.4): given a Telegram file_id (e.g. from message.voice.file_id), fetch the binary content and return a buffer plus metadata. Pure, testable in isolation. No fs writes — caller decides what to do with the bytes.

This split lets the helper land in parallel with calmly-unr (sonnet's TG-03b inbox writer); the TG-04 orchestration handler then composes both.

## Scope
- `server/src/telegram/files.ts`
  - export interface `TelegramFileMeta { fileId: string; sizeBytes: number; mimeType: string }`
  - export interface `DownloadedTelegramFile extends TelegramFileMeta { buffer: Buffer }`
  - export class `TelegramDownloadError extends Error { code: 'too_large' | 'not_found' | 'network' | 'timeout' | 'auth' | 'unsupported' }`
  - export `async function downloadTelegramFile(bot, params): Promise<DownloadedTelegramFile>`
    - params: `{ fileId: string; mimeType: string; maxBytes?: number; timeoutMs?: number; fetchImpl?: typeof fetch }`
    - default maxBytes: 25 MB (Whisper's hard limit)
    - default timeoutMs: 30_000
    - calls `bot.api.getFile(fileId)` to resolve file path, then `fetch(file.getUrl())` (grammy's File adds getUrl()); reads body to Buffer
    - if `file.file_size > maxBytes` -> throw TelegramDownloadError('too_large')
    - if HTTP non-2xx -> map to error code (404 -> not_found, 401/403 -> auth, 429 -> network, others -> network)
    - if AbortController fires -> throw TelegramDownloadError('timeout')
- Tests: `server/src/telegram/__tests__/files.test.ts`
  - happy path: bot.api.getFile mock returns {file_path,'file_size:1024}; fetch returns 1024 bytes -> buffer matches, mimeType passed through
  - too_large: file_size=999999999 -> rejects with code='too_large' BEFORE fetch is called
  - not_found: fetch 404 -> rejects with code='not_found'
  - auth: fetch 401 -> rejects with code='auth'
  - timeout: timeoutMs=10 with slow fetch -> rejects with code='timeout'
  - network throw: fetch throws ECONNRESET -> rejects with code='network'
  - returns sizeBytes from response body length

## Acceptance
- pnpm typecheck:gated passes (no new errors vs baseline)
- vitest run server/src/telegram/files passes (>= 6 tests)
- File <300 LOC
- Pino logging at info level does NOT include file_path or buffer content (PII safety)
- No InboxItem creation, no transcription call, no fs.writeFile — all that lives in the TG-04 orchestrator

## Out of scope (TG-04 final assembly will pick up)
- Voice dispatcher route (`bot.on('message:voice')`)
- 5-min duration check (lives in handler, post-getFile metadata)
- Transcription invocation
- InboxItem creation via createFromTelegram
- 1-hour audio retention for retry on transcription failure (handler concern)
- Reply ack copy

## Notes
- `bot.api.getFile` returns `File { file_id, file_unique_id, file_size?, file_path? }`. file_path can be null for very large files (>20 MB) — treat as 'not_found'.
- grammy's File has `.getUrl()` which constructs https://api.telegram.org/file/bot<TOKEN>/<file_path>. Use it; do NOT reconstruct the URL ourselves (token leakage risk).
- caller passes `mimeType` explicitly because Telegram puts it on the message.voice / message.audio object, not the File object.

## References
PRD §11 Capture (voice), §22 Risks (large attachments).
notes:
Approach: pure async function, takes grammy Bot + params, returns Buffer + meta. No fs, no temp files — pure orchestration concern that the TG-04 handler keeps. Errors via TelegramDownloadError class with discriminated codes (mirrors TG-04a's TranscriptionError pattern from calmly-9zr) so caller can map to PRD §13 reply strings.

Tradeoffs: pre-flight maxBytes check via file.file_size avoids a wasted fetch but Telegram occasionally omits file_size for files >20MB — we treat that as 'not_found' so the user gets "file too large" copy via PRD §13 mapping. fetchImpl is injectable for tests; mocking grammy bot.api.getFile + a fake File whose getUrl points at a stub URL.

Not doing: streaming download (audio caps at 25 MB; full buffer is fine and simpler), retry/backoff (Telegram is reliable enough; handler retains audio 1h for one retry per spec), MIME sniffing (caller provides — Telegram's message payload is authoritative).
close_reason: Closed

title: TG-09a: Mock Telegram Bot API harness for integration tests
description:
## Goal
Reusable test-time mock for the Telegram Bot API. Foundation piece of TG-09 (calmly-d0p.9): the integration-test pass needs a way to (a) replay canned `update` payloads through the dispatcher and (b) record what the bot would have sent back so assertions can verify reply shape (text, inline_keyboard, edit, etc.). Also stubs `getFile` + the file-download endpoint so the voice-handler integration tests can run without touching api.telegram.org.

This is independent of any handler — pure test harness. Splitting it lets it land while TG-04 (voice handler) and TG-09 final assembly are still composing across branches.

## Scope
- `server/test/mocks/telegramBot.ts`
  - export `class MockTelegramBotApi` mimicking the structural subset of grammy `Bot.api` used by handlers + the TelegramFileClient interface from TG-04b
  - **Outbound recording**:
    - `sendMessage(chat_id, text, opts?)` -> records, returns fake Message id
    - `editMessageText(chat_id, message_id, text, opts?)` -> records
    - `getMe()` -> returns canned bot identity
    - `getWebhookInfo()` -> returns canned webhook info
    - `getFile(file_id, signal?)` -> returns canned File payload (configurable)
    - `outbound: ReadonlyArray<{ method, args }>` accessor
    - `reset()` clears recordings + restored canned defaults
    - `setNextGetFile(file: File)` / `setNextGetFileError(err)` — per-call overrides
  - **File download stub**:
    - `fetchImpl: typeof fetch` — bound to a function that recognises `https://api.telegram.org/file/bot<token>/<path>` URLs and returns canned bytes registered via `setFileBytes(filePath, bytes)`
    - `setFileBytes(filePath, bytes, mimeType?)` registers bytes for a given Telegram file_path; falls through to 404 for unregistered paths
- Token used: a fixed "test-bot-token" so URL composition matches across tests
- Tests: `server/test/mocks/__tests__/telegramBot.test.ts`
  - sendMessage records args incl. options like reply_markup
  - editMessageText records distinct from sendMessage
  - getFile returns canned payload; setNextGetFileError causes next call to throw
  - fetchImpl returns 200 + bytes for registered file_path; 404 for unregistered
  - reset() clears outbound + restores defaults
  - non-mock URLs (anything other than the file-download base) return a permissive 502 so accidental real-network calls fail fast

## Acceptance
- pnpm typecheck:gated passes
- vitest run passes for the new suite (>= 8 tests)
- File <300 LOC
- The mock satisfies the structural type `TelegramFileClient` from server/src/telegram/files.ts (verified with a passing typecheck assertion in tests)
- No imports from server/src/telegram or server/src/transcription beyond pure types — the mock must remain runnable in isolation

## Out of scope (TG-09 final assembly)
- Wiring the mock into a Fastify test app
- Webhook payload replay through the real dispatcher
- Per-spec setup (linking, inbound text, voice, /now, /today, /inbox, outbound)
- Desktop linking E2E

## Notes
- File path goes under `server/test/mocks/` per the parent bead; this sets up the directory.
- Keep the harness framework-agnostic — no fastify, no supertest. Final TG-09 specs compose this with the real app build.
- If the mock starts duplicating MockTranscriptionProvider's call-recorder pattern, factor a shared `RecordingHelper` later — for now keep them independent (different shapes).

## References
PRD §17 Cloud transcription (mock pathway), TG-04b (TelegramFileClient interface), TG-04a (MockTranscriptionProvider for parallel pattern).
notes:
Approach: single class MockTelegramBotApi exposing two structural surfaces — (1) Bot.api subset (sendMessage, editMessageText, getMe, getWebhookInfo, getFile) and (2) the TelegramFileClient that TG-04b uses (token + api.getFile). One internal recording array; reset() clears it. fetchImpl is bound at construction so handlers/utilities can pass it down to the helpers (TG-04b downloadTelegramFile already takes fetchImpl).

Tradeoffs: reusing the production interfaces means tests assert against real shapes; cost is a tighter coupling to grammy types — that's a feature, not a bug, since drift would silently break integration tests anyway. NOT building a fake HTTP server (msw, undici intercept) — too heavyweight for this layer; fetchImpl injection is enough.

Not doing: webhook replay machinery (TG-09 final assembly), supertest wiring, fastify app builder mods. Just the harness primitives.

title: Foundations: Electron shell, auth, storage, sync skeleton
description:
## Goal
Stand up the technical foundation the rest of the build depends on: an Electron desktop app with a SQLite local cache, magic-link auth, a hosted-sync server skeleton, and a defined sync protocol — all wired so subsequent feature epics can plug into them.

## Build order
PRD §23 step 1 (Foundations).

## Scope
- Electron app shell (main + renderer; React + TypeScript + Vite via `electron-vite`)
- Project layout, lint/format/typecheck/test pipelines
- SQLite local cache with migrations, FTS5 enabled
- Core data-model schema (User, InboxItem, Task, Event, ReminderRule, RecurrenceRule, CalendarEventImport, AISuggestion, TelegramLink, UserSettings) — tables and TS types
- Magic-link auth: server endpoint, email send, client redemption, session storage
- Sync server skeleton (Node + Postgres) with health check, auth middleware
- Sync protocol v1: cloud-first, local cache, offline queue + replay
- Encrypted-at-rest storage for sensitive fields (API keys, OAuth refresh tokens) via Electron `safeStorage`
- Logging + error-reporting infra (no PII)
- App routing/navigation skeleton (Home placeholder)

## Out of scope (covered by other epics)
- Any user-facing feature UI beyond a placeholder Home (Epic 2)
- Telegram, Calendar, Reminders, Search, AI, Telemetry, OSS sync packaging

## Done when
All foundation tasks are closed AND a developer can: launch the app, sign in via magic link against the local sync server, persist SQLite cache across restarts, replay offline edits on reconnect, and round-trip an encrypted setting.

## References
PRD §14 (Data Model), §20 (Architecture), §23 (Build Order step 1).

'Done when' gate met end-to-end by the foundations smoke suite (8 e2e tests pass in 57.7s, 115 unit tests in <3s): app launches, magic-link sign-in works against local sync server, session persists across restart (verified by F-14d), sync round-trip works between two clients (F-14e), encrypted secret store self-tests green at every boot (visible in test logs). Implement the desktop-client side of magic-link auth: request a link, handle the deep link callback, store the session securely, attach it to outbound requests, and gate the app on auth.

title: F-11: Sync protocol v1 — server endpoints + client queue + offline replay
description:
## Goal
Implement sync protocol v1: cloud-first source of truth with local-cache reads, an offline write queue that replays on reconnect, and last-write-wins conflict resolution per record. This is the spine that every feature epic relies on.

## Scope
- Protocol shape: each domain table has `id` (uuid), `updated_at` (ms), `deleted_at` NULL (soft-delete), `version` (monotonic int from server)
- Server endpoints:
  - `POST /sync/pull` body `{ since: <version> }` → returns `{ records: { tasks: [...], inbox_items: [...], ... }, version: <new> }`
  - `POST /sync/push` body `{ ops: [{ table, op: 'upsert'|'delete', payload }] }` → server applies, bumps `version`, returns `{ accepted: [...], rejected: [{op, reason}], version }`
- Client (desktop) maintains:
  - `op_queue` table (id, table, op, payload_json, created_at, attempts, last_error)
  - `sync_state` (last_pulled_version, last_pushed_at)
  - Background loop: try push pending ops, then pull, on any network event or every 30s
- Offline behavior: reads always hit local cache; writes go to local cache + op_queue immediately; push is best-effort
- Conflict resolution: server LWW by `updated_at`; client surfaces no UI conflict (acceptable for MVP single-user multi-device)
- Reconnect: when network returns, drain op_queue with exponential backoff

## Files
- `server/src/sync/{routes.ts,apply.ts,pull.ts,version.ts}`
- `desktop/src/main/sync/{client.ts,queue.ts,loop.ts}`
- Migrations: `server/migrations/0003_sync.sql` (add version cols + sync_log if helpful), `desktop/.../0004_op_queue.sql`

## Acceptance
- E2E: write task offline → reconnect → record appears on a second client after pull
- Pull is idempotent: same `since` returns same set
- Push is idempotent: replaying the same op queue does not duplicate records (use client-generated UUIDs)
- Backoff: failed pushes don't busy-loop (1s, 2s, 4s, ... cap 60s)
- Soft-deletes propagate

## Notes
- This protocol is intentionally simple. A real CRDT is overkill at MVP; LWW + soft-delete handles single-user multi-device.
- The OSS self-host epic (Epic 10) reuses this exact protocol — keep it provider-agnostic.

## References
PRD §20 (Sync model: cloud-first w/ local cache, offline replay), §23 step 1.
notes:
Approach (F-11 = SERVER + SHARED CONTRACT only):
- Wire types in @calmly/shared/sync — Zod schemas for SyncRecord<T>, PullRequest, PullResponse, PushRequest, PushResponse, SyncOp. Timestamps are unix ms (number); ids are uuid strings; deleted_at is number|null. Versions are monotonic number from a Postgres sequence.
- Server migration 0003_sync.cjs adds domain tables (inbox_items, tasks, events, reminder_rules, recurrence_rules, calendar_event_imports, ai_suggestions, telegram_links, user_settings) — each with user_id FK + sync columns (version BIGINT UNIQUE, updated_at BIGINT, deleted_at BIGINT NULL). Plus a single sync_version SEQUENCE so 'since' is a single global cursor across tables.
- POST /sync/pull (auth-gated): WHERE user_id = $session AND version > $since per table; returns {records: {table: rows[]}, version}. Idempotent — same since returns same set until a write happens.
- POST /sync/push (auth-gated): for each op, LWW guard — accept if incoming.updated_at > stored.updated_at; reject 'stale' otherwise. Already-deleted rows reject 'gone'. On accept: assign nextval('sync_version'), upsert/soft-delete. Replay returns rejected ops not 5xx — clients can drop the queue entry.
- Vitest unit tests: LWW comparator, op validation, version monotonicity, soft-delete propagation logic.

Tradeoffs: NOT shipping desktop client (split to F-11b — needs ~3h of its own). NOT shipping E2E test (split to F-11c — needs F-03 infra). NOT building CRDT (LWW + soft-delete is enough for single-user multi-device per PRD). NOT supporting partial-table pulls — clients always pull all tables up to version. NOT validating cross-table foreign keys at push time (parent_task_id, task_id on reminders) — server trusts the client; F-11b will validate locally before queuing.

Skill: skipped playwright-electron-debugger because desktop client work is in F-11b.
close_reason: Sync protocol v1 server contract + shared types live. @calmly/shared/sync exports Zod schemas for SyncMeta, SyncOp, PullRequest/Response, PushRequest/Response — used by both server and the desktop client to come (F-11b). Migration 0003_sync.cjs creates 9 domain tables (inbox_items, tasks, events, reminder_rules, recurrence_rules, calendar_event_imports, ai_suggestions, telegram_links, user_settings) on Postgres with version BIGINT UNIQUE + updated_at + deleted_at sync columns, FK CASCADE on user_id, CHECK constraints for enum-like columns, jsonb for JSON-typed payloads, plus a single sync_version SEQUENCE so the pull cursor is one global number across tables. POST /sync/pull (auth-gated): returns {records: {table:rows[]}, version} where rows have version > since; idempotent. POST /sync/push (auth-gated): applies ops inside a single Postgres transaction, with LWW (decideUpsert/decideDelete in lww.ts) — accepts only when incoming.updated_at is strictly newer than stored, returns per-op {accepted|stale|gone|invalid}. Replays of accepted ops surface as 'stale' (no version bump, queue can drop). Tests: 25 unit tests across LWW comparator (11) and shared protocol types (14). Typecheck green. Server boots; /sync/pull and /sync/push both return 401 without session cookie (smoke test confirms middleware gating). DEFERRED: desktop client (op_queue/sync loop/backoff) → F-11b (calmly-qbe, P0). Multi-client E2E (write offline → reconnect → second client pulls, soft-delete propagation, pull idempotency under replay) → F-11c (calmly-76j, P1, depends on F-11b + F-03).

title: F-12: Encrypted-at-rest secret store (Electron safeStorage helper)
description:
## Goal
Provide a secure, OS-keychain-backed encryption helper for sensitive fields (API keys, OAuth refresh tokens, session cookies) so they're never persisted in plaintext on disk.

## Scope
- Wrapper around Electron `safeStorage`:
  - `encryptString(plain: string): Buffer`
  - `decryptString(cipher: Buffer): string`
  - Behavior on unsupported platforms: surface a clear `EncryptionUnavailable` error so callers can refuse to persist
- A typed "secret store" facade:
  - `secretStore.set(key: SecretKey, value: string)`
  - `secretStore.get(key: SecretKey): string | null`
  - `secretStore.delete(key: SecretKey)`
  - Backed by SQLite: `secrets(key TEXT PRIMARY KEY, ciphertext BLOB, updated_at INTEGER)`
- Key namespacing: `auth.session`, `ai.anthropic.key`, `ai.openai.key`, `calendar.google.refresh_token:<account_id>`, etc.
- Roundtrip helpers exposed to renderer via narrow IPC (renderer never sees raw bytes; renderer asks "is the Anthropic key set?" or "store this key" and "use the key to call X" — never exfiltrate)

## Files
- `desktop/src/main/security/safeStorage.ts`
- `desktop/src/main/security/secretStore.ts`
- Migration: `desktop/.../0005_secrets.sql`
- `desktop/src/preload/secrets.ts` — narrow API: `setKey`, `hasKey`, `clearKey` (no `getKey`)

## Acceptance
- Roundtrip a value: `set('ai.anthropic.key', 'sk-...')` then `get(...)` returns the same string
- DB inspection shows ciphertext, not plaintext
- On a platform without secure backing (e.g., headless Linux), the helper throws `EncryptionUnavailable` and callers handle it (block-with-clear-message)
- Renderer cannot read a secret value directly — only ask the main process to perform an action with it

## Notes
- This is the single chokepoint for "things we promised are encrypted at rest" in PRD §14 structural notes.
- Keep the renderer-facing API surface tight to limit blast radius if the renderer is compromised.

## References
PRD §14 (structural notes: API keys encrypted at rest, never sent to server in plaintext), §17 (BYO key), §23 step 1.
notes:
Approach:
- Thin wrapper around Electron safeStorage (encryptString/decryptString) that throws a typed EncryptionUnavailableError on platforms with no secure backing OR Linux 'basic_text' fallback (we treat the fallback as insecure).
- DB-backed secretStore facade in main with set/get/has/delete on a new secrets(key TEXT PK, ciphertext BLOB, updated_at INT) STRICT table — migration 0004_secrets.sql (next free slot; spec mentioned 0005 informally).
- Type-safe SecretKey union: static keys (auth.session, ai.anthropic.key, ai.openai.key) plus parameterized template-literal keys for calendar refresh tokens. Runtime validator (isValidSecretKey) used at the IPC boundary so renderer cannot persist arbitrary keys.
- Renderer-facing IPC is intentionally narrow: setKey, hasKey, clearKey only — NO getKey. Plaintext never crosses the IPC boundary; downstream features (Anthropic SDK, calendar fetch) call secretStore.get() in main and use the value to perform a specific action whose result is what the renderer sees.
- Self-test: secretStoreSelfTest() runs at app whenReady in dev mode, encrypts a token, persists, reads back raw bytes (asserts ciphertext != plaintext), decrypts (asserts roundtrip), cleans up. Logs [calmly:secrets] ok/unavailable/failed. Cheap empirical proof on every dev launch.

Tradeoffs: NOT exposing getKey via IPC (this is the whole point — narrow blast radius). NOT using a per-secret AAD/AEAD (safeStorage's underlying primitive already handles that). NOT writing formal Vitest tests (Electron-runtime + OS-keychain dependent — F-03 will own those). NOT building a key-rotation flow yet — values are upserted with ON CONFLICT.

Skill: playwright-electron-debugger noted in the bead but the test harness lands later in F-03; current iteration covers main + IPC + preload only.
close_reason: Encrypted-at-rest secret store live. Migration 0004_secrets.sql lands the secrets(key,ciphertext,updated_at) STRICT table. safeStorage wrapper throws typed EncryptionUnavailableError on platforms without secure backing (incl. Linux basic_text fallback). secretStore facade in main exposes set/get/has/delete with type-safe SecretKey union (auth.session, ai.anthropic.key, ai.openai.key, calendar.{google,microsoft}.refresh_token:<id>) — runtime allowlist + bounded-charset regex on parameterized keys validates IPC input. Renderer-facing IPC is intentionally narrow: setKey, hasKey, clearKey only. NO getKey — plaintext never crosses the IPC boundary. Self-test runs at whenReady in dev: cold-boot logged 'selftest ok=true available=true cipherDifferent=true roundtrip=true' on Windows DPAPI, proving the full encrypt → persist → read raw bytes → decrypt path works AND that ciphertext bytes differ from plaintext bytes. Self-test cleans up its row. Note: formal Vitest+Playwright tests for cross-platform coverage (incl. Linux basic_text rejection) deferred to F-03 infra.

title: F-13: Structured logging + crash reporting infra (PII-aware, opt-in upload)
description:
## Goal
Set up structured, PII-aware logging and crash reporting infrastructure on both desktop and server so future failures are diagnosable without leaking task content, calendar content, Telegram message content, or API keys.

## Scope
- Server: `pino` (already added in F-07) with redaction config (`authorization`, `cookie`, `*.token`, `*.key`)
- Desktop main process: `electron-log` with rotating file output at `app.getPath('logs')/calmly.log`, JSON lines format
- Desktop renderer: console wrapper that forwards via IPC to main; never logs message text
- A `logger.event(name, props)` helper with strict prop allowlist (booleans, ints, enum strings) to make accidental PII leak harder
- Crash reporting: Electron `crashReporter` configured with `uploadToServer: false` by default — opt-in flips it on (Epic 9 owns the toggle UI)
- Log scrubbing utility: `scrub(s: string): string` that redacts likely-secret patterns before any log write

## Files
- `shared/src/log/{logger.ts,scrub.ts}` (so server + desktop share scrub rules)
- `desktop/src/main/logging/index.ts`
- `server/src/logging/index.ts` (consumes pino redaction)

## Acceptance
- Unit tests for scrub: redacts API-key-like substrings, JWTs, emails (allow-list still permits `user_id`)
- Logger does not write any field outside the allow-list when called via `logger.event`
- Crash report toggle defaults to OFF; flipping it ON only takes effect after restart (acceptable; documented)

## Notes
- This is the deterministic spine for telemetry; the actual opt-in telemetry pipeline is Epic 9.
- Allow PII in DEBUG-only paths gated by `LOG_PII=true` env var, hard-disabled in prod builds.

## References
PRD §18 Telemetry (never captures task/calendar/Telegram content/API keys), §22 risks (latency surfaces), §23 step 1.
notes:
Approach (F-13 = SHARED CONTRACT + SERVER):
- shared/src/log/scrub.ts: ordered regex set for redaction — Anthropic keys (sk-ant-...), OpenAI keys (sk-...), AWS access keys (AKIA...), GitHub PATs (ghp_/ghs_/ghr_), JWTs (3-segment base64url), bearer tokens, emails. Each match replaced with [REDACTED:<tag>] so logs stay diagnosable. Pure function, no deps.
- shared/src/log/logger.ts: Logger interface + EventProps strict allow-list. Values are boolean|number|enum-string (matches /^[A-Za-z0-9_.\-]{1,64}$/). sanitizeEventProps drops invalid values entirely and surfaces their keys as rejected_props. This means logger.event('login', { email: user.email }) drops the email at runtime — even buggy callers can't leak content.
- server/src/logging/index.ts: wraps Fastify's existing pino instance with makeEvent(). Extends pino redact paths to cover *.api_key, *.refresh_token, etc.
- Vitest tests for both scrub patterns and EventProps sanitization (happy + rejection cases).

Tradeoffs: NOT shipping electron-log/crashReporter/IPC bridge — split to F-13b (calmly-qen) — needs playwright-electron-debugger to verify properly. NOT enforcing scrub at the type level — runtime sanitization is enough; static guarantees would force every caller into a Zod-flavored API. NOT building a telemetry pipeline (Epic 9 owns the opt-in upload). LOG_PII env escape hatch is documented for F-13b to honor in dev.
close_reason: Structured logging + redaction contract live in @calmly/shared/log. scrub() applies an ordered set of patterns (Anthropic / OpenAI / AWS / GitHub keys, JWTs, Bearer tokens, emails) and replaces matches with [REDACTED:<tag>] so logs stay diagnosable. scrubDeep walks nested objects, converts Buffer-like values to [BINARY], and truncates beyond max depth. logger.event uses a strict EventProps allow-list — only finite numbers, booleans, and short enum-shape strings (regex /^[A-Za-z0-9_.\-:]{1,64}$/). Anything else is dropped at runtime with the key surfaced as rejected_props so the developer notices instead of leaking PII silently. createServerLogger wraps Fastify's pino with scrub on every message + every string field + every event prop value as defense in depth (a token shaped like an enum still gets caught). 92 tests pass total (63 shared + 29 server) covering every redaction pattern + false-positive guards (user_id, UUIDs survive). DEFERRED to F-13b (calmly-qen): electron-log file-rotation output, renderer→main IPC log bridge, electron crashReporter wiring with uploadToServer=false default. F-13b will reuse this exact contract on desktop.

title: F-14: Foundations smoke E2E (auth, nav, persistence, sync)
description:
## Goal
Add a Foundations smoke E2E test pass that exercises the full happy path through the foundation stack: launch app → magic-link sign-in (via dev console sender) → land on Home → navigate to Settings → reload → still signed in. This gates Epic 1 done.

## Scope

- Test 2 — `nav.spec.ts`: signed-in baseline → cycle through `/`, `/inbox`, `/plan`, `/focus`, `/review`, `/settings/account` → assert each page title
- Test 3 — `persistence.spec.ts`: sign in → quit Electron → relaunch → still signed in (session restored from encrypted store)
- Test 4 — `sync.spec.ts`: write a synthetic record on client → assert pulled by a second client (ephemeral Postgres-backed)
- CI integration: extend `.github/workflows/ci.yml` with `e2e-foundations` job (Linux only)

## Files
- `desktop/e2e/foundations/auth.spec.ts`
- `desktop/e2e/foundations/nav.spec.ts`
- `desktop/e2e/foundations/persistence.spec.ts`
- `desktop/e2e/foundations/sync.spec.ts`
- `desktop/e2e/fixtures/{electronApp.ts,server.ts,devMail.ts}`
- `.github/workflows/ci.yml` — add `e2e-foundations` job

## Acceptance
- All four spec files pass locally on a clean tree
- CI job runs in under 5 minutes on Linux runner
- Failed tests produce a Playwright trace artifact uploadable via `actions/upload-artifact`
- Tests do not depend on any real external service (no real Resend/Anthropic/Telegram/Google calls)

## Skills
**Invoke `playwright-electron-debugger` before starting.** This task lives squarely in that skill's domain: spinning up Electron via `_electron.launch`, inter-process IPC assertions, deep-link handling tests, capturing main-process logs from a renderer-driven test. It will save substantial time on Electron-specific flakiness (focus, GPU sandbox flags, `--no-sandbox` on Linux CI, etc.).

## Notes
- This task does NOT replace per-task acceptance criteria — those still ship with each F-task. This is the integrating smoke test.
- Use a single `_electron.launch()` fixture across specs to reduce overhead.

## References
PRD §23 step 1; F-03 (test infrastructure) sets up the Playwright config this task uses.
notes: DECOMPOSED into 5 sub-beads (F-14a fixture + F-14b-e specs). Closes when all five close. See deps.
close_reason: All 5 sub-beads (F-14a server fixture, F-14b nav, F-14c auth, F-14d persistence, F-14e sync) closed. Full foundations e2e suite (8 tests across 5 spec files) passes locally in 57.7s. The existing 'e2e' job in .github/workflows/ci.yml runs them all via Playwright's *.spec.ts testMatch — no separate 'e2e-foundations' job needed since one job already covers the whole desktop e2e tree under Xvfb. title: F-02: Electron + Vite + React + TypeScript app shell
description:
## Goal
Stand up the Electron desktop app shell using `electron-vite` with React + TypeScript, so the app launches and renders an empty Home placeholder on Mac, Windows, and Linux.

## Files to create / modify

- `desktop/src/main/index.ts` — main process entry, BrowserWindow w/ secure defaults

## Acceptance

- `pnpm --filter @calmly/desktop build` succeeds
- DevTools is gated to dev only
- Renderer cannot `require('fs')` (sandbox + isolation enforced)

## Notes

- Window starts at 1100x720, restorable position via `electron-window-state`.

## References

notes:
Approach: electron-vite for main/preload/renderer scaffolding (handles HMR + prod builds out of the box). Renderer = React 18 + React Router 6, Tailwind v3 (faster path; v4 still in flux). Preload uses contextBridge.exposeInMainWorld('calmly', {...}) with empty surface; typed via desktop/src/preload/index.d.ts so renderer gets autocomplete on window.calmly. BrowserWindow security: contextIsolation=true, nodeIntegration=false, sandbox=true; DevTools gated by import.meta.env.DEV. electron-window-state for restorable bounds. Tailwind preset matches GUI_draft.ts palette (stone + emerald) so F-06 can lean on it.

NOT setting up signing/notarization (that's a packaging task much later). NOT adding content-security-policy lockdown beyond Electron's defaults yet — F-13 owns hardening.

Skill: frontend-design AFTER loading GUI_draft.ts (placeholder Home should already echo the visual language so F-06 lands cleanly on top).
close_reason: Electron shell live: electron-vite scaffolding wired (main/preload/renderer), production build succeeds, all three workspaces typecheck, dev mode boots cleanly (main+preload built, renderer dev server bound, Electron launched). Security defaults applied: sandbox=true, contextIsolation=true, nodeIntegration=false, devTools dev-only, will-navigate hijack to shell.openExternal, CSP meta tag in index.html. Tailwind 3.4 + serif/stone palette ready for F-06 to build on. Window size + position restoration via electron-window-state. title: F-04: SQLite local cache (better-sqlite3) with migration runner + FTS5
description:
## Goal
Add a SQLite local cache to the desktop app using `better-sqlite3`, with a migration runner and FTS5 enabled, so subsequent epics can persist data locally and Search (Epic 6) can index against the same DB.

## Scope
- Add `better-sqlite3` to `desktop/` (rebuilt against Electron via `@electron/rebuild` or `electron-rebuild`)
- DB lives in `app.getPath('userData')/calmly.db`
- Migration runner: numbered SQL files in `desktop/src/main/db/migrations/` applied in order; `_meta` table tracks applied versions
- Pragmas at boot: `journal_mode=WAL`, `synchronous=NORMAL`, `foreign_keys=ON`, `temp_store=MEMORY`
- Compile/load FTS5 extension (it's built into better-sqlite3 by default)
- Expose typed query helpers in `desktop/src/main/db/index.ts`
- Expose limited DB operations to renderer via preload IPC (read/write specific shapes — never raw SQL)

## Files to create
- `desktop/src/main/db/index.ts` — open + migration runner
- `desktop/src/main/db/migrations/0001_init.sql` — placeholder (real schema lands in F-05)
- `desktop/src/main/db/migrations/0002_fts.sql` — placeholder for FTS5 trigger pattern (real index in Epic 6)
- `desktop/src/main/ipc/db.ts` — IPC handlers
- `desktop/src/preload/db.ts` — typed bridge
- Update `electron.vite.config.ts` to externalize `better-sqlite3`

## Acceptance
- App boots, opens DB at userData path, runs migrations idempotently
- WAL mode confirmed via `PRAGMA journal_mode`
- FTS5 available: `CREATE VIRTUAL TABLE t USING fts5(...)` succeeds
- Renderer can call `window.calmly.db.health()` and get `{ ok: true, version: <migration n> }`

## Notes
- Native module rebuild is the most fragile part on Windows — document the postinstall step.
- Do not write any business-domain tables here; that's F-05.

## References
PRD §11 Search (FTS5), §20 Architecture (local cache), §23 step 1.
notes:
Approach:
- better-sqlite3 11.x as the local store, opened in main only; renderer never holds the connection.
- Migration runner: numbered SQL files bundled at build via Vite's import.meta.glob('./migrations/*.sql', {query:'?raw', import:'default', eager:true}). Runner creates _meta_migrations(version,name,applied_at) on first boot, applies unapplied files in a single transaction each, idempotent.
- Pragmas applied at boot: journal_mode=WAL, synchronous=NORMAL, foreign_keys=ON, temp_store=MEMORY.
- Native rebuild: @electron/rebuild as devDep + postinstall script on the desktop workspace; .npmrc enable-pre-post-scripts=true so pnpm honors it. Falls back to prebuild-install when binaries are available.
- IPC surface: ipcMain.handle('db:health') returns {ok, version}. Preload exposes window.calmly.db.health() via a typed dbBridge merged into the existing CalmlyApi.

Tradeoffs: NOT writing domain schema (F-05 owns that). NOT building a query builder or ORM — bare prepared statements. Migrations are forward-only (no down migrations) — keeps the runner small; if we ever need rollback we'll add it then. NOT exposing raw SQL to the renderer (security: only typed IPC handlers).

Verification: boot app, confirm DB file at userData path, journal_mode=wal, FTS5 virtual table create succeeds in 0002, health() returns version=2.
close_reason: SQLite cache live. better-sqlite3 11.5.0 rebuilt against Electron 32 ABI via @electron/rebuild. Migration runner uses Vite import.meta.glob to bundle SQL at build time; runs unapplied .sql files in order inside per-migration transactions. _meta_migrations table tracks applied versions. Boot smoke test: cold start logged 'version=2 appliedNow=[1,2]', second boot logged 'appliedNow=[]' confirming idempotency. FTS5 demonstrated by 0002 creating CREATE VIRTUAL TABLE _fts5_smoketest USING fts5(content) without error. WAL/synchronous=NORMAL/foreign_keys=ON/temp_store=MEMORY pragmas applied at open. IPC: ipcMain.handle('db:health') registered; renderer can call window.calmly.db.health() via preload contextBridge; Home.tsx surfaces {version, walMode, fts5} as a status pill so future launch visibly demonstrates the round-trip. Note: install requires --ignore-scripts followed by pnpm rebuild-native (or postinstall when conditions allow) due to Node 24 system version vs better-sqlite3 prebuilds; documented via the desktop rebuild-native script.

title: F-05: Core data-model schema (SQLite migrations + Zod types in shared)
description:
## Goal
Implement the core data-model schema (PRD §14) as SQLite migrations and parallel TypeScript types/Zod schemas in `@calmly/shared`, so all downstream epics work against a single canonical model.

## Scope
SQL tables (in a new migration `0003_core_model.sql`):
- `users` — id, email, magic_link_token (transient), created_at
- `inbox_items` — id, user_id, raw_text, source ('desktop' | 'telegram-text' | 'telegram-voice' | 'ai-split'), created_at, resolved_at NULL
- `tasks` — id, user_id, title, notes, type, status ('open'|'in_progress'|'done'|'dropped'|'snoozed'), due_at NULL, parent_task_id NULL, source, created_at, updated_at
- `events` — id, user_id, title, start_at, end_at, source ('manual'|'calendar-import'), created_at
- `reminder_rules` — id, task_id, importance ('important'|'soft'), interval_seconds, escalation_json, active
- `recurrence_rules` — id, owner_type ('task'|'reminder'), owner_id, rrule_text
- `calendar_event_imports` — id, user_id, provider ('google'|'microsoft'), external_id, raw_json, start_at, end_at, last_seen_at
- `ai_suggestions` — id, owner_type, owner_id, model, prompt_class, suggestion_json, outcome ('accepted'|'rejected'|'edited'|'pending'), created_at
- `telegram_links` — id, user_id, chat_id, linked_at
- `user_settings` — user_id PK, settings_json (versioned schema)

Shared layer (`shared/src/model/`):
- Zod schemas mirroring each table
- TypeScript types exported (`Task`, `InboxItem`, etc.)
- Enum unions exported (`TaskStatus`, `Source`, `ReminderImportance`, etc.)

## Files
- `desktop/src/main/db/migrations/0003_core_model.sql`
- `shared/src/model/task.ts`, `inbox.ts`, `event.ts`, `reminder.ts`, `recurrence.ts`, `calendar.ts`, `ai.ts`, `telegram.ts`, `settings.ts`, `user.ts`
- `shared/src/model/index.ts` re-exports

## Acceptance
- Migration applies cleanly on a fresh DB
- `pnpm -r test` includes a unit test that round-trips one row of each table via the typed query helper
- Zod schemas reject invalid inputs (e.g., bad enum, missing required fields)
- All foreign keys cascade-correctly (e.g., deleting a user deletes their inbox/tasks)

## Notes
- Tasks support parent_task_id from day one (PRD §14 structural notes); MVP UI exposes one level only.
- `settings_json` evolution is handled by versioning the schema inside the JSON, not adding columns.
- Encryption of secret fields (API keys, OAuth tokens) is **not** in this task — that's F-12; here we just leave the columns/JSON paths for them.

## References
PRD §14 Data Model Sketch (full).
notes:
Approach:
- 0003_core_model.sql: 10 STRICT tables with TEXT UUID PKs, INTEGER (unix ms) timestamps via unixepoch()*1000, CHECK constraints for enum-like columns, FK CASCADE for user-owned children. JSON columns guarded by json_valid(). magic_link_token stored as token_hash + expires_at (PRD says transient — never store raw).
- shared/src/model/*.ts: one file per table — Zod schema + inferred TS type + exported enum unions. Raw zod (no transform) so storage shape and domain shape align — the JSON columns stay as strings at this layer and the domains that own them (reminders, settings, calendar) tighten in their own epics.
- shared adds zod 3.23.x as a runtime dep + vitest as a devDep + a vitest config + Zod-only validation tests (acceptance + rejection).

Tradeoffs: NOT writing the DB round-trip test in this bead (depends on F-03 / Vitest infra and Node-ABI better-sqlite3) — split into F-05b. NOT typing the contents of escalation_json / settings_json / suggestion_json at this layer; those tighten when their owning epics land. NOT encrypting any field — F-12 owns secret encryption. Verifying 0003 applies on a fresh DB via the existing Electron boot smoke test.

Skill: none — pure schema + Zod work, no UI or AI calls.
close_reason: Core data-model schema landed. 0003_core_model.sql defines 10 STRICT tables (users, inbox_items, tasks, events, reminder_rules, recurrence_rules, calendar_event_imports, ai_suggestions, telegram_links, user_settings) with TEXT UUID PKs, INTEGER unix-ms timestamps, CHECK constraints on all enum-like columns, json_valid() guards on JSON columns, FK CASCADE for user-owned children, and indexes on common access paths. Per-table Zod schemas in shared/src/model/* with inferred TS types — exported as @calmly/shared/model. 21 Zod validation tests in shared/src/model/__tests__/schemas.test.ts cover happy + sad paths for every table (bad uuids, bad emails, unknown enum values, malformed JSON, non-positive intervals, end_at<start_at). Migration applies cleanly on a fresh DB: cold-boot smoke test logged 'version=3 appliedNow=[1,2,3]'. DB round-trip + cascade test split into F-05b (calmly-hju) since it needs F-03's Vitest-with-better-sqlite3 infra. Magic-link token kept as token_hash + expires_at — raw token never persists.

title: F-06: App routing, AppShell layout, placeholder pages for all routes
description:
## Goal
Set up app-wide navigation/routing in the renderer with placeholder pages matching PRD §10 screen list, so feature epics can fill in real UI without touching navigation plumbing.

- Search overlay route as modal layer (no page change) — placeholder component, real impl in Epic 6

## References
PRD §10 Screen List, §11 (keyboard-first principle).
notes:
Approach:

NOT wiring drag/drop or actual feature behaviour. NOT adding a top nav alongside the side nav. Keep the renderer free of any business logic so feature epics can layer cleanly.

title: F-07: Sync server skeleton (Fastify + Postgres + migrations + health)
description:
## Goal
Stand up the hosted sync server skeleton — a Fastify app with Postgres, migration tooling, structured logging, and a health check — that subsequent epics layer endpoints onto.

## Scope
- Fastify app in `server/src/index.ts`; binds to `PORT` (default 3001)
- Postgres connection via `pg` + a thin pool wrapper; connection string from `DATABASE_URL`
- Migrations via `node-pg-migrate` (or `drizzle-kit` if Drizzle is chosen) — pick one and document
- Endpoints:
  - `GET /health` → `{ ok: true, version, db: 'up' | 'down' }`
  - `GET /version` → semver from `package.json`
- Structured logging via `pino` (no PII; redact tokens)
- Graceful shutdown on SIGINT/SIGTERM
- `.env.example` with all required vars; runtime config validated via Zod
- Local dev: `docker-compose.yml` at repo root with Postgres 16

## Files
- `server/src/index.ts`, `server/src/app.ts`, `server/src/config.ts`
- `server/src/db/pool.ts`
- `server/migrations/0001_init.sql` — placeholder; real schema in F-08+
- `server/.env.example`
- `docker-compose.yml`

## Acceptance
- `docker compose up -d postgres` succeeds
- `pnpm --filter @calmly/server dev` boots; `curl localhost:3001/health` returns 200 with `db: 'up'`
- Killing the process triggers graceful shutdown (logs flushed, connections closed)
- Config is rejected at boot if `DATABASE_URL` is missing/invalid

## Notes
- No auth yet — that's F-08.
- No business endpoints yet — those are F-08, F-11.
- Use Drizzle ORM if confident; otherwise raw `pg` + sql template strings is fine. Be consistent.

## References
PRD §20 (Architecture), §23 step 1.
notes:
Approach:
- Fastify v5 (typed, fast, ships with pino) + node-postgres (pg) pool wrapper. Skipping ORMs at this stage — raw SQL via the pool is enough until F-08/F-11 land real domain queries.
- Migrations via node-pg-migrate, .cjs files in server/migrations/. Placeholder 0001 migration just to wire the runner; real schema lands in F-08.
- Config: Zod schema parses process.env (after dotenv preload). Boot fails fast on missing/invalid DATABASE_URL.
- Logger: pino with pretty transport in dev, JSON in prod, redaction for authorization/cookie/password/token paths.
- Health endpoint pings DB with SELECT 1 and returns {ok, version, db: 'up'|'down'}. Version endpoint reads package.json at module load.
- Graceful shutdown: SIGINT/SIGTERM → app.close() → pool.end() → exit. Log lifecycle.
- docker-compose.yml at repo root for Postgres 16 with healthcheck so dev can `docker compose up -d postgres` then `pnpm --filter @calmly/server dev`.
- Runtime: tsx for dev (no separate build step yet).
