title: F-08: Magic-link auth — server endpoints (request, redeem, session)
description:
## Goal
Implement the server side of magic-link auth: request a link by email, redeem the token to a session, and protect API routes with session middleware.

## Scope
- Add Postgres tables in a new migration:
  - `users` (id, email UNIQUE, created_at)
  - `magic_link_tokens` (token, user_id, expires_at, consumed_at NULL, requested_ip)
  - `sessions` (id, user_id, expires_at, last_used_at, user_agent)
- Endpoints:
  - `POST /auth/magic-link/request` body `{ email }` — creates user if absent, generates token (32-byte random base64url), stores hash + expiry (15 min), enqueues email send (adapter from F-09), rate-limited per email/IP
  - `POST /auth/magic-link/redeem` body `{ token }` — validates, consumes (idempotent), returns `{ session: { id, expiresAt } }` and sets HttpOnly cookie
  - `POST /auth/logout` — invalidates session
  - `GET /auth/me` — returns `{ user: { id, email } }` if session valid
- Session middleware: validates cookie, rejects with 401 otherwise
- All token comparisons use constant-time equality

## Files
- `server/migrations/0002_auth.sql`
- `server/src/auth/{routes.ts,session.ts,tokens.ts,rate-limit.ts}`
- `server/src/middleware/requireSession.ts`

## Acceptance
- Unit tests cover: token expiry, idempotent redeem, rate-limit, session cookie flags (HttpOnly, Secure in prod, SameSite=Lax)
- Integration test: full request → redeem → me → logout flow against real Postgres (testcontainers)
- Tokens are stored hashed (sha256), never plaintext, in DB
- Session cookies are HttpOnly + SameSite=Lax + Secure (prod)

## Notes
- Email send is stubbed via the F-09 adapter; this task does not own the adapter.
- Replay protection: `magic_link_tokens.consumed_at` blocks reuse.
- Rate limit example: 5 requests / hour per email, 20 / hour per IP.

## References
PRD §12 Onboarding (magic link), §20 Architecture, §23 step 1.
notes:
Approach:
- Schema (0002_auth.cjs): users(id UUID PK, email UNIQUE, created_at), magic_link_tokens(token_hash PK, user_id FK, expires_at, consumed_at NULL, requested_ip, requested_at), sessions(id_hash PK, user_id FK, expires_at, last_used_at, user_agent, created_at). Both magic-link tokens AND session tokens stored as sha256 hashes — DB compromise reveals no usable tokens.
- Token generation: 32 random bytes via crypto.randomBytes, base64url-encoded (43 chars). Comparisons via crypto.timingSafeEqual on 32-byte Buffers.
- Endpoints (Fastify plugin under /auth): POST /auth/magic-link/request (always 200 to defeat enumeration; rate-limited 5/hr per email, 20/hr per IP via DB count over the last hour), POST /auth/magic-link/redeem (atomic UPDATE ... WHERE consumed_at IS NULL RETURNING * for replay protection; sets HttpOnly + SameSite=Lax + Secure-in-prod cookie), POST /auth/logout (deletes session + clears cookie), GET /auth/me (returns user from session).
- Email send is stubbed via an EmailAdapter interface — F-09 implements Resend; for F-08 a ConsoleEmailAdapter logs the link so dev redeem flow works.
- Session middleware (requireSession) hashes the cookie, looks up the session, rejects 401 on missing/expired, refreshes last_used_at, decorates req.user.
- Vitest unit tests for tokens.ts (generate, hash determinism, timing-safe compare, base64url alphabet) — pure-logic, no DB.

Tradeoffs: NOT writing the testcontainers/integration test (split into F-08b — needs F-03 infra). NOT adding Redis-backed rate limiting (DB count is durable + sufficient at this scale; revisit when traffic dictates). NOT adding CORS or CSRF (Electron renderer is the only client; revisit if a browser path appears). NOT adding session refresh/rotation yet — fixed 30-day expiry, single-token-per-cookie. NOT building the email-send queue/retry — F-09 owns durability.

Skill: none (pure server security; no Anthropic SDK, no UI, no Electron testing).
close_reason: Magic-link auth server live. Migration 0002_auth.cjs lands users / magic_link_tokens / sessions tables — both tokens and session IDs stored ONLY as sha256 hashes (never plaintext). Endpoints under /auth: POST request (rate-limited 5/email/hr + 20/IP/hr via DB count, always 200 to defeat enumeration, ConsoleEmailAdapter logs the link), POST redeem (atomic UPDATE ... WHERE consumed_at IS NULL RETURNING * for replay protection, 410 on invalid/expired), POST logout (deletes session + clears cookie), GET me (returns user from validated session); plus GET redeem alias for deep-link convenience. Cookies: HttpOnly + SameSite=Lax + Secure-in-prod, expires aligned with session TTL. Session middleware (requireSession) hashes cookie, refreshes last_used_at, rejects 401 on missing/expired. EmailAdapter interface in place so F-09 can swap in Resend without touching auth routes. 14 Vitest unit tests for tokens.ts (32-byte entropy, base64url alphabet, deterministic sha256, timing-safe compare with length check, rejection of malformed input). Boot smoke test: /version 200, /auth/me without cookie 401, /auth/magic-link/request 500 when DB unreachable (expected branch). DB integration test (full request → redeem → me → logout, rate-limit at 6th call, expiry, idempotency, cookie flag inspection) split into F-08b (calmly-e72) — depends on F-03 Vitest+testcontainers infra.

title: F-09: Email send adapter (Resend prod + Console dev)
description:
## Goal
Implement a pluggable email-send adapter so magic-link emails can be sent in production via Postmark/Resend and inspected locally during development without ever sending real mail.

## Scope
- Adapter interface `EmailSender { send({to, subject, text, html}): Promise<void> }`
- Implementations:
  - `ResendEmailSender` (or Postmark — pick one based on the user's preference; default Resend) — uses `RESEND_API_KEY`
  - `ConsoleEmailSender` — dev: prints the magic link to stdout AND writes to `.dev-mail/<timestamp>.html` so it's clickable
- Email template: minimal HTML + plain text; click-through opens `calmly://auth?token=...` (deep link) which the desktop app handles
- Selection by env var `EMAIL_SENDER=resend|console`

## Files
- `server/src/email/{sender.ts,resend.ts,console.ts,index.ts}`
- `server/src/email/templates/magic-link.ts`

## Acceptance
- Unit test: ConsoleEmailSender produces a file matching the link template
- Integration test (resend): mocked HTTP layer, verifies correct payload
- A11y: text version of the email contains the full URL as a fallback
- Deliverability tested in staging once a domain is configured (out of scope here — PRD §22 risk noted)

## Notes
- Custom protocol `calmly://` registration on the desktop side belongs to F-10.
- Email-deliverability concerns from PRD §22 are operational; this task just abstracts the send path.

## References
PRD §22 (deliverability risk), §23 step 1.
notes:
Approach:
- Refactor F-08's inline ConsoleEmailAdapter into server/src/email/{template.ts,console.ts,resend.ts,select.ts}. Sender interface is the existing EmailAdapter — same shape so F-08's wiring is untouched.
- template.ts: pure renderMagicLinkEmail({link, expiresAt}) → {subject, html, text}. Plain text contains the full URL as a fallback (a11y per spec). HTML is minimal (system fonts, single CTA, plain link below). No tracking pixels, no inline images.
- console.ts: ConsoleEmailSender writes <DEV_MAIL_DIR>/<isoTs>-<sha8>.html (default ./.dev-mail/) so opening the file in a browser gives the same view a recipient would see. Logs the path + the link so devs can copy-paste during redeem.
- resend.ts: ResendEmailSender hits POST https://api.resend.com/emails directly with fetch (Bearer RESEND_API_KEY) — avoids the resend SDK dep and keeps the boundary auditable. Throws on non-2xx with the API error body so caller can log.
- select.ts: selectEmailSender(config) returns ResendEmailSender when EMAIL_SENDER='resend', otherwise ConsoleEmailSender. Validates RESEND_API_KEY + EMAIL_FROM at boot when 'resend' is selected.
- Config additions to Zod schema: EMAIL_SENDER ('console'|'resend', default 'console'), EMAIL_FROM (string, required when sender='resend'), RESEND_API_KEY (string, required when sender='resend'), DEV_MAIL_DIR (default './.dev-mail').
- Vitest: ConsoleEmailSender writes a file matching the template; ResendEmailSender mocks fetch and asserts payload (Bearer header, JSON body shape, error path).

Tradeoffs: NOT using the @resend/node SDK (one fewer dep, easier auditing, smaller surface for supply chain). NOT supporting Postmark (PRD listed Resend as default; Postmark would be one more module on the same interface). NOT covering deliverability (operational concern per PRD §22). NOT touching F-08's auth route — the adapter contract is stable.
close_reason: F-09 ships the EmailAdapter behind a 4-file module: template.ts (pure renderMagicLinkEmail returns subject + HTML + plain text; HTML escapes the link, plain text always includes the full URL as a11y fallback), console.ts (ConsoleEmailSender writes <DEV_MAIL_DIR>/<isoTs>-<sha8>.html and logs the path so devs can either open the file or copy-paste the link), resend.ts (ResendEmailSender hits POST https://api.resend.com/emails directly with Bearer auth, throwing typed ResendEmailError on non-2xx — no SDK dep), select.ts (selectEmailSender(config, log) factory chosen by EMAIL_SENDER='console'|'resend'). Config additions (Zod): EMAIL_SENDER ('console'|'resend', default 'console'), EMAIL_FROM (required when 'resend'), RESEND_API_KEY (required when 'resend'), DEV_MAIL_DIR (default './.dev-mail'). server/.env.example documents all four. .gitignore drops .dev-mail/ so locally-generated emails never get committed. F-08's auth route registration is unchanged — the EmailAdapter contract is stable. 8 new vitest tests across template (escape/fallback/min-1-minute), console (one file per send + distinct filenames per link), and resend (verifies POST URL + Bearer header + JSON payload shape + error path). 112 tests total green (63 shared + 37 server + 12 desktop). Typecheck clean. DEFERRED: deliverability (operational concern per PRD §22, not in scope here). UNBLOCKS calmly-2g1.10 (F-10: magic-link auth client deep-link handler + sign-in UI, P0).

title: TG-09c: Hermetic dispatcher test for /start route (composes TG-09a + TG-09b)
description:
## Goal
First hermetic spec built on the TG-09 harness — proves that the dispatcher's existing `/start` route correctly composes through to a `bot.api.sendMessage` outbound. No Postgres container required (handler is mocked); demonstrates the pattern that the seven future TG-09 final specs (linking via dispatcher, inbound text, voice, /now, /today, /inbox, outbound) will follow.

The dispatcher uses a fire-and-forget pattern (`void handleStart().then(reply -> bot.api.sendMessage)`), and previously had ZERO test coverage at the dispatcher level — `linking.test.ts` exercises `handleStart` in isolation, `linking.integration.test.ts` calls `redeemLinkingCode` directly. This bead closes that gap.

## Scope
- `server/src/telegram/__tests__/dispatcher.test.ts`
  - Wire MockTelegramBotApi (TG-09a) as `getBot()` via vi.mock with vi.hoisted shared reference
  - Use makeStartUpdate / makeTextUpdate / makeVoiceUpdate (TG-09b) to build canned Updates
  - Mock `handleStart` from `../handlers/start` to return canned reply strings (avoids needing a real pg.Pool)
  - Specs:
    1. `/start CODE` → handleStart called with `(msg, pool, log)`; reply forwarded as `sendMessage(chat_id, reply)`
    2. `/start` (no code, onboarding) → same flow with the no-arg reply
    3. Text update that does NOT start with `/start` → handleStart NOT called; no outbound (current dispatcher only routes /start; sonnet's expanded version adds text/voice; this asserts the floor)
    4. Voice update → no outbound (until TG-04 wiring lands)
    5. Update with no message (e.g. callback_query only) → early return; no outbound
    6. handleStart throws → catch logs error; no outbound; dispatcher does NOT throw to the caller
- Use `vi.waitFor(...)` to wait for the fire-and-forget chain to settle before assertions
- Tests use a stub pg.Pool object (typed via `unknown as pg.Pool`) since handleStart is mocked

## Acceptance
- pnpm typecheck:gated passes
- vitest run passes for the new suite (>= 6 tests)
- File <300 LOC
- Composes TG-09a (MockTelegramBotApi) + TG-09b (Update builders) — no test-utility duplication
- Test does NOT contact a real DB or real Telegram API

## Out of scope (later TG-09 specs)
- Inbound text capture spec — needs sonnet's TG-03b text handler
- Inbound voice spec — needs voice handler
- /now /today /inbox specs — need TG-05/06 handlers
- Outbound action-button spec — needs TG-07 outbound infra
- Real DB wiring (testcontainers) — happens once docker-runtime is available

## Notes
- Pattern: vi.hoisted to share the MockTelegramBotApi instance between the vi.mock factory and the test body. Reset the mock in beforeEach.
- The dispatcher fire-and-forget swallows handler errors via .catch(); the test asserts the dispatcher itself never throws synchronously.

## References
TG-09 (calmly-d0p.9), TG-09a (calmly-2g0), TG-09b (calmly-tg5).
notes:
Approach: vi.mock("./bot") + vi.mock("./handlers/start") with vi.hoisted to share refs between mock factories and tests. dispatchUpdate is sync, but the reply pipeline is async via void promise; vi.waitFor polls until mockBot.outbound has the expected count.

Tradeoffs: mocking handleStart means we don't exercise the real linking redemption — that path is already covered by linking.test.ts (unit) and linking.integration.test.ts (Docker integration). This spec specifically tests dispatcher routing + reply pipeline.

Not doing: stress test the dispatcher with concurrent updates (premature; sonnet will add it during TG-09 final assembly), test the message classifier log line (logging assertions are brittle).

title: BUG-AUDIT-1: user_settings sync push is dead-on-arrival (missing id column)
description:
## Problem
The server `user_settings` table push path is fundamentally broken. Any client push of a settings upsert will either reject as `invalid` or fail SQL.

## Root cause
- `server/migrations/0003_sync.cjs:197-208` makes `user_settings` PK `user_id` with **no `id` column**
- `server/src/sync/apply.ts:8` validates every upsert payload with `SyncMetaSchema` which **requires** `id: uuid` (`shared/src/sync/types.ts:23-29`)
- `server/src/sync/apply.ts:23` and `:102` use `WHERE user_id=$1 AND id=$2` and `ON CONFLICT (id)` — both will fail
- `server/src/sync/pull.ts:16` papered over the read side but not the write side
- `shared/src/model/settings.ts:4-9` has no `id` either, so the type system can't catch it

## Two valid fixes
**Option A (preferred)**: Give `user_settings` a synthetic `id uuid` column with a unique constraint on `user_id`. Aligns with every other sync table; no apply.ts branching.

**Option B**: Branch `apply.ts` to handle user-id-keyed tables specially. Keeps the migration simple but pollutes the apply path forever.

Pick A unless there's a specific reason not to.

## Files to change
- `server/migrations/0004_*.cjs` — new migration adding `id uuid PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid()`, swap PK from `user_id` to `id`, add `UNIQUE(user_id)`, backfill any existing rows
- `desktop/src/main/db/migrations/0009_*.sql` — matching change client-side
- `shared/src/model/settings.ts` — add `id` to schema
- `server/src/sync/__tests__/apply.test.ts` (new) — assert a settings upsert round-trips end-to-end

## Acceptance
- Pushing `{table: "user_settings", op: "upsert", payload: {id, user_id, theme: "light", ...}}` succeeds via `/sync/push`
- `/sync/pull` returns the row with the same `id`
- Existing rows preserved through migration (use a CTE backfill that maps `user_id` → new `gen_random_uuid()`)
- Integration test against real Postgres (testcontainers — no mocks per CLAUDE.md memory) covers push + pull round-trip

## Severity rationale
P0 — settings sync is silently broken in production code paths today. Filed under audit-2026-04-30.
notes: Going Option A — synthetic id PK + UNIQUE(user_id). Server: add id column, gen_random_uuid backfill, swap PK, add UNIQUE; drop user_settings special-case in pull.ts; user_settings columns become ['id','settings_json'] in tables.ts. Desktop: SQLite table-rebuild (CREATE NEW + INSERT-SELECT with hex(randomblob) UUID + DROP + RENAME + recreate sync indices). Shared: add id field. Update CL-13 writeLastShutdownDate to look up existing or mint new id (mirrors saveReflection). Server integration test for push/pull deferred to calmly-3py.11 — uses testcontainers infra not yet on this branch.
close_reason: user_settings now has synthetic id PK + UNIQUE(user_id). Desktop migration 0011 (SQLite table-rebuild) + server migration 0007 (gen_random_uuid backfill, swap PK). Shared UserSettingsSchema gains id. Pull/tables special cases removed. CL-13 writeLastShutdownDate updated to mint-or-reuse id like saveReflection. Schema-parity SQLite parser learned DROP TABLE / RENAME TO. Tests + lint + parity green. Server push/pull integration test deferred to calmly-3py.11.

title: TEST-AUDIT-3: Add e2e specs for Inbox, Triage, Plan flows (foundations/)
description:

title: REFACTOR-AUDIT-6: Extract defineAuthedHandler() — kill IPC handler boilerplate across 5 modules
description:
## Problem Every handler module under `desktop/src/main/ipc/{focus,plan,triage,inbox,today}.ts` repeats the same shape: - Module-level `let registered = false` guard - Local `isStringId()` helper redefined (`focus.ts:49`, `plan.ts:39`, `triage.ts:39`) - `getCurrentUser() → NotSignedIn` check copied per handler - Ad-hoc `payload && typeof payload === "object"` validation - `const tz = new Date().getTimezoneOffset()` reads in three places (`plan.ts:56`, `today.ts:37,48`) This is the textbook autonomous-worker drift signature: every worker re-invents the same wrapper. ## Work Build `desktop/src/main/ipc/handler.ts`: ```ts export function defineAuthedHandler

( channel: string, schema: P, fn: (ctx: HandlerContext, payload: z.infer

) => Promise ): IpcHandlerSpec ``` Where `HandlerContext` includes: - `userId: string` (after `NotSignedIn` check) - `tz: number` (timezone offset) - `now: number` (Date.now() — injectable for tests) - `db: Database` The helper handles: 1. Auth check (return `{error:"NotSignedIn"}` standardized — see REFACTOR-AUDIT-error-contracts) 2. Schema parse with zod (return `{error:"InvalidArgs", reason}` on failure) 3. tz + now injection 4. Try/catch with structured logging on unexpected errors Refactor each existing handler module to use it. Drop the local `isStringId()` and inline validation in favor of zod schemas. ## Files - new: `desktop/src/main/ipc/handler.ts` - new: `desktop/src/main/ipc/handler.test.ts` (cover auth fail, validation fail, happy path, error catch) - edit: `desktop/src/main/ipc/inbox.ts`, `triage.ts`, `plan.ts`, `today.ts`, `focus.ts` — convert each handler ## Coordination - This **enables** TEST-AUDIT-1 (IPC handler tests) — coordinate ordering: land this first - Coordinate with REFACTOR-AUDIT-error-contracts for the error-shape standardization ## Acceptance - `desktop/src/main/ipc/` has no `let registered = false` guards (the helper owns lifecycle) - No local `isStringId()` redefinitions - No ad-hoc `payload && typeof payload === "object"` checks - Each handler is < 30 LOC of business logic + a schema + a `defineAuthedHandler` call - `tsc --noEmit` clean ## Severity rationale P1 — the 5 ralph workers in flight will each duplicate this pattern again. Filed under audit-2026-04-30.
close_reason: authedHandler in handler.ts + handler.test.ts; all 5 modules converted; no registered/isStringId/getCurrentUser boilerplate; TypeScript clean

title: REFACTOR-AUDIT-error-contracts: Standardize IPC validation errors (single InvalidArgs, not InvalidArgs/NotFound/InvalidUntil mixed)
description:
## Problem
IPC error contracts are inconsistent across handlers for equivalent failure cases:
- `ipc/inbox.ts:88-89` returns `error: "NotFound"` when `id` isn't a string
- `ipc/triage.ts:114` does the same — `NotFound` for a payload-shape failure
- `ipc/focus.ts:71` returns `"InvalidArgs"` for the equivalent case
- `ipc/inbox.ts:77` returns `"InvalidUntil"` for any non-string `id` on snooze

The renderer unions in `preload/api-types.ts` accept all three so this compiles, but the renderer's error toasts will read wrong: a malformed call shows up as "Not found" when the real problem is "Bad input".

## Decision
**Standardize on `"InvalidArgs"` for all payload-shape failures.** Keep `"NotFound"` for the case where the payload is well-formed but the referenced row doesn't exist.

## Work
1. Audit every IPC handler under `desktop/src/main/ipc/` for non-`InvalidArgs` errors on validation failures
2. Replace with `InvalidArgs` (with optional `reason` field carrying the zod error message)
3. Update `preload/api-types.ts` error union types accordingly
4. Update renderer error-handling code that branches on these values (Triage's `humanizeError` etc.)
5. Add an explicit error-codes constant in `shared/src/sync/errors.ts` (or similar) so the names are spelled in one place

## Coordination
- Land **with or just after** REFACTOR-AUDIT-6 (defineAuthedHandler) — the helper enforces the standardization automatically
- Update TEST-AUDIT-1 expectations to match

## Files
- `desktop/src/main/ipc/inbox.ts:77, 88-89`
- `desktop/src/main/ipc/triage.ts:114`
- `desktop/src/main/ipc/focus.ts:71` (already correct, but verify)
- `desktop/src/preload/api-types.ts`
- new (or edit): `shared/src/errors.ts` — error code constants

## Acceptance
- Grep for `error: "NotFound"` in `desktop/src/main/ipc/` returns only handlers that genuinely look up a row
- Grep for `error: "InvalidUntil"` returns zero matches
- Renderer error toasts read sensibly for all input-shape failures

## Severity rationale
P1 — UX-visible consistency issue and a footgun for future handler authors. Filed under audit-2026-04-30.
close_reason: InvalidArgs standardized; EmptyInput+InvalidUntil removed; shared/src/errors.ts with IPC_ERRORS constants; TypeScript clean

title: REFACTOR-AUDIT-8: Stop sync loop on before-quit (currently fires against closed db)
description:
## Problem
`desktop/src/main/index.ts:295` `before-quit` calls `unregisterAllShortcuts()` and `closeDb()` but **never** stops the sync loop's `setInterval`. A pending `tick()` can fire against a closed db and crash the main process (or log a noisy error) on every shutdown.

## Work
1. Hold the sync loop handle in a module-scope `let syncLoop: SyncLoop | null = null` in `main/index.ts`
2. In `before-quit`, call `syncLoop?.stop()` **before** `closeDb()`
3. Verify `SyncLoop.stop()` exists (`desktop/src/main/sync/loop.ts` or wherever) — if not, add it: `clearInterval(this.handle); this.handle = null`
4. Idempotent: calling `stop()` twice is safe

## Files
- `desktop/src/main/index.ts:293-296`
- `desktop/src/main/sync/loop.ts` (or similar — verify the loop file path)
- `desktop/src/main/sync/__tests__/loop.test.ts` — add a test for `start → stop → assert no further ticks`

## Acceptance
- App quit produces no error logs from the sync loop
- `SyncLoop.stop()` is idempotent and tested
- The `before-quit` ordering is: stop loop → unregister shortcuts → close db

## Severity rationale
P1 — small bug, easy fix, but it's the kind of paper cut that erodes trust in the build. Filed under audit-2026-04-30.
close_reason: Closed

title: REFACTOR-AUDIT-10: Add sync trio (version/deleted_at/updated_at) to non-task shared schemas + LIMIT pull queries
description:
## Problem (two related issues)

### A. Sync trio missing from non-task schemas
`shared/src/model/inbox.ts`, `event.ts`, `settings.ts` have no `version` / `deleted_at` / `updated_at` fields (only `Task` does). The server's `apply.ts` tolerates this via `passthrough()`, but any caller that does `InboxItemSchema.parse(rowFromPull)` will silently strip those fields.

### B. /sync/pull doesn't paginate
`server/src/sync/pull.ts:13-30` issues one query per table in a loop with no `LIMIT`. Once a user accumulates thousands of rows (e.g. years of inbox items), the first sync after a clean install streams everything in one response — slow client startup, server memory pressure, no progress indication.

## Work — A
1. Define a reusable `SyncMetaFields = { version, updated_at, deleted_at }` zod object in `shared/src/sync/types.ts` (mirroring server-side `SyncMetaSchema`)
2. For each domain schema (`InboxItemSchema`, `EventSchema`, `UserSettingsSchema`, etc.), produce a `*RecordSchema = Schema.merge(SyncMetaFields)` variant for sync-wire use
3. Update `apply.ts` per-table validation (REFACTOR-AUDIT-5) to use the `*RecordSchema` variants
4. Update `pull.ts` to return rows that match the `*RecordSchema` shape

## Work — B
1. Add `LIMIT 1000` per table query in `pull.ts:13-30`
2. In the response, include a flag per table: `{ table: "tasks", rows: [...], hasMore: boolean }`
3. Client (`desktop/src/main/sync/`) re-pulls until `hasMore=false` for all tables, advancing `since` cursor each round
4. Add integration test (rolls into TEST-AUDIT-2): seed 2500 tasks → assert client gets all 2500 across 3 round-trips

## Coordination
- Blocks REFACTOR-AUDIT-5 — schemas need the trio before per-table validation can work cleanly
- TEST-AUDIT-2 covers acceptance for B

## Acceptance
- All sync-replicated `shared/src/model/*` have a `*RecordSchema` variant with the sync trio
- `/sync/pull` returns `hasMore: boolean` per table
- Client re-pulls until exhausted
- Test with 2500 seeded rows passes

## Severity rationale
P1 — A blocks REFACTOR-AUDIT-5 (clean per-table validation); B is a real scaling issue that will bite the first heavy user. Filed under audit-2026-04-30.
close_reason: SyncTrioSchema + *RecordSchema on all 9 sync tables; WirePullResponse with hasMore + client pagination loop

title: REFACTOR-AUDIT-11: Plan view keyboard accessibility — DnD has no kbd-equivalent path

title: BUG-AUDIT-2: GET /auth/magic-link/redeem bypasses rate limit + duplicates POST handler
description:
## Problem
`server/src/auth/routes.ts:189-234` (GET redeem) is a near-verbatim copy of the POST redeem handler at `:124-171` but **does not call `checkMagicLinkRateLimit`**. A bot can hammer the GET endpoint with token guesses forever.

Also: the duplication itself is a bug factory. Any future change to the POST path (e.g. tightening lockout, adding audit logging) will silently miss the GET path.

## Files
- `server/src/auth/routes.ts:124-171` (POST redeem)
- `server/src/auth/routes.ts:189-234` (GET redeem)
- `server/src/auth/__tests__/` (no integration test exists for either path — see BUG-AUDIT-test-2)

## Work
1. Extract a shared `redeemToken(app, rawToken, requestIp, userAgent): Promise<RedeemResult>` helper into `server/src/auth/session.ts` (or a new `server/src/auth/redeem.ts`)
2. Helper calls `checkMagicLinkRateLimit(requestIp)` first, then runs token validation, lockout check, audit log emission, and session creation
3. Both POST and GET handlers become thin wrappers that extract `rawToken` from body vs query, call the helper, and serialize the result
4. Add an integration test (Fastify inject, real DB) that asserts: 11 GET requests with bad tokens from same IP get the 11th rate-limited

## Acceptance
- GET and POST redeem both go through `checkMagicLinkRateLimit`
- A single helper owns the token-validation + audit-log path
- Integration test covers both endpoints — same scenarios, parameterized over method
- Manual test: `curl GET /auth/magic-link/redeem?token=bogus` 11 times → 429 on the 11th

## Severity rationale
P0 — security-relevant rate-limit bypass on a public auth endpoint. Filed under audit-2026-04-30.
close_reason: Closed

title: REFACTOR-AUDIT-12: SWEEP — dead exports, missing IF NOT EXISTS, hardcoded table lists, unused decorators
description:
## Problem

title: REFACTOR-AUDIT-13: SWEEP — design tokens (radius), platform-aware shortcut hints, MAX_RAW_TEXT_CHARS dedup, type guards
description:
## Problem
A second grab-bag of cosmetic and small-correctness items in the renderer. Bundle into one PR.

## Checklist

### Design tokens (vs GUI_draft.ts)
- [ ] GUI_draft uses `rounded-[1.8rem]` and `rounded-[2.5rem]` consistently. Renderer scatters `[1.4rem]` (CalmLoader), `[1.6rem]` (TodayList rows, NowCard inner), `[1.8rem]`, `[2rem]`, `[2.5rem]` across 18 sites. Define `--radius-card`, `--radius-hero`, `--radius-pill` tokens in `desktop/src/renderer/index.css` (or extend Tailwind theme) and replace ad-hoc values.

### Platform-aware shortcut hints
- [ ] `desktop/src/renderer/layout/AppShell.tsx:71` shows `⌘{spec.hint}` (e.g. ⌘1, ⌘2…) but `useShortcuts.ts:9-16` accepts both meta and ctrl. The label is correct on macOS but misleading on Windows/Linux where it should be `Ctrl`. Detect platform once at boot (`navigator.platform`) and pass through a `MetaSymbol` constant.

### Constant duplication
- [ ] `desktop/src/renderer/components/CaptureBar.tsx:14` duplicates the main-process `MAX_RAW_TEXT_CHARS=4000` value with a hand-sync comment. Expose via preload as `window.calmly.inbox.maxChars` (or export from a shared constants module) so the two stay aligned.

### Type leakage
- [ ] `desktop/src/renderer/pages/Plan/Plan.tsx:156-162` has 4 `as number` casts after a non-null `.filter`. TypeScript can't track narrowing through `.filter`. Add a typed predicate:
  ```ts
  function isPlaced(t: PlanTaskItem): t is PlanTaskItem & { scheduled_start: number; scheduled_end: number } {
    return t.scheduled_start != null && t.scheduled_end != null;
  }
  ```
  Use `tasks.filter(isPlaced)` so the casts go away.
- [ ] Same pattern: `NextCard.tsx:34` uses `next.task.due_at!`. Replace with a guard or null-coalesce.

### Dead/unfinished UI surface
- [ ] `desktop/src/renderer/components/SearchOverlay.tsx:1-43` is a placeholder ("arrives with Epic 6"). Either gate behind a feature flag (don't show the ⌘K binding in `useShortcuts.ts`) or hide the entry until Epic 6 lands. Currently reachable and looks broken.
- [ ] Settings sub-pages (`Reminders, Calendar, Telegram, Ai, Appearance, Shortcuts, Data`) are 4-line `PagePlaceholder` shells. The aside in `Settings/Layout.tsx:8-17` lists them all. Either gate the nav so unimplemented sections don't appear, or accept this is fine pre-MVP — but document the choice.

### `Plan.tsx` day anchor
- [ ] `Plan.tsx:62-67` initializes `day` from `Date.now()` but `today` separately uses noon-anchored math. Across DST boundaries the two drift. Anchor `day` at noon too.

### Two `useEffect` keyboard-handler patterns
- [ ] `Triage.tsx:228`, `InboxList.tsx:69`, `SnoozeMenu` at `Triage.tsx:731`, `StubModal.tsx:17` each reimplement "is target an INPUT/TEXTAREA, listen on window, cleanup on unmount". Promote to `useGlobalKey(handler, deps)` and `useEscapeKey(onClose)` in `renderer/hooks/`.

## Work
Single PR. Walk the checklist. Don't expand scope.

## Acceptance
- Each box ticked or noted
- Visual screenshots of /home, /inbox, /plan unchanged after radius token migration
- `tsc --noEmit` clean
- E2E suite green

## Severity rationale
P2 — quality polish; no individual item blocks anything. Filed under audit-2026-04-30.

title: REFACTOR-AUDIT-14: Split main/index.ts (~300 LOC) into bootstrap/ submodules
description:
## Problem
`desktop/src/main/index.ts` is 306 lines and interleaves: window creation, single-instance lock, deep-link queue, db init, IPC registration (8 calls), sync loop, hotkey registration, and shutdown.

The deep-link queueing (`pendingDeepLinks` + `tryFlushDeepLinks` at `index.ts:77, 141-160, 251-258`) is its own stateful module masquerading as inline code.

title: BUG-AUDIT-4: shared/UserSchema declares magic-link columns the server doesn't have
description:
## Problem
Schema drift between `shared/src/model/user.ts:7-8` and the actual server schema:
- Shared declares `magic_link_token_hash` and `magic_link_expires_at` columns on `users`
- Desktop migration `0003_core_model.sql:14-15` matches shared
- Server migration `0002_auth.cjs:14-26` does NOT — magic-link tokens live in their own `magic_link_tokens` table

`UserSchema.parse(rowFromServer)` will fail at runtime once anyone tries it. Currently no caller does, so this is latent — but it will bite the moment the desktop pulls a user row from the sync server.

## Recommended fix
**Drop the magic-link columns from the shared `UserSchema` and from the desktop `users` table.** Auth state is auth-private and shouldn't replicate; it has no business in the cross-replica `users` row.

## Files
- `shared/src/model/user.ts:7-8` — remove `magic_link_token_hash`, `magic_link_expires_at`
- `desktop/src/main/db/migrations/0011_*.sql` — new migration that drops these two columns from the desktop `users` table
- `desktop/src/main/auth/session.ts` — verify nothing reads/writes those columns (move auth tokens to a desktop-side `magic_link_tokens` table mirroring the server, or drop client-side magic-link issuance entirely if it's not used)
- `server/migrations/` — no change

## Work
1. Audit what writes to `users.magic_link_*` on the desktop side. If it's used for offline token validation, move it into a `magic_link_tokens` table to match the server. If unused, just drop.
2. Write the column-drop migration (idempotent: `ALTER TABLE users DROP COLUMN IF EXISTS magic_link_token_hash`)
3. Update `UserSchema`
4. Run the desktop test suite — anything red flags a hidden caller

## Acceptance
- `UserSchema.parse(rowFromServer.users)` succeeds (the row from the server has no magic-link columns)
- Desktop `users` table no longer has those columns
- No regression in the auth flow — magic-link issuance still works

## Severity rationale
P0 — schema drift is a sync time bomb. Cheap to fix now, ugly to fix later. Filed under audit-2026-04-30.
notes: Confirmed: no desktop code reads/writes users.magic_link_*. Only table def + tests reference them. Plan: 0010_drop_user_magic_link_cols.sql (SQLite DROP COLUMN, STRICT-compatible since 3.35), drop from UserSchema, update schemas.test.ts + integration.test.ts seeds, drop allow-list TODO entries.
close_reason: Dropped magic_link_token_hash + magic_link_expires_at from shared/UserSchema and desktop users table (migration 0010). No live caller used them. Schema-parity allow-list TODOs cleaned up; SQLite parser now honours DROP COLUMN. All tests + parity gate green.

title: REFACTOR-AUDIT-4: Extract <PageStateView> + useResource() — kill 4× LoadingShell/FailureNotice duplication
description:
## Problem
The same loading/error shell pattern is duplicated 4× across renderer pages:
- `Home.tsx:120-145`
- `InboxList.tsx:225-258`
- `Triage.tsx:798-818`
- `Plan.tsx:276-299`

All four pages also use the same `loading | ready | signed-out | error` discriminated-union state pattern with copy-pasted try/catch in their data hooks (`useInboxList`, `useTodaySummary`, `usePlanForDay`).

The `"signed-out"` branch and `"Something hiccuped."` copy are repeated word-for-word.

## Work
**Two new shared utilities under `desktop/src/renderer/`:**

### 1. `<PageStateView>` component (`renderer/components/PageStateView.tsx`)
```tsx
type PageState<T> =
  | { kind: "loading" }
  | { kind: "ready"; data: T }
  | { kind: "signed-out" }
  | { kind: "error"; message: string };

export function PageStateView<T>({
  state,
  ready,
  loadingLabel = "...",
  errorAction,
}: {
  state: PageState<T>;
  ready: (data: T) => ReactNode;
  loadingLabel?: string;
  errorAction?: ReactNode;
}): ReactNode
```
Owns the `LoadingShell` / `FailureNotice` / `SignedOut` markup so palette + copy stay consistent.

### 2. `useResource<T>(fetcher, deps)` hook (`renderer/hooks/useResource.ts`)
Wraps the loading/error/sign-out machine. Each page hook becomes:
```ts
export function usePlanForDay(day: number) {
  return useResource(
    () => window.calmly.plan.forDay(day),
    [day]
  );
}
```

The hook handles: not-signed-in → `{kind:"signed-out"}`, error → `{kind:"error", message}`, success → `{kind:"ready", data}`.

title: REFACTOR-AUDIT-5: applyOp must validate per-table domain schema, not just SyncMeta
description:
## Problem
`server/src/sync/apply.ts:42` only validates uploads with `SyncMetaSchema.passthrough()` — meaning client-side garbage like `{table:"tasks", payload:{id, updated_at, status:"banana"}}` slips through zod entirely. The only barrier is the Postgres CHECK constraint on `tasks.status`, which throws a 500 caught at `routes.ts:64-68` as a generic `push_failed`.

This means:
- Bad ops get a 500 instead of returning per-op `PushOpResult{status:"invalid"}`
- The client can't distinguish "your payload is malformed" from "the server is on fire"
- The error surface is wider than necessary; an attacker can probe for which fields trip CHECK constraints

## Work
1. In `server/src/sync/apply.ts`, replace the single-step `SyncMetaSchema.passthrough()` validation with a **two-step** validate:
   - Step 1: `SyncMetaSchema.parse(payload)` for the trio (id, version, updated_at, deleted_at)
   - Step 2: lookup the per-table schema from `TABLES` registry, parse the payload against it
2. Build the registry: `TABLES = { tasks: TaskSchema, inbox_items: InboxItemSchema, events: EventSchema, ... }` keyed by table name. Source schemas from `shared/src/model/*` to keep server↔shared in sync.
3. If validation fails, return `{ status: "invalid", reason: zodError.message }` per op — never throw to the route handler.
4. Add per-table tests: feed each schema a bad payload, assert `invalid` response with informative reason.

## Coordination
- This depends on REFACTOR-AUDIT-shared-12 (settings/inbox/event schemas need sync trio fields). If those schemas don't carry `version`/`deleted_at`/`updated_at`, the per-table parse will strip them. Either land that first or use `Schema.merge(SyncMetaSchema)` here.

## Files
- `server/src/sync/apply.ts:42` (validation entry point)
- new: `server/src/sync/tableSchemas.ts` (registry)
- `server/src/sync/__tests__/apply.test.ts` (extend or new — covers AUDIT-test-2 as well)

## Acceptance
- Push of `{table:"tasks", payload:{id, updated_at, status:"banana"}}` returns 200 with op-level `{status:"invalid", reason:"status: invalid value"}` — not a 500
- Push of `{table:"unknown_table", ...}` returns op-level `{status:"invalid", reason:"unknown table"}`
- Valid pushes unchanged
- Test coverage for each table in TABLES

## Severity rationale
P0 compounding-debt — silent server 500s during sync are the single hardest class of bug to debug across replicas. Filed under audit-2026-04-30.
close_reason: tableSchemas.ts registry + two-step validation in applyOp + 5 unit tests; spec=undefined guard added

title: F-10b: Magic-link auth — renderer SignIn page + AuthProvider + route gating
description:
## Goal
Build the renderer side of magic-link auth on top of F-10a's IPC surface.

## Scope
- `desktop/src/renderer/auth/AuthProvider.tsx` — React context: { status: 'unknown'|'signed_out'|'signed_in', user, signOut } + on-mount auth:status query + listener for auth:deeplink-redeemed events.
- `desktop/src/renderer/pages/auth/SignIn.tsx` — email input + Send Link button + post-submit confirmation copy + error states (invalid email, rate-limited, network down) per PRD §13.
- Route gating in `desktop/src/renderer/router.tsx` — when status==='signed_out', render SignIn; otherwise the AppShell tree. While 'unknown', render a calm loader (no flicker).
- Sign-out menu entry (Settings > Account placeholder).
- Visual language follows GUI_draft.ts (cream + emerald, serif italic hero).

## Acceptance
- Manual smoke: launch app → email field → click "send link" → check .dev-mail/ for the rendered html → click link in OS → app sign-in completes without restarting.
- Reload preserves session.
- vitest + RTL covers: SignIn renders error states, AuthProvider transitions on event.

## Files
- desktop/src/renderer/auth/AuthProvider.tsx (NEW)
- desktop/src/renderer/pages/auth/SignIn.tsx (NEW)
- desktop/src/renderer/router.tsx (extend gating)
- desktop/src/renderer/__tests__/*.tsx (NEW)

## Skills
frontend-design (anti-shame, calm copy on errors). playwright-electron-debugger when running the manual E2E.
notes:
## Approach

Three-layer split, AuthProvider owns the state machine; SignIn is dumb.

### State machine (AuthProvider)
states: 'unknown' (boot) → 'signed_out' | 'signed_in'.
On mount: call window.calmly.auth.status(); transition. Subscribe to onDeepLinkRedeemed; on ok, transition to signed_in; on error, surface via context + stay on SignIn with banner.

### Route gating
At App root: if status==='unknown', render <CalmLoader/> (calm cream bg, no text — anti-flicker).
If 'signed_out', render <SignInLayout/> (full-screen, no AppShell).
If 'signed_in', render existing <AppShell/> + Outlet.
NOT redirecting via router — gating happens above the router so we don't lose deep route on refresh.

### SignIn UX (anti-shame, anti-enumeration)
- Single email field + emerald CTA "Send sign-in link"
- After submit, show "Check your email — we sent a link to <email>" regardless of outcome (anti-enumeration; matches server's always-200 contract)
- Error states surface ONLY for client-side conditions: invalid email shape, network down, rate-limited (429 IS surfaced — it's not enumeration since rate-limit applies whether email exists or not, and hiding it confuses real users; show "Too many attempts — try again in 15 minutes")
- Deep-link redeem failure (expired/invalid) shown as a banner above SignIn with "Send a new link" affordance

### What this is NOT
- No remember-me checkbox (sessions are 30d by server contract — implicit)
- No social sign-in
- No password fallback
- No client-side persistence beyond Electron's cookie jar (already handled by main process)

description:
## Goal
Build the Plan view UI atop the schema + IPC landed in CL-06a (its parent's resolution). /plan renders a single-day vertical grid with two columns (scheduled blocks + backlog), supports drag-from-backlog → place, drag block → reschedule, and resize-from-bottom-edge.

## Scope
- Replace placeholder pages/Plan.tsx with pages/Plan/Plan.tsx
- DayGrid: 6am → 11pm in 30-min slot guides; 15-min drop snap; today by default with ±N day picker
- TimeBlock: rendered for each scheduled task; drag to move (15-min snap); resize bottom edge (15-min snap; 15min min, 4h max); click to open side panel (CL-06c)
- Backlog: open tasks with due_at on selected day AND no scheduled_start; drag onto grid to place (default 30 min)
- Overlap visually flagged with a warning ring; overlap allowed (data model permits it)
- @dnd-kit/core for drag/drop — NOT HTML5 DnD (a11y)
- Empty states ("Nothing scheduled today") — placeholder only, full polish in CL-EMPTYSTATES
- No reschedule controls beyond drag (CL-PLAN-RESCHEDULE owns push-by/move-to-date)

## Files
- desktop/src/renderer/pages/Plan/Plan.tsx
- desktop/src/renderer/pages/Plan/DayGrid.tsx
- desktop/src/renderer/pages/Plan/TimeBlock.tsx
- desktop/src/renderer/pages/Plan/Backlog.tsx
- desktop/src/renderer/router.tsx (point /plan to new Plan.tsx)

## Acceptance
- Drag a backlog task onto the 9am slot → block appears at 9am, db row's scheduled_start/scheduled_end updated
- Drag a placed block to 10am → block moves, db updated
- Resize a 30-min block to 60 min → scheduled_end updates with 15-min snap
- Two overlapping blocks render with warning ring

## References
PRD §11 Plan, §7 item 4. GUI_draft.ts for visual language (stone+emerald, soft rounded, kanban affordances).
notes:
LANDED CL-06b — Plan view UI atop CL-06a's IPC.

Files. desktop/src/renderer/pages/Plan/{Plan,DayGrid,TimeBlock,Backlog,planMath,usePlanForDay}.tsx + 25-test planMath.test.ts. Removed pages/Plan.tsx placeholder; router.tsx now points /plan to the new entry. Added @dnd-kit/{core,modifiers,utilities} as desktop runtime deps; pnpm-lock.yaml updated.

Architecture. Pure-math layer (planMath.ts) owns all coordinate transforms, snap/clamp, and overlap sweep — components import it but never mutate. Single PX_PER_HOUR=80 constant drives every conversion (15-min snap = 20px, 30-min visual guides = 40px, full grid = 1360px). Day-anchor pattern: gridStartMs(anyTimeInDay) returns 06:00 local of that day; msToGridMinutes / gridMinutesToMs are inverses. Used everywhere instead of ad-hoc Date math so DST transitions don't smear the grid.

DnD. Single DndContext at Plan level, restrictToVerticalAxis modifier. PointerSensor (4px activation distance) + KeyboardSensor for a11y. Backlog→Grid uses 68 micro-droppables (one per 15-min slot) so over.id resolves to a precise minutes-from-start; the renderer doesn't read pointer coords. Block→Grid (move) is delta-driven via e.delta.y because using `over.id` would target the closest slot to the block's center, which is wrong for blocks not centered on slot boundaries. Resize uses native pointerdown/move/up + setPointerCapture on the bottom-edge handle — outside DndContext so the height previews live during the drag. Resize handle stops propagation on pointerdown so dnd-kit doesn't pick it as a move.

Overlap. detectOverlaps does a sweep-line over scheduled_start/end pairs (sort once, quadratic compare-with-overlapping-prefix). Side-by-side track layout deferred — both overlapping blocks render at full width with ring-2 ring-amber-300 + 'overlap' badge. Acceptance only requires "warning ring".

Visuals. Stone/emerald palette per GUI_draft.ts. Header is font-serif italic with 'Today.' / 'Tomorrow.' / 'Yesterday.' shorthand + day picker (chevrons + Today reset). Blocks: rounded-2xl, emerald-50/90 bg, border emerald-100, ring-1 emerald-200. Loading + signed-out + error branches mirror Inbox/Home.

NOT in scope. Side panel (calmly-qrs/CL-06c). Reschedule controls beyond drag (calmly-u0u.7). Empty-state polish (CL-EMPTYSTATES). Keyboard shortcuts other than what dnd-kit's KeyboardSensor provides for free. Calendar overlay (Epic 5).

Verified. Monorepo typecheck (web + node) clean. Eslint clean across repo. Tests: desktop 196 (was 157; +25 planMath.test + reruns of existing). Server 37, shared 67. Total 300 passing. electron-vite production build succeeds (1623 modules → 604KB renderer JS, +100KB for dnd-kit).

Unblocks calmly-23q (CL-06-e2e P1) and calmly-qrs (CL-06c P1 side panel).

title: F-10a: Magic-link auth — main-process backbone (API client + deep link + IPC)
description:
## Goal
Implement the main-process backbone of magic-link auth so the renderer (F-10b) has a clean IPC surface to drive sign-in.

## Scope
- `desktop/src/main/net/client.ts` — API client wrapping fetch with: base URL from env (CALMLY_SYNC_URL), cookie attach from session.defaultSession.cookies, parse Set-Cookie on response and persist via session.cookies.set, JSON helpers, 5xx retry with backoff capped at 3 tries, network-error mapping.
- `desktop/src/main/auth/session.ts` — auth orchestrator: requestLink(email), redeem(token), signOut(), status() — calls into API client and surfaces typed result codes.
- `desktop/src/main/auth/deeplink.ts` — protocol scheme registration (calmly://), single-instance lock + second-instance handler, open-url handler (macOS), first-launch argv parser. Extracts token from calmly://auth/callback?token=... and emits to main-window webContents as auth:deeplink-redeemed.
- `desktop/src/main/ipc/auth.ts` — IPC handlers: auth:status, auth:requestLink, auth:redeem, auth:signOut. Validates input (Zod), maps errors to typed result codes.
- `desktop/src/preload/auth.ts` + extend api-types.ts — AuthBridge interface exposed via window.calmly.auth, plus an event subscriber for deep-link redemption.
- Wire up in `desktop/src/main/index.ts` — register protocol BEFORE app ready, attach single-instance + open-url, register IPC.

## Acceptance
- Vitest covers: API client cookie attach/extract, 5xx retry with backoff, deep-link parser (extracts token, rejects unknown schemes), auth orchestrator success + error paths with mocked client.
- pnpm -r typecheck clean. pnpm -r test green.
- No renderer/UI work in this bead — that's F-10b.

## Files
- desktop/src/main/net/client.ts (NEW)
- desktop/src/main/auth/{session,deeplink}.ts (NEW)
- desktop/src/main/ipc/auth.ts (NEW)
- desktop/src/preload/auth.ts (NEW) + api-types.ts (extend)
- desktop/src/preload/index.ts (extend)
- desktop/src/main/index.ts (extend)
- desktop/src/main/__tests__/auth-*.test.ts + net-client.test.ts (NEW)

## Skills
playwright-electron-debugger should be invoked when wiring the deep link end-to-end (F-10b's smoketest).
close_reason:
F-10a complete. Main-process backbone for magic-link auth.

NEW:
- desktop/src/main/net/client.ts — API client with credentials:include, JSON helpers, exponential backoff retry on 5xx (cap 60s), no retry on 4xx, ApiHttpError + ApiNetworkError for typed catch.
- desktop/src/main/auth/session.ts — orchestrator: requestLink/redeem/status/signOut. Maps server status codes to typed result enums (invalid_email/rate_limited/network/server, invalid_or_expired/invalid_request, etc.). Pre-flight email + token shape validation to avoid pointless round-trips.
- desktop/src/main/auth/deeplink.ts — pure parsing of calmly://auth/callback?token=... (no electron import; vitest-friendly).
- desktop/src/main/auth/deeplink-install.ts — Electron wiring (setAsDefaultProtocolClient, open-url, second-instance).
- desktop/src/main/ipc/auth.ts — ipcMain handlers for auth:status/requestLink/redeem/signOut.
- desktop/src/preload/auth.ts — AuthBridge exposing the above + onDeepLinkRedeemed event subscription.

CHANGED:
- desktop/src/main/index.ts — single-instance lock acquired before whenReady; deep-link install registered early to catch macOS open-url firing before window exists; pendingDeepLinks queue flushed on did-finish-load; cold-start argv scan; main-window webContents.send pushes redeem result on auth:deeplink-redeemed channel.
- desktop/src/preload/{index.ts,api-types.ts} — added auth bridge surface.

WHY no manual Set-Cookie parsing: production fetch is session.defaultSession.fetch (Electron 28+), which auto-handles Set-Cookie into the persistent cookie jar; the existing sync client's getCookieHeader will pick up the auth session cookie automatically. Session persistence is "free" via Electron's persistent cookie store; no extra secretStore round-trip needed.

TESTS (43 new):
- net/__tests__/client.test.ts (8): JSON POST shape, GET no-body, baseUrl trailing-slash strip, 4xx no-retry, 5xx retry-with-backoff up to maxRetries, success after retry, ApiNetworkError after exhausted retries.
- auth/__tests__/session.test.ts (20): isPlausibleEmail / isWellFormedToken edge cases; orchestrator success + every error mapping for requestLink/redeem/status/signOut.
- auth/__tests__/deeplink.test.ts (15): parseDeepLink (extract, percent-decode, case-insensitive scheme, reject unknown protocols/hosts/paths/empty-token, non-strings, optional trailing slash); findDeepLinkInArgv.

title: BUG: ralph worker dies during 'Analyzing response from productive timeout'
description:
## Symptom
Both sonnet and opus workers crash deterministically when they hit ralph's CLAUDE_TIMEOUT_MINUTES=30 limit on iterations with lots of file changes. Log pattern:

```
[WARN] Claude Code execution timed out after 30 minutes
[INFO] Timeout but N file(s) changed — treating iteration as productive
[INFO] Saved Claude session: ...
[INFO] 🔍 Analyzing response from productive timeout...
<process dies here, no Loop #N+1 startup>
```

Observed twice in same session:
- sonnet @ 2026-05-01 10:12:11, 42 files changed
- sonnet @ 2026-05-01 11:20:51, 65 files changed

## Root cause hypothesis
Ralph's productive-timeout analyzer hangs/segfaults parsing very large Claude streaming output. Process tree dies, no clean exit, status.json stays 'running'.

## Fix options
1. File the bug upstream against frankbria/ralph-claude-code
2. Wrap the productive-timeout branch in ralph_loop.sh in a 'timeout' guard that forces a Loop continuation if analysis stalls
3. Lower CLAUDE_TIMEOUT_MINUTES to 15-20m to surface 'too big' beads earlier (forces decomposition, avoids triggering this code path)

## Workaround
Manual relaunch — clear .ralph/.ralph_session + .circuit_breaker_state + .exit_signals + .response_analysis + .call_count + .token_count, then nohup bash start-sonnet.sh.

description:
## Goal
Implement the reminders engine: Important/Soft tiers, user-defined repeat intervals, scheduling, dispatch via Telegram (when linked) with Done/Snooze/Reschedule action buttons, and desktop notification fallback.

## Build order
PRD §23 step 4 (Reminders engine).

## Scope
- ReminderRule data model behavior (schema lives in Epic 1)
- Per-task reminder profile + per-profile defaults in Settings
- Interval scheduler (e.g., every 10m until ack, every 4h, daily) — server-side worker
- Telegram delivery channel: send messages with inline Done/Snooze 10m/Reschedule buttons
- Desktop notification channel as fallback when Telegram not linked
- Inline action handlers (Done closes, Snooze reschedules, Reschedule opens picker)
- "Important" vs "Soft" rendering differences
- Settings → Reminders page: profile editor, defaults

## Out of scope
- Four-tier reminder profiles (PRD §8 explicitly out)
- Adaptive reminder AI (PRD §8)
- WhatsApp/SMS channels (PRD §8)

## Done when
A user can attach a reminder to a task with importance + interval, get pushed to Telegram or desktop, and resolve via Done/Snooze/Reschedule.

## References
PRD §11 Reminders, §7 desktop item 8, §8 Out of Scope (four-tier, WhatsApp/SMS).

title: RM-01: ReminderRule UI + per-task reminder editor
description:
## Goal
Build the per-task reminder editor UI: importance toggle (Important / Soft), repeat interval picker, escalation toggle. Persists a `ReminderRule` attached to the task via the existing data model.

## Scope
- React component `ReminderRuleEditor` (modal/popover invokable from a task row's "..." menu and from task detail)
- Inputs:
  - **Importance**: segmented Important / Soft (default Soft)
  - **Repeat interval**: preset chips (10 min, 30 min, 1 h, 4 h, daily) + "Custom" → number + unit (min/hour/day) — minimum 5 min
  - **Repeat behavior**: "Until I mark Done" (Important default) vs "Once" (Soft default)
  - **Escalation** (Important only): toggle "Bring window forward each repeat" (no system-modal hijack — we are not Windscribe)
  - **Start at**: optional datetime; default = now
- Save → POST/PUT to `/tasks/:id/reminder-rule`; remove → DELETE
- Empty state on tasks: "No reminder" with "Add reminder" link
- Visual indicator on task row when a reminder is set (bell icon, filled for Important / outline for Soft) — full intrusion behavior in rm07
- Form uses Zod validation; reuses shared `ReminderRule` schema from Epic 1 data model

## Files
- `desktop/src/renderer/features/reminders/ReminderRuleEditor.tsx`
- `desktop/src/renderer/features/reminders/ReminderBadge.tsx`
- `desktop/src/renderer/features/reminders/api.ts` (client calls)
- `desktop/src/renderer/state/reminders.ts` (React Query hooks)
- `server/src/reminders/routes.ts` (`PUT /tasks/:id/reminder-rule`, `DELETE /tasks/:id/reminder-rule`, `GET /tasks/:id/reminder-rule`)
- `server/migrations/00xx_reminder_rules.sql` (only if not already created in Epic 1 — check first)
- Tests: component test for editor, integration test for routes

## Acceptance
- Opening editor on a task with no rule shows empty form with defaults; saving creates a `ReminderRule` row linked to the task
- Editing an existing rule pre-fills values; saving updates row
- Removing a rule deletes the row
- Custom interval below 5 min is rejected with inline error
- Bell badge appears on the task row when a rule is set; clicking opens the editor
- Server routes enforce ownership (user can only edit their own task's rule)

## Notes
- Schema `ReminderRule` already exists from Epic 1 (data model). If field shape needs extension (e.g., `escalate` boolean), do it via additive migration — do not break existing fields.
- Per PRD §8: four-tier profiles, adaptive AI, and WhatsApp/SMS are explicitly out of scope.
- Profiles (defaults applied across tasks) are rm02 — this task is per-task only.

## References
PRD §11 Reminders (importance, intervals, actions), §7 desktop item 8, §14 ReminderRule.

description:

title: RM-03: Server-side scheduler/dispatcher worker (interval + dedupe + retry)
description:
## Goal
Build the server-side reminder scheduler/dispatcher worker: wakes on an interval, finds due `ReminderRule` instances, dispatches one notification per due fire, dedupes within a window, retries on transient failure, and records delivery state.

## Scope
- New worker `server/src/reminders/scheduler.ts` running in the same Node process as the API (Fastify plugin with a `setInterval` driver, default tick = 30s)
- Computes next-fire time per rule based on `start_at`, `interval_min`, `last_fired_at`, `repeat_until_done`
- New table `reminder_deliveries` (id, rule_id, user_id, scheduled_for, fired_at nullable, channel, status enum: pending/sent/failed/skipped/acked, attempt_count, last_error)
- Dedupe: do not fire if a `pending` or `sent` delivery exists within the rule's interval/2
- Channel selection logic (interface only — channels themselves in rm04 + rm05): asks `ChannelRouter.pickChannel(userId)` → returns `'telegram' | 'desktop'`; calls `Channel.deliver(delivery)`
- Retry: on `Channel.deliver` failure, increment `attempt_count`; up to 3 attempts with exponential backoff (1m, 5m, 15m); then mark `failed` and emit domain event
- Stop firing rule when associated task is `done` or `archived`
- Manual cancel: `POST /reminder-deliveries/:id/cancel`
- Graceful shutdown on SIGTERM (finish in-flight ticks, persist state)
- Time math uses UTC internally; rule storage uses UTC
- Telemetry counters: `reminders_fired`, `reminders_failed`, `reminders_acked`

## Files
- `server/migrations/00xx_reminder_deliveries.sql`
- `server/src/reminders/scheduler.ts`
- `server/src/reminders/router.ts` (ChannelRouter interface + impl)
- `server/src/reminders/channels/types.ts` (Channel interface)
- `server/src/reminders/state.ts` (next-fire computation, pure functions)
- Tests: `server/src/reminders/scheduler.test.ts` (uses fake timers + mock channels)

## Acceptance
- A rule with `interval_min=10`, `start_at=now-1min` fires once on next tick; the next fire is scheduled 10 min later
- A rule for a `done` task does NOT fire
- Dedupe: triggering two ticks within the same interval does not produce two deliveries
- Failed delivery retries up to 3 times then marks `failed` and emits the domain event
- Tick performance: a 1k-rule scenario completes within 1s on the test runner
- Worker shuts down cleanly on SIGTERM (test asserts no in-flight delivery is duplicated on restart)

## Notes
- Channels are wired by rm04 (Telegram) and rm05 (desktop). Until both land, use a `LogChannel` for tests.
- Distributed locking is not needed at MVP scale — single-process worker is fine. Document as a follow-up risk in scheduler.ts header.
- Calendar reminders (event-time triggers) are out of scope here; only `ReminderRule`-driven.

## References
PRD §11 Reminders (delivery, intervals), §22 Risks, §23 step 4.

title: RM-04: Telegram delivery channel (Done / Snooze / Reschedule buttons)
description:
## Goal
Implement the Telegram delivery channel: takes a `reminder_delivery` row, sends a Telegram message via the outbound infrastructure (Epic 3 tg07), with inline buttons Done / Snooze 10m / Reschedule.

## Scope
- `server/src/reminders/channels/telegram.ts` implementing `Channel` interface
- Message text format:
  - Important: `🔔 *<task title>*\nNext: <next step or '—'>`
  - Soft: `<task title>` (no bell, no bold)
- Buttons (inline, via tg07's `sendMessage`):
  - `Done` → action `reminder.done` with payload `{ deliveryId, taskId }`
  - `Snooze 10m` → action `reminder.snooze` payload `{ deliveryId, minutes: 10 }`
  - `Reschedule` → action `reminder.reschedule` payload `{ deliveryId, taskId }`
- On `TelegramNotLinkedError` from outbound infra: return `{ ok: false, fallback: true }` so router falls back to desktop channel (rm05)
- On Telegram 403 (user blocked bot): same fallback signal + emit domain event (already emitted by tg07; this channel just respects it)
- On other errors: return `{ ok: false, fallback: false }` so scheduler retries
- Updates `reminder_deliveries.status` to `sent` and stores `outbound_message_id` for callback correlation

## Files
- `server/src/reminders/channels/telegram.ts`
- `server/src/reminders/router.ts` (extend: prefer Telegram if linked, else desktop)
- Tests: `server/src/reminders/channels/telegram.test.ts` (mock outbound)

## Acceptance
- Linked user with Important rule receives a bold/bell-prefixed message with all three buttons
- Linked user with Soft rule receives plain message with all three buttons
- Unlinked user → channel returns fallback signal, no message sent
- Blocked user → channel returns fallback signal, delivery marked appropriately
- `reminder_deliveries.outbound_message_id` is populated on success
- Tests verify correct payload shapes for each button

## Notes
- Action handlers (the Done/Snooze/Reschedule logic) are in rm06 — this task only ships the send side.
- Edit-on-snooze (greying out buttons after press) is rm06.
- Depends on tg07 (outbound infra) and rm03 (Channel interface + scheduler).

## References
PRD §11 Reminders (Telegram delivery, action buttons), §7 Telegram bot.

title: RM-05: Desktop notification fallback channel
description:
## Goal
Implement the desktop notification fallback channel: when Telegram is unlinked or fallback is signaled, deliver a reminder via Electron's native notification API with Done / Snooze / Reschedule actions.

## Scope
- New IPC channel `reminders:incoming` from main → renderer
- Server-to-desktop transport: piggyback on the existing sync stream (Epic 1 F-11) — push a `pending_reminder` event to the connected desktop client; client acks
- Main process: receives the event via the sync transport; calls `new Notification({ title, body, actions })`
  - Important: title prefixed with bell, sticky if platform supports
  - Soft: standard notification
  - Three actions: Done / Snooze / Reschedule (Windows uses Action Center buttons; macOS uses notification actions; Linux best-effort)
- Click on notification body opens the desktop app to the task's Focus or detail page
- Action click → POSTs to `/reminder-deliveries/:id/action` with `{ action }` — server handles via rm06's action registry
- If desktop client is offline (no live sync connection), reminder remains `pending`; on reconnect, undelivered reminders within last 30 min are flushed
- New table column `reminder_deliveries.desktop_acked_at` for desktop-side ack tracking

## Files
- `server/src/reminders/channels/desktop.ts`
- `server/src/sync/events.ts` (extend with `pending_reminder` event type)
- `desktop/src/main/reminders/notifier.ts`
- `desktop/src/main/reminders/index.ts` (subscribe to sync events, dispatch to notifier)
- `desktop/src/renderer/state/reminders.ts` (action invocation helper)
- `server/migrations/00xx_desktop_acked.sql`
- Tests: server channel test, desktop notifier unit test (mock Notification)

## Acceptance
- Unlinked user with a fired rule receives a desktop notification with three action buttons
- Clicking Done sends the action POST and the notification dismisses
- Offline desktop client: reminder remains pending; on reconnect within 30 min, notification fires
- Important reminders use bell prefix; Soft do not
- Notifications respect OS-level Do Not Disturb (no special override — we are not Windscribe — per rm07 intrusion design)

## Notes
- Native notifications on Windows require an AppUserModelID and packaged app; in dev, fall back to a basic toast and log a warning.
- Linux notification action support is patchy — fallback is to open the app on click and let the user resolve there.
- Per PRD §8: WhatsApp/SMS channels are out of scope.

## References
PRD §7 Reminders (desktop notification fallback), §11 Reminders (delivery), §13 Error states.

title: RM-06: Inline action handlers (Done / Snooze / Reschedule)
description:
## Goal
Wire the inline action handlers for reminder Done / Snooze / Reschedule, called from both Telegram callbacks and desktop notification action POSTs.

## Scope
- `server/src/reminders/actions.ts` — three handler functions:
  - `handleDone({ deliveryId })`: marks delivery `acked`, marks the underlying rule `done` (stop further fires), marks task complete only if user opted in via setting (default: NO — Done acks the reminder, not the task; explicit per PRD calmness principle). Edits/replaces the original Telegram message to "Done ✓ <title>" with no buttons.
  - `handleSnooze({ deliveryId, minutes })`: marks delivery `snoozed`, schedules a fresh delivery `now + minutes`. Edits original message to "Snoozed until <HH:mm> — <title>" with no buttons.
  - `handleReschedule({ deliveryId, taskId })`: marks delivery `acked`. For Telegram: opens a date-picker mini-flow — sends a follow-up message with date chips (Today evening, Tomorrow, In 2 days, This weekend, Custom). For desktop: deep-links into desktop app's task detail with the date picker focused.
- Register all three with both:
  - Telegram action registry from tg07
  - HTTP route `POST /reminder-deliveries/:id/action` (for desktop)
- Idempotency: pressing Done twice (e.g., user clicks both Telegram and desktop notification) is a no-op on the second call
- Update `reminder_deliveries.status` and `acked_at`
- Audit log: each action records actor (telegram/desktop) + timestamp

## Files
- `server/src/reminders/actions.ts`
- `server/src/reminders/handlers/done.ts`, `snooze.ts`, `reschedule.ts`
- `server/src/reminders/routes.ts` (add `/reminder-deliveries/:id/action`)
- `server/src/telegram/actions.ts` (register handlers — uses registry from tg07)
- `desktop/src/renderer/features/reminders/RescheduleDeepLink.tsx` (handles `calmly://reschedule/<taskId>`)
- Tests for each handler covering idempotency, edit-message behavior, snooze re-scheduling

## Acceptance
- Pressing Done in Telegram: original message becomes "Done ✓ <title>", delivery row `acked`, no further fires
- Pressing Snooze 10m: original message becomes "Snoozed until …", a new delivery is scheduled 10 min later, fires correctly
- Pressing Reschedule (Telegram): user receives the date-chip follow-up; selecting a chip updates `task.due_date` and acks the delivery
- Reschedule (desktop): opens the app on the task with the date picker focused
- Done twice in a row (Telegram + desktop) → second is a no-op (idempotency)
- Action POST endpoint requires authenticated session + delivery ownership

## Notes
- "Mark task done from reminder" remains a setting (default off). The Done button on a reminder closes the reminder, not the task, by design — this aligns with PRD principle of calmness vs. punishment.
- Reschedule's chip presets must match the rest of the app's date chips for consistency.
- Depends on rm03 (delivery rows + scheduler), rm04 (Telegram channel), rm05 (desktop channel + deep link), tg07 (action registry).

## References
PRD §11 Reminders (Done / Snooze / Reschedule actions), §4 Product Principles (calmness, recovery framing), §14 ReminderRule.

title: RM-07: Important vs Soft visual treatment + intrusion behavior
description:
## Goal
Apply the Important vs Soft visual treatment and intrusion behavior across both Telegram delivery and desktop notification, per the PRD's calmness principle: Important is visible and persistent; Soft is unobtrusive. Neither hijacks the user's screen.

## Scope
- Centralize importance-based formatting in `server/src/reminders/formatting.ts`:
  - Telegram message templates: Important uses bell + bold; Soft is plain
  - Desktop notification: Important is sticky (stays in tray until acted on); Soft auto-dismisses after 8s
- Desktop in-app surfaces:
  - Home page "Now" card shows a small bell badge if an Important reminder is currently pending (un-acked)
  - Active-reminder bar at the bottom of the app shell when ≥1 Important reminder is pending — collapsible, shows count, click to expand list with the same Done/Snooze/Reschedule actions
- Soft reminders do NOT show in the active-reminder bar; they only fire as a single notification
- Reminder list view in Settings → Reminders: "Pending now" section showing currently-firing reminders with quick actions
- No screen-takeover modal, no system-level always-on-top windows — explicitly forbidden per PRD §4 (calmness, not punishment)
- Theme tokens: `--reminder-important-fg`, `--reminder-soft-fg`, `--reminder-bell` — added to design tokens

## Files
- `server/src/reminders/formatting.ts` (centralized templates; rm04 + rm05 import from here)
- `desktop/src/renderer/features/reminders/ActiveRemindersBar.tsx`
- `desktop/src/renderer/features/reminders/PendingReminderBadge.tsx`
- `desktop/src/renderer/pages/settings/RemindersSettings.tsx` (extend with Pending Now section)
- `desktop/src/renderer/styles/tokens.css` (add reminder tokens)
- Refactor: rm04's telegram channel and rm05's desktop notifier consume `formatting.ts` (NOT inline strings)
- Tests: snapshot tests for templates (Important + Soft for both channels)

## Acceptance
- Important reminder produces bell+bold Telegram message and sticky desktop notification
- Soft reminder produces plain Telegram message and auto-dismissing desktop notification
- Home page bell badge appears only when ≥1 Important reminder is pending; clears when all are acked
- Active-reminder bar appears with correct count when Important reminders are pending; expanded view exposes Done/Snooze/Reschedule
- Soft reminders do not appear in the active-reminder bar
- No code path uses `alwaysOnTop`, `setAlwaysOnTop`, or `kiosk` mode for reminders (lint check or grep verifies)
- Visual snapshot/manual screenshot pass for Home page with and without pending Important reminders

## Notes
- This task should land AFTER rm04 + rm05 so refactoring the inline templates is meaningful.
- "Intrusion behavior" here means: Important is persistent and visible, Soft is gentle. It does NOT mean steal-focus or modal blocking.
- Per PRD §8: adaptive reminder AI is out of scope — these are static rules.

## References
PRD §11 Reminders (importance levels), §4 Product Principles (calmness, recovery framing), §7 desktop item 8, §8 Out of Scope.

title: RM-08: Reminders lifecycle integration test (virtual clock)
description:
## Goal
Integration test pass for the reminders engine — full lifecycle from rule creation through scheduled dispatch to action handling, on both Telegram and desktop notification channels.

## Scope
- Use the Telegram mock from TG-09 + a desktop notification mock that records `Notification` calls
- Time-control: use a virtual clock (Vitest fake timers or sinon) to advance scheduler ticks without real waits
- Specs:
  1. **Rule creation**: create task with `Important` rule, interval=600s → DB shows ReminderRule + next_due_at
  2. **Telegram dispatch**: linked user, advance clock past next_due_at → mock Telegram captures one `sendMessage` with three inline buttons (Done / Snooze 10m / Reschedule)
  3. **Desktop fallback**: unlinked user, advance clock → desktop notification mock records the call (Telegram mock unchanged)
  4. **Done action**: simulate inline button "done" callback → task status='done', rule deactivated
  5. **Snooze action**: "snooze 10m" callback → next_due_at advanced 10m, rule still active
  6. **Reschedule action**: "reschedule" callback → server emits a follow-up message with date picker; selecting "tomorrow 09:00" updates due_at
  7. **Important vs Soft**: dispatch one of each → assert different message templates (e.g., Soft has no escalation copy, Important repeats per interval)
  8. **Escalation**: Important rule, repeat interval=10m, advance clock 30m without ack → 3 dispatches (idempotent — no dupes within a tick)

## Files

- `server/test/helpers/virtualClock.ts`

## Acceptance

title: F-14e: E2E sync.spec.ts — write on client A → reconnect → client B pulls (multi-client smoke)
description:
## Goal
Guard the cloud-first sync round-trip: write on one client, second client pulls.

## Scope
- desktop/e2e/foundations/sync.spec.ts.
- Steps: launch two Electron instances with DIFFERENT --user-data-dirs but SAME server fixture → sign both in (same user, two cookie jars OR a shared session) → write a synthetic record on client A via window.calmly.db (or sync.push) → wait for sync push → trigger sync pull on client B → assert record visible.
- Note the overlap with F-11c (calmly-76j) — coordinate so we don't write duplicate coverage.

## Acceptance
- Spec passes; tolerates LWW timing (uses expect.poll for the pull).

## Depends on
F-14a, F-14c
notes:
DESIGN: spec at desktop/e2e/foundations/sync.spec.ts.

Two Electron clients with separate user-data-dirs sign in as the same email (server resolves to same user). The 'write on A' step uses HTTP POST to /sync/push from the test process with A's session cookie extracted via electronApp.evaluate({ session }) — neither window.calmly.db nor window.calmly.sync.push exist (renderer has only sync.status and sync.syncNow). Doing the push via the same HTTP path the production sync client uses keeps the assertion meaningful: A's authenticated session writes to the cloud, B's authenticated session pulls.

Then call client B's window.calmly.sync.syncNow() and assert (with expect.poll for LWW timing tolerance) that pulled >= 1 and lastPulledVersion >= server-reported version. Idempotency check: a second syncNow at the same cursor should pull 0 records.

Synthetic record: inbox_items upsert with id=uuid, raw_text='F-14e smoke', source='desktop', created_at=now, plus sync meta (updated_at=now, deleted_at=null, version=0).

Coordinates with F-11c (calmly-76j): F-11c will own the comprehensive sync test (offline → reconnect → soft-delete → idempotency cycling). F-14e stays narrowly the smoke happy-path.

NOT doing: offline mode, soft-delete propagation, asserting record content via a renderer DB read API (none exists; server-side cursor advancement IS the assertion). NOT adding test-only IPC handlers.

Two Electron clients sign in as same user → test process pushes via /sync/push with A's cookie → B's syncNow pulls and cursor advances; idempotent on replay. 6.8-7.7s flow, ~17s incl. testcontainer boot. title: TG-04a: Transcription provider abstraction (types + OpenAI + mock + env)
description:
## Goal
Foundation for TG-04 (voice -> transcript -> Inbox). Abstract the transcription layer so the bot voice handler in TG-04 can call a provider-agnostic interface, and tests can swap in a mock without hitting the network.

This is independent of TG-03's InboxItem creation pattern, so it can land in parallel with calmly-unr (sonnet's TG-03 implementation).

## Scope
- `server/src/transcription/types.ts` — `TranscriptionProvider { transcribe(audio: Buffer, mimeType: string): Promise<TranscriptionResult> }` and `TranscriptionResult { text: string; durationSec: number; }`. Error class `TranscriptionError` with codes: `provider_error`, `audio_too_long`, `unsupported_format`, `auth`, `quota`, `timeout`.
- `server/src/transcription/openai.ts` — `OpenAIWhisperProvider` POSTs to `https://api.openai.com/v1/audio/transcriptions` (model `whisper-1`); maps non-2xx to `TranscriptionError` codes; respects `fetch` abort signal; reads key from constructor.
- `server/src/transcription/mock.ts` — `MockTranscriptionProvider` returns canned transcript; supports failure injection for tests.
- `server/src/transcription/index.ts` — `getTranscriptionProvider(env)` factory: returns OpenAI when `TRANSCRIPTION_PROVIDER=openai` (default) and `OPENAI_TRANSCRIPTION_KEY` is set; returns mock when `TRANSCRIPTION_PROVIDER=mock`; throws if openai chosen without key.
- `server/.env.example` — append `OPENAI_TRANSCRIPTION_KEY`, `TRANSCRIPTION_PROVIDER` (commented, default openai).
- Tests under `server/src/transcription/__tests__/`:
  - `openai.test.ts` — happy path, 401 -> auth, 429 -> quota, network error -> provider_error, abort -> timeout. Uses fetch mock.
  - `mock.test.ts` — happy path + failure injection.
  - `index.test.ts` — factory selects correctly per env, throws on missing key.

## Acceptance
- pnpm typecheck:gated passes (no new errors vs baseline)
- pnpm --filter server test passes for the new suite
- All files <300 LOC
- No telegram dependency: `grep -r telegram server/src/transcription` returns nothing

## Out of scope (TG-04 will pick up)
- Voice message handler in dispatcher
- Telegram `getFile` audio download
- Temp audio file management + 1h retention
- InboxItem creation + ack reply
- 5-min duration check (lives in handler, not provider)

## References
PRD §11 Capture (voice), §17 Cloud transcription, §13 Error states.
notes: Approach: pure functions + factory; provider gets key via constructor (testable). No fs / temp file logic — that's the handler's job in d0p.4. fetch via injectable param so openai.test.ts can mock without nock. AbortController for timeout. Errors: TranscriptionError class with code field (NOT new ipc errors — these are server-internal; the handler maps to user-facing PRD §13 string at telegram-reply layer).
