title: BUG: dev magic-link email points at HTTP redeem URL, doesn't trigger calmly:// deep link
description: In dev (EMAIL_SENDER=console), the magic-link email contains `{APP_URL}/auth/magic-link/redeem?token=...` (e.g. `http://localhost:3001/...`). Clicking it in a browser hits the server's GET handler which returns JSON and sets a cookie on the *browser* — but the desktop app needs a `calmly://auth/callback?token=...` URL to fire its protocol handler (deeplink-install.ts). E2E tests work around this by parsing the token and synthesizing the deep link manually (desktop/e2e/foundations/_helpers.ts:160). Suggested fix: have the GET /auth/magic-link/redeem handler 302 to `calmly://auth/callback?token=...` when the request looks like a browser navigation (Accept: text/html), so clicking the link in any browser opens the desktop app cleanly. Keep the JSON response for programmatic clients (Accept: application/json or X-Requested-With present).
close_reason: GET /auth/magic-link/redeem now 302s browser navigations (Accept: text/html) to calmly://auth/callback?token=...; JSON preserved for programmatic clients. Server vitest covers both branches + edge cases; E2E helper comment updated. (1ffa011)

title: F-03a: Lint + format + Husky + GitHub Actions CI (lint/typecheck/unit jobs)
description:
## Goal
Establish lint, format, and CI infrastructure so every subsequent task can rely on a fast, deterministic check loop. (Playwright + Electron E2E split to F-03b.)

## Scope
- ESLint flat config at root (typescript-eslint + react-hooks + prettier-compatible) — single config covering shared/server/desktop with workspace-specific overrides.
- Prettier config + .prettierignore at root.
- Root scripts: pnpm lint / lint:fix / format / format:check.
- Husky + lint-staged for pre-commit (lint --fix + prettier --write on staged files).
- GitHub Actions CI workflow (.github/workflows/ci.yml) with jobs: setup (cache pnpm + node 20), typecheck, lint, format-check, test (workspace-recursive vitest). Linux-only runner, fail-fast off so each job's status is visible.

## Acceptance
- pnpm lint, pnpm format:check, pnpm typecheck, pnpm test all pass on a clean tree.
- ESLint actually flags a deliberate console.log in a sample file, then is fixed.
- CI workflow file passes yamllint and the jobs run in topological order.

## Out of scope
- Playwright + Electron smoke test → F-03b (calmly-cqp). The CI workflow will gain an e2e job there.
- Pre-existing typecheck/test scripts already work; the bead just adds lint/format on top.
notes:
## Approach (F-03a)

### Stack choices
- ESLint v9 flat config (eslint.config.js at repo root) — single config tree with workspace-aware globs. typescript-eslint v8 with recommended (NOT recommended-type-checked initially — that requires per-tsconfig setup that's overhead for the gain). react-hooks for the desktop/renderer glob. eslint-config-prettier disables style rules so prettier owns formatting.
- Prettier with project defaults: 80-char width, double quotes (matches existing code), semis on, trailingComma=all.
- Husky v9 (modern simple init) + lint-staged for pre-commit (lint --fix + prettier --write on staged).
- GitHub Actions: ubuntu runner, pnpm cache, separate jobs typecheck/lint/format-check/test running in parallel after a single setup. fail-fast off so each surfaces independently.

### Tradeoffs / NOT doing
- NOT enabling type-aware lint rules (no-floating-promises etc.) yet — they're ~5x slower and need parser project config per workspace; revisit when test feedback gets noisy.
- NOT pinning rules tightly: starting with a small allowlist of ESLint defaults + typescript-eslint recommended; tighten later as patterns emerge.
- NOT touching the existing test/typecheck scripts; they already work — just extending the surface.
- NOT writing the Playwright + Electron piece — split to F-03b.

### Risk
Existing code may need a few small fixes (unused vars, missing return types) on first lint run. If the volume is non-trivial, document the known violations rather than reflowing across 50 files.
close_reason:
F-03a complete. Lint + format + CI infrastructure landed.

NEW:
- eslint.config.mjs (flat config) at repo root: typescript-eslint recommended (non-type-checked, fast), react-hooks + react-refresh for the renderer, eslint-config-prettier last so formatter rules don't conflict, CJS override for *.cjs migrations, looser rules for tests.
- .prettierrc.json (80/2-space/double-quote/trailing-comma=all/lf) + .prettierignore (long-form docs, generated dirs, lockfile, GUI_draft.ts).
- Root scripts: pnpm lint / lint:fix / format / format:check.
- Lint-staged config in root package.json (eslint --fix + prettier --write on staged ts/tsx/js + json/md/yml).
- .github/workflows/ci.yml: ubuntu-latest with NODE_VERSION=20, PNPM_VERSION=9.12.3, jobs setup (deps cache) → typecheck / lint / format / test in parallel. concurrency.cancel-in-progress on per-ref so superseded runs don't queue.

CHANGED:
- desktop/src/renderer/auth/AuthContext.ts (new) split off from AuthProvider.tsx so react-refresh/only-export-components stops complaining about hooks-next-to-component exports. Consumers (AuthGate, SignIn, Settings/Account) updated.
- desktop/src/main/net/client.ts: replaced `while (true) // eslint-disable` with `for (;;)` (lint preferred).
- 50+ files reformatted by Prettier on first run; no behavioral changes.

PUNTED to F-03c (calmly): Husky pre-commit hook file (.husky/pre-commit). Husky + lint-staged deps + config are wired; only the hook file itself remained, and the .husky directory was permission-restricted in this iteration.

Verified: pnpm lint / pnpm format:check / pnpm -r typecheck / pnpm -r test all green. 178 tests pass (63 shared + 37 server + 78 desktop).

UNBLOCKS F-03b (calmly-cqp): Playwright Electron config + E2E smoke + CI e2e job — needs playwright-electron-debugger skill.

title: TG-02a: Telegram linking foundation — pg migration + linking service + unit tests
description:
## Goal
Foundation for TG-02 (calmly-d0p.2): server-side state + pure service module that the HTTP routes (TG-02b) and bot /start handler (TG-02b) call into.

## Scope

### Migration (server-only — codes never sync to clients)
`server/migrations/00xx_telegram_linking_codes.cjs` creates:
- code TEXT PRIMARY KEY (8-char alphanumeric, uppercase)
- user_id UUID NOT NULL REFERENCES users(id) ON DELETE CASCADE
- expires_at BIGINT NOT NULL (epoch ms)
- consumed_at BIGINT NULL
- created_at BIGINT NOT NULL
- INDEX (user_id, created_at) for the rate-limit query (count active codes per user)

### Service (`server/src/telegram/linking.ts`)
Exports pure async functions taking a pg.Pool:

- `generateLinkingCode(pool, userId, now)` → `{ ok: true, code, expiresAt } | { ok: false, error: 'rate_limited' }`
  Creates an 8-char code, caps at 5 active per user (active = not consumed AND not expired).
  Code format: A-Z0-9, uppercase, randomly generated, retry on collision.

- `redeemLinkingCode(pool, code, chatId, telegramUsername, now)` → `{ ok: true, userId } | { ok: false, error: 'not_found' | 'expired' | 'already_used' }`
  Atomic transaction: locate code, validate not expired + not consumed, mark consumed, upsert telegram_links row (replacing existing link if user already linked from a different chat — caller logs the change).

- `getLinkingStatus(pool, userId)` → `{ linked: false } | { linked: true, chatId, telegramUsername, linkedAt }`

- `unlinkTelegram(pool, userId)` → `{ ok: true; deleted: number }`

### Unit tests (`server/src/telegram/__tests__/linking.test.ts`)
Use mocked pg.Pool (existing pattern in server/src/auth/__tests__/...). Cover:
- generateCode happy path
- generateCode rate limit (6th request rejected)
- generateCode collision retry
- redeem happy path (uppercase normalization, replaces existing link)
- redeem expired
- redeem already-used
- redeem not-found
- getStatus linked + unlinked
- unlink

## Out of scope (TG-02b)
- HTTP route wiring (POST /telegram/linking/code, GET /telegram/linking/status, POST /telegram/linking/unlink) with auth middleware
- Bot /start handler
- Dispatcher routing for /start
- Integration test using a real DB fixture

## Acceptance
- pnpm typecheck:gated stays clean (no new errors)
- Unit tests pass; coverage on service >= 90%
- Lint clean
- Service has no Fastify or grammy imports — pure pg.Pool consumer
close_reason: Foundation shipped — server-only telegram_linking_codes migration (0010), pure linking service with generateLinkingCode/redeemLinkingCode/getLinkingStatus/unlinkTelegram, and 16 unit tests against a mocked pg.Pool. No Fastify or grammy imports — TG-02b will wire HTTP routes + /start handler + integration test on top. Commit befa285.

title: F-05b: DB round-trip integration test for core model (Vitest + better-sqlite3)
description:
## Goal
Add the integration test that round-trips one row of every table in the core model through better-sqlite3, validating both the SQL schema and the Zod parsers.

## Why this is split from F-05
F-05 lands the schema and Zod types and verifies the migration applies cleanly on a fresh DB via the Electron-launch smoke test. The proper DB round-trip test needs Vitest infra (provided by F-03) and a Node-ABI better-sqlite3 build separate from the Electron-ABI one used at runtime. Splitting keeps F-05 a single-iteration P0 deliverable and lets the sonnet worker land this once F-03 ships.

## Scope
- Add Vitest to desktop (or wherever the test lives) once F-03 brings the test runner
- Resolve the Node vs Electron ABI rebuild problem (e.g., separate `pnpm rebuild-native:node` script, or use node:sqlite, or run tests under Electron)
- For each table in `0003_core_model.sql`:
  1. Apply migrations to a fresh in-memory DB
  2. Insert one row constructed via the Zod schema (`Schema.parse(...)`)
  3. SELECT the row back, parse via `Schema.parse(row)`, deep-equal compare
- Verify FK cascade: deleting a user removes their inbox/tasks/events/etc.
- Verify CHECK constraints reject invalid enum values

## Acceptance
- `pnpm -r test` runs and passes the integration suite
- One round-trip assertion per table
- One cascade assertion (delete user → child rows gone)
- One CHECK violation assertion (bad enum rejected by DB)

## References
PRD §14, parent F-05.
notes:
LANDED: 14 round-trip integration tests in desktop/src/main/db/__tests__/integration.test.ts.

Engine choice. Used node:sqlite (host Node bundled libsqlite) instead of better-sqlite3 to avoid the Electron-vs-Node ABI rebuild trap. Stable in Node 24+, available behind --experimental-sqlite in 22.5+. Migrations are read directly from the .sql files via fs (no shared runMigrations dependency to keep the test self-contained); foreign_keys=ON pragma applied so the cascade assertion exercises the real FK chain.

Coverage. One round-trip assertion (INSERT a Zod-built row, SELECT, parse back through the schema, assert key fields) for users, inbox_items, tasks (with the schedule pair), events, reminder_rules, recurrence_rules, calendar_event_imports, ai_suggestions, telegram_links, user_settings — every domain table the migrations create. PRAGMA table_info(focus_sessions) check confirms all 8 migrations applied cleanly. FK CASCADE assertion: insert user + inbox + task; delete user; both children gone. Two CHECK violation assertions: bad source enum on inbox_items + bad status enum on tasks both throw.

Tradeoffs. (a) node:sqlite vs better-sqlite3 may diverge on libsqlite version specifics; for schema/Zod portability this is low risk. The comment at the top of the file warns against repurposing for performance assertions. (b) Hand-rolled NodeSqliteDatabase typing locally — avoids bumping @types/node workspace-wide for a test-only API. (c) describe.skipIf(!nodeSqlite) gracefully skips if the host Node lacks the module rather than crashing the whole vitest run. (d) ExperimentalWarning fires on Node 22.x but doesn't affect passes; on Node 24+ the warning goes away.

Verified. Typecheck (web + node) clean; eslint clean on the test; 14 new tests pass; 171 desktop total. No new deps, no engines bump.

This pattern is the template for F-08b (server Postgres integration via testcontainers) and F-11c (multi-client sync E2E).
close_reason: 14 round-trip + cascade + CHECK integration tests landed using node:sqlite. Pattern template for F-08b and F-11c.

## Scope

title: POL-01: Telemetry pipeline (opt-in, allow-listed events, client batching + server ingest)
description:
## Goal
Ship the opt-in telemetry pipeline (off by default) — desktop client batching of allow-listed events and a server ingestion endpoint — so adoption / friction signals can be measured without ever capturing task, calendar, Telegram, or API-key content.

## Scope
- Allow-list of event names (e.g., `app.opened`, `capture.created`, `triage.completed`, `ai.suggestion.accepted|rejected|edited`, `error.shown`) — defined in `shared/src/telemetry/events.ts`
- Strict prop allow-list per event: only booleans, ints, short enum strings, and stable IDs (`anonymous_id`, `session_id`); no free text, no titles, no message bodies
- Client batcher: buffers events in SQLite (`telemetry_outbox` table), flushes every 60s or 50 events when telemetry is enabled; drops silently when disabled
- Anonymous device ID generated on first run (UUID v4), stored in secret store; never tied to user account
- Server endpoint: `POST /telemetry/ingest` accepts batched payloads, validates against the same allow-list, writes to `telemetry_events` table; rejects with 400 on unknown event/prop
- Hard kill switch: setting `telemetry.enabled = false` immediately stops emission AND purges outbox
- Reuse `logger.event` allow-list helper from F-13 as the single emission API

## Files
- `shared/src/telemetry/events.ts` (event + prop schema, Zod)
- `shared/src/telemetry/client.ts` (batcher, flush, allow-list enforcement)
- `desktop/src/main/telemetry/index.ts` (SQLite outbox + flush worker)
- `desktop/migrations/00XX_telemetry_outbox.sql`
- `server/src/routes/telemetry.ts` (ingest endpoint)
- `server/migrations/00XX_telemetry_events.sql`

## Acceptance
- With telemetry off (default), zero network calls to `/telemetry/ingest`; outbox stays empty
- With telemetry on, batched events arrive at server within 60s; payloads strictly schema-validated
- Attempting to emit an unknown event name throws in tests; attempting to attach a non-allow-listed prop throws
- Disabling telemetry mid-session purges outbox and stops further sends
- Server rejects payloads containing fields like `title`, `body`, `message` with 400

## Notes
- This task is the pipeline only; the Settings UI (toggle + inspector) is a separate task (`pol_telemetry_ui`).
- Crash reporting is a separate, independent toggle (`pol_crash_reporting`).
- Keep the anonymous_id rotation policy documented but not user-facing in MVP.

## References
PRD §18 Telemetry (opt-in, captures listed; never captures task/calendar/Telegram content/API keys), §23 step 9, §4 (Trustworthy, transparent).
close_reason: pipeline + schema + worker + server endpoint + 14 tests; off by default

title: POL-10: Visual regression + a11y + anti-shame copy audit
description:
## Goal
Visual regression and accessibility audit pass — Playwright visual snapshots of every primary screen + axe-core a11y sweep. Locks the design language in place and surfaces accessibility regressions.

## Scope
- **Visual regression**:
  - Playwright `toHaveScreenshot()` snapshots of: Home (empty + populated), Inbox (focused triage), Plan (with events + tasks), Focus (active session + idle), Review (with completed items), Settings (each sub-page), Sign-in
  - Light + dark theme variants (if dark theme implemented; else single mode)
  - Snapshots stored under `desktop/e2e/visual/__snapshots__/`
  - Update flow: `pnpm test:visual --update-snapshots` for intentional changes
- **Accessibility audit**:
  - `@axe-core/playwright` integration; one check per primary screen
  - Zero violations of `wcag2a` and `wcag2aa` rules
  - Manual a11y checklist (in this task's PR description): keyboard-only walkthrough, focus order, screen-reader names for icons
- **Anti-shame language audit**: programmatic check that copy strings on error/empty/recovery screens do NOT contain banned words from `desktop/src/copy/banned.ts` (e.g., "failed", "you should have", "missed", "wasted") — replace with PRD §4 anti-shame alternatives

## Files
- `desktop/e2e/visual/{home,inbox,plan,focus,review,settings,signin}.visual.spec.ts`
- `desktop/e2e/a11y/all-screens.spec.ts`
- `desktop/test/copy/banned-words.spec.ts`
- `desktop/src/copy/banned.ts` — list of banned words + suggested replacements

## Acceptance
- Visual snapshots committed; CI fails on diffs
- Zero axe wcag2aa violations across all primary screens
- No banned words in any user-facing string (test scrapes the bundled renderer for known copy keys)
- Manual checklist completed and recorded in the PR

## Skills
**Invoke `frontend-design`** to review the snapshots and inform per-screen visual decisions before locking them in. The skill helps avoid the generic-AI-aesthetic trap and aligns with PRD §4 design principles.
**Invoke `playwright-electron-debugger`** for the Playwright visual + a11y harness — flake-resistant snapshot configuration in Electron is non-trivial.

## Notes
- Snapshots are notoriously flaky on different render backends — pin the CI runner to a fixed image and run with `--reporter=line`.
- This task is the design-quality gate before MVP ship.

## References
PRD §4 Product Principles, §13 Empty/Error states (anti-shame language).

title: POL-02: Telemetry settings UI — toggle + 'what is sent' inspector
description:
## Goal
Build the Settings UI for telemetry — a clear opt-in toggle, a "what is sent" inspector showing the exact payload of buffered events, and the ability to opt out at any time — so users can verify the privacy claim themselves.

## Scope
- Settings → Privacy → Telemetry section
- Toggle: "Help improve Calmly with anonymous usage data" — off by default; copy explains what is + isn't sent in plain language
- "What is sent" inspector: live view of the most recent N (e.g., 50) events currently buffered in the outbox, with raw JSON expandable per event
- Inspector also shows the static allow-list (event names + accepted props) so power users can audit what's possible to send
- "Send a test event now" button (dev/QA aid; gated to non-prod or always-on but harmless)
- Disabling the toggle immediately calls the purge hook from `pol_telemetry_pipeline`
- Link to the public docs page describing the telemetry endpoint (placeholder URL is fine)

## Files

- `desktop/src/renderer/pages/Settings/Privacy/TelemetryInspector.tsx`
- `desktop/src/preload/telemetry.ts` (narrow IPC: `getOutbox`, `getAllowList`, `setEnabled`, `purge`)
- Settings copy in `shared/src/copy/settings.ts`

## Acceptance
- Toggling off purges outbox and stops emission (verified in e2e test)
- Inspector shows real buffered events when telemetry is on; shows empty state with allow-list reference when off
- Copy passes the anti-shame / transparency review: no dark-pattern phrasing, default state is clearly OFF
- Keyboard-accessible: tab order, screen-reader labels on toggle and JSON disclosure controls

## Notes

title: POL-03: Crash reporting (Electron crashReporter, opt-in, separate toggle)
description:
## Goal
Ship opt-in Electron crash reporting as a toggle separate from telemetry, so users can choose to share native crashes (main + renderer) without enabling usage telemetry.

## Scope
- Activate Electron `crashReporter` (configured during F-13 with `uploadToServer: false`); flipping the Settings toggle enables `submitURL` and uploads
- Server endpoint: `POST /crash/ingest` accepts minidump uploads (multipart/form-data); stores blob + metadata to disk or object storage path; no user content beyond stack
- Strip identifiers: no email, no anonymous_id correlation with telemetry events; just `app_version`, `os`, `process_type`
- Settings → Privacy → Crash Reports section: independent toggle with copy explaining what's in a crash report and what isn't
- "View last crash report" button if a dump exists locally (read-only inspector listing file size, timestamp, version)
- Toggle change requires restart to take effect — surface a clear non-modal banner saying "Restart Calmly to apply"
- Default OFF on every fresh install and after migration

## Files
- `desktop/src/main/crash/index.ts` (configure crashReporter, handle restart-required state)
- `desktop/src/renderer/pages/Settings/Privacy/CrashReportSection.tsx`
- `server/src/routes/crash.ts`
- `desktop/src/preload/crash.ts` (narrow IPC: `getStatus`, `setEnabled`, `getLastReportMeta`)

## Acceptance
- Default OFF; toggling ON + restart begins uploading on next crash
- Toggling OFF prevents any upload after next start; in-flight queued dumps are deleted from local cache
- Crash payload contains no email, no task content, no API keys (verified by test that triggers a renderer crash and inspects the captured file)
- Server endpoint accepts a dump and returns 202; rejects oversized payloads (>10 MB) with 413

## Notes
- Symbol upload + symbolication is out of scope for this task; raw dumps are enough for MVP.
- Settings UI lives next to the telemetry section but the toggles are wholly independent.

## References
PRD §18 Telemetry ("crash reports are separate and also opt-in"), §4 (Trustworthy), §23 step 9.

title: POL-04: Error states pass — calendar, OAuth, Telegram, voice transcription, sync (shared <ErrorState>)
description:
## Goal
Implement consistent, recovery-oriented error states for all integration failures from PRD §13 — calendar fail, OAuth expired, Telegram offline / blocked / not linked, voice transcription failed, sync failed — backed by a shared `<ErrorState>` component so every state answers: what happened, what to do, whether anything is lost.

## Scope
- Build `<ErrorState>` component: icon, headline, body copy, primary action button, optional secondary "learn more" link, optional "loss disclosure" line ("Nothing is lost — your captures are safe locally")
- Variants per integration failure with concrete copy + recovery action:
  - Calendar connection failed (Google or Microsoft) → "Reconnect"
  - Calendar OAuth token expired → "Sign in again"
  - Telegram offline (delivery failed network) → "Retry now"; auto-retry with backoff in background
  - Telegram bot blocked / user removed bot → "Re-link Telegram" with link flow entry point
  - Telegram bot not linked but feature expects it → "Link Telegram" deep link to Settings
  - Voice transcription failed → "Retry transcription" + offer typed fallback for the captured audio
  - Sync failed (local cache out of date) → show last-sync timestamp, "Try again" button; clarify local edits are queued
- Wire each failure code path to render `<ErrorState>` with the right variant; no raw stack traces shown to user
- Each variant emits a telemetry `error.shown` event with `error_type` enum (using the allow-list from `pol_telemetry_pipeline`)

## Files
- `desktop/src/renderer/components/ErrorState/ErrorState.tsx`
- `desktop/src/renderer/components/ErrorState/variants.ts` (variant catalog with copy)
- `shared/src/errors/codes.ts` (canonical error code enum used by client + server)
- Update integration call sites:
  - `desktop/src/renderer/pages/Plan/CalendarPanel.tsx`
  - `desktop/src/main/calendar/oauth.ts` (surface expiry as code)
  - `desktop/src/renderer/pages/Settings/Integrations/Telegram.tsx`
  - `desktop/src/main/telegram/delivery.ts`
  - `desktop/src/renderer/pages/Inbox/VoiceItem.tsx`
  - `desktop/src/main/sync/queue.ts`

## Acceptance
- Every listed failure mode has an automated test that forces the failure and asserts the corresponding `<ErrorState>` variant renders with the right copy + action
- Copy reviewed against §4 anti-shame principle (covered comprehensively in `pol_anti_shame_copy`); this task ships baseline copy that the copy pass will refine
- No raw error string from a network/library leaks into the UI — only mapped error codes
- Recovery actions actually work: clicking "Reconnect" on a calendar failure triggers the OAuth flow

## Notes
- AI / Ollama failures are intentionally OUT of scope — see `pol_error_states_ai`.
- The shared `<ErrorState>` is reused by `pol_empty_state_polish` for empty-but-actionable states; design the props API to accommodate both.

## References
PRD §13 Error states (calendar fail, OAuth expired, Telegram offline / blocked / not linked, voice transcription failed, sync failed), §4 (Recovery-centered, Anti-shame), §23 step 9.

title: POL-05: Error states pass — AI / Ollama failures (key, quota, timeout, not running)
description:
## Goal
Implement error states for all AI failure modes from PRD §13 — Ollama not running / model not pulled, API key missing or invalid, API call failed or timed out, API quota exceeded — using the shared `<ErrorState>` component, so AI failures degrade gracefully and never break the deterministic core loop.

## Scope
- Variants in the `<ErrorState>` catalog, each with concrete recovery action:
  - Ollama not running → "Start Ollama" hint + docs link; the surrounding feature still works in deterministic mode
  - Ollama model not pulled → show selected model + `ollama pull <model>` hint
  - API key missing → "Add API key in Settings" deep link to Settings → AI
  - API key invalid (401/403) → "Update API key" + reason ("the provider rejected this key")
  - API call timed out → "Try again"; never silently retry on cloud-key cost-bearing calls
  - API quota exceeded (429 / provider-specific quota) → clear copy that this is the user's own provider account, not Calmly's; link to provider billing page
- AI buttons (Triage Cleanup, Make Startable, Brain-dump Split, Stuck Help, Daily Plan) degrade to inline `<ErrorState>` rather than disappearing

title: POL-06: Onboarding refinement — 5-min first-run, integration prompts deferred to moment-of-need
description:
## Goal
Tighten the onboarding flow so a brand-new user can complete first-run in under 5 minutes by signing in via magic link only, with every integration prompt deferred to the moment the user first reaches a feature that needs it.

## Scope
- First-run flow: app open → magic-link sign-in → land on Home with a friendly empty Now view; nothing else required
- Remove any forced setup steps for Telegram / Google / Microsoft / Ollama / API keys from first-run
- Moment-of-need prompts (small inline cards, dismissable, never modal blockers):
  - First time user opens Plan with no calendar connected → "Connect a calendar to see your day"
  - First time user wants mobile capture / requests reminder via desktop → "Link Telegram for mobile capture"
  - First time user toggles AI on → branch into Local (Ollama setup hint) or Cloud (API key entry) based on chosen mode
  - First time user toggles Local AI mode and Ollama is unreachable → "Install or start Ollama" hint
- Each prompt has "Maybe later" — user can dismiss without penalty; reappears next time they hit the same trigger
- Track `onboarding.first_run_completed_at` and per-integration `prompt_seen_at` / `prompt_dismissed_at` in local settings (not in telemetry — purely local)
- Settings → Integrations remains the single page exposing the full integration surface

## Files
- `desktop/src/renderer/pages/FirstRun/FirstRun.tsx` (sign-in only; no integration steps)
- `desktop/src/renderer/components/PromptCard/PromptCard.tsx` (dismissable inline card)
- `desktop/src/renderer/features/onboarding/prompts.ts` (catalog of moment-of-need prompts + their triggers)
- `desktop/src/renderer/pages/Plan/EmptyCalendarPrompt.tsx`
- `desktop/src/renderer/pages/Settings/Integrations/index.tsx` (verify it's the single full-surface page)

## Acceptance
- Manual time-trial: a fresh install reaches a usable Home state in under 5 minutes (sign-in is the only required step)
- No integration prompt appears in first-run; each only appears when its feature is first opened
- Dismissed prompts stay dismissed for that session and across restarts until the trigger fires again
- Settings → Integrations still exposes all five integrations for users who want to set them up proactively

## Notes
- Empty-state visuals/copy on Home / Inbox / Plan are refined by `pol_empty_state_polish`; this task wires the integration-prompt logic only.
- Anti-shame copy pass (`pol_anti_shame_copy`) refines wording later.

title: POL-07: Keyboard shortcuts pass (Cmd/Ctrl+K, capture hotkey, focus controls, navigation, docs)
description:
## Goal
Implement and document a coherent keyboard-shortcut layer — global capture hotkey, in-app command palette, focus-session controls, navigation — so the keyboard-first principle is realized.

## Scope
- Global capture hotkey (default `Cmd/Ctrl + Shift + Space`) opens the quick-capture popover from anywhere on the OS; configurable in Settings
- Command palette: `Cmd/Ctrl + K` opens search + actions (jump to page, run command, find a task)
- Navigation: `g h` (Home), `g i` (Inbox), `g p` (Plan), `g f` (Focus), `g r` (Review) — vim-style chord navigation
- Focus session controls: `Space` to start/pause focus timer, `Esc` to end session early, `n` to mark current task done and pick next
- Inbox triage: `j` / `k` to move selection; `Enter` to triage; `1` / `2` / `3` for triage actions
- Settings → Keyboard page: lists every shortcut, allows rebinding the global capture hotkey, reset-to-defaults button
- Help modal: `?` shows context-aware shortcut list for the current page
- All shortcuts respect the focused element (don't fire when typing in an input unless the chord is global)

## Files
- `desktop/src/renderer/features/shortcuts/registry.ts` (single source of truth for shortcuts + descriptions)
- `desktop/src/renderer/features/shortcuts/useShortcut.ts` (hook + global manager)
- `desktop/src/renderer/components/CommandPalette/CommandPalette.tsx`
- `desktop/src/renderer/components/ShortcutHelp/ShortcutHelp.tsx`
- `desktop/src/main/globalShortcut.ts` (registers OS-level capture hotkey via Electron `globalShortcut`)
- `desktop/src/renderer/pages/Settings/Keyboard/KeyboardSection.tsx`

## Acceptance
- Every shortcut listed in the registry is wired and tested; `?` modal renders the full list
- Global capture hotkey opens the capture popover even when Calmly isn't focused
- Rebinding the global hotkey persists across restarts; conflict detection rejects already-claimed combos with a clear message
- Shortcuts don't fire while user is typing in a text input (except global ones)
- Settings → Keyboard documents every shortcut; matches the in-app help modal exactly (single source of truth)

## Notes
- Mac Cmd vs Windows/Linux Ctrl is handled by a single `mod` token in the registry.
- Accessibility: every shortcut has a non-keyboard equivalent; `?` modal is screen-reader-readable.

## References
PRD §4 Product Principles (Keyboard-first), §12 (low cognitive load), §23 step 9.

title: POL-09: Anti-shame language pass — copy review across all error/empty/recovery states
description:
## Goal
Do a comprehensive copy review across every error state, empty state, and recovery flow so the app's voice consistently honors the §4 anti-shame principle — "language supports recovery, not guilt."

## Scope
- Build a copy style guide: voice, tone, banned phrases (e.g., "you forgot", "you missed", "you failed", "you're behind"), preferred phrases (e.g., "ready when you are", "this can wait", "your captures are safe")
- Audit and rewrite every string in:
  - `desktop/src/renderer/components/ErrorState/variants.ts`
  - `desktop/src/renderer/components/EmptyState/variants.ts`
  - Reminder delivery copy (Telegram + desktop) for missed / overdue items
  - Sync-failure / OAuth-expired / quota-exceeded copy specifically — these are highest-friction moments
  - "Make Startable" and "Stuck rescue" AI copy — must never imply user is stuck because of a personal failing
  - Daily Shutdown / Review copy when items roll over uncompleted

title: F-11b: Sync protocol v1 — desktop client (op_queue, sync loop, backoff, offline replay)
description:
## Goal
Wire the desktop side of sync protocol v1 against the server contract that F-11 lands.

## Why this is split from F-11
F-11 ships the protocol types in @calmly/shared/sync, the server-side migration with domain tables + sync columns, and the /sync/pull + /sync/push endpoints with LWW idempotency. The desktop client (op_queue, sync_state, sync loop, exponential backoff, IPC surface) is its own ~3h slice and lands once the server contract is stable.

## Scope
- Desktop migration adds version + deleted_at columns to F-05's domain tables (or builds on a fresh sync schema if cleaner).
- New tables: op_queue(id, table, op, payload_json, created_at, attempts, last_error) and sync_state(last_pulled_version, last_pushed_at).
- desktop/src/main/sync/{client.ts,queue.ts,loop.ts}: HTTP client against the server, queue persistence, background loop driven by network events + 30s tick.
- Backoff: 1s, 2s, 4s, ..., cap 60s on failed push.
- IPC surface: window.calmly.sync.{status, sync()} so the renderer can show a sync indicator and trigger manual sync.

## Acceptance
- Offline write → record lands in op_queue
- Reconnect → queue drains; first failure backs off exponentially
- Pull is idempotent: same since-version returns same records
- pnpm -r test green with sync-loop unit tests (mock HTTP)

## Notes
- Real cross-device E2E (write on client A, read on client B) is F-11c.
notes:
Approach (full F-11b, single iteration):
- Migration 0005_sync_columns.sql: ALTER each of F-05's 9 STRICT domain tables to add `version INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0` and `deleted_at INTEGER NULL` (SQLite STRICT permits ADD COLUMN when the type is one of the strict types and the new column is NULL or has a literal DEFAULT — our types satisfy both). Plus new STRICT tables: op_queue(id TEXT PK, table_name, op CHECK IN ('upsert','delete'), payload_json, created_at, attempts, last_error) and sync_state singleton (id PK CHECK id=1, last_pulled_version, last_pushed_at).
- src/main/sync/backoff.ts: pure function attempts→delayMs (1s, 2s, 4s, ..., cap 60s) — Vitest-tested as the only easy unit-test.
- src/main/sync/queue.ts + state.ts: take a Database.Database parameter so they're testable without the better-sqlite3 native binding (Electron-ABI ≠ Node-ABI). Real callers pass getDb().
- src/main/sync/client.ts: pull/push wrappers around fetch, sending the calmly_session cookie from Electron's session cookie jar so auth round-trips. Returns parsed PullResponse / PushResponse from @calmly/shared/sync.
- src/main/sync/loop.ts: start/stop background tick; on each tick, drain the queue (push), then pull new since the cursor; on push failure, increment attempts and back off; on pull failure, just retry next tick. Triggered manually via IPC + every 30s + on app online events.
- IPC: window.calmly.sync.{status(), syncNow()} via narrow preload bridge.

Tradeoffs: NOT validating ops against domain schemas before queuing (Zod validation lands when individual mutators are written — the queue is content-agnostic). NOT handling token-refresh / re-auth — when the server returns 401, the loop logs and pauses; F-10 will own re-auth. NOT pursuing per-table cursor — global since-version (server uses one sequence). NOT writing E2E (split: F-11c).
close_reason: Sync protocol v1 desktop client live. Migration 0005_sync_columns.sql adds version (DEFAULT 0) + deleted_at (NULL) to F-05's 9 STRICT domain tables — verified cold-boot logged 'version=5 appliedNow=[1,2,3,4,5]'. Plus new STRICT tables op_queue (id, table_name, op CHECK 'upsert'|'delete', payload_json json_valid, created_at default unixepoch*1000, attempts, last_error) and sync_state singleton (id PK CHECK id=1). queue.ts and state.ts take a Database parameter so they're testable without the better-sqlite3 native binding. backoff.ts is pure math — 1s, 2s, 4s, ..., capped at 60s. client.ts wraps fetch with an injected cookie-header function so Electron's session cookie jar drives auth. loop.ts implements runSyncOnce: drain queue (push), advance cursor (pull), with retry-eligible filtering (rows wait until created_at + backoff(attempts) ≤ now). Accepted/stale/gone results all remove the op (replay-safe); invalid bumps attempts. createSyncLoop wraps it with start/stop/syncNow and a 30s interval. IPC: window.calmly.sync.{status, syncNow}. 12 desktop unit tests (6 backoff + 6 loop) cover happy path, replay safety, error handling, and cursor monotonicity. Typecheck clean. Note: electron-vite externalizeDepsPlugin needed an exclude for @calmly/shared so the schema imports actually bundle. CALMLY_SYNC_URL env var with default localhost:3001 picks the server. Real auth wiring (writing the calmly_session cookie into Electron's session jar after redeem) is F-10's job; multi-client E2E is F-11c (calmly-76j).

title: F-13b: Desktop logging — electron-log file output, renderer→main IPC bridge, crashReporter wiring
description:
## Goal
Wire the desktop side of F-13's logging contract into Electron.

## Why this is split from F-13
F-13 lands the shared scrub regex set, the strict EventProps allow-list, and the server's pino-backed logger. The Electron-specific pieces (electron-log file rotation, renderer→main IPC log bridge, crashReporter init with uploadToServer=false default) deserve their own iteration once the contract is stable, and they need playwright-electron-debugger to verify properly.

## Scope
- Add electron-log to desktop; configure rotating JSON-line file at app.getPath('logs')/calmly.log
- desktop/src/main/logging/index.ts — Logger implementation that calls scrub on all string fields, exposes makeEvent() backed by electron-log
- IPC handler 'log:event' that the renderer's typed bridge calls
- desktop/src/preload/log.ts — narrow typed bridge: only event(name, props), no raw log forwarding
- desktop/src/main/index.ts — call electron crashReporter.start({ uploadToServer: false }) before app.whenReady
- LOG_PII env-gated escape hatch for dev — prod builds hard-disable

## Acceptance
- Cold-boot writes to calmly.log on disk
- Renderer's window.calmly.log.event(...) round-trips to main and lands in the file
- A planted "sk-ant-test123..." string in a log message is replaced with [REDACTED:api_key_anthropic]
- crashReporter.getUploadToServer() returns false by default

## References
F-13, PRD §18.
notes:
## Approach

Reuse the F-13 shared contract verbatim, port to desktop via electron-log.

### Layers
1. desktop/src/main/logging/index.ts — createDesktopLogger({ transport, allowPii }): Logger.
   Mirror of createServerLogger: scrub() on every message + every string field + every event prop value (defense in depth).
2. desktop/src/main/logging/electron-log-transport.ts — configureElectronLog (file path, rotation, JSON-line format) + electronLogTransport(level, msg, fields). Runtime-only — not imported by tests.
3. desktop/src/main/ipc/log.ts — registerLogIpc(logger): only 'log:event'. Renderer cannot forward raw log.{trace,info,...} to keep the IPC surface narrow.
4. desktop/src/preload/log.ts — LogBridge: { event(name, props) } only.
5. desktop/src/main/index.ts — crashReporter.start({ uploadToServer: false }) BEFORE app.whenReady; configureElectronLog() at module scope; create logger + registerLogIpc inside whenReady.

### Testability
The transport is injected. Tests pass a vi.fn capturing records and assert scrub + sanitize behavior without touching electron-log. electron-log itself is exercised manually + future F-14 E2E.

### LOG_PII gate
allowPii = !app.isPackaged && process.env.LOG_PII === 'true'. In packaged builds, LOG_PII is hard-disabled regardless of env value.

### What this is NOT
- No telemetry upload pipeline (Epic 9).
- Not migrating existing console.log calls in main/index.ts — adds one logger.info("boot") to exercise the path; per-call migration is a follow-up.
- crashReporter dump collection only; no upload.
close_reason:
F-13b complete. Desktop logging — electron-log file output, renderer→main IPC bridge, crashReporter wiring.

NEW:
- desktop: electron-log@5.2.0 dependency.
- desktop/src/main/logging/index.ts — createDesktopLogger({transport, allowPii}). Mirrors createServerLogger: scrub on every message + every string field + every event prop value (defense in depth against tokens that fit the EventProps shape regex).
- desktop/src/main/logging/electron-log-transport.ts — configureElectronLog (calmly.log filename, 10 MB rotation, JSON-line format) + electronLogTransport mapping LogLevel→electron-log levels (trace→silly, fatal→error).
- desktop/src/main/ipc/log.ts — registerLogIpc; only 'log:event' (renderer can't dump raw log lines).
- desktop/src/preload/log.ts — LogBridge: { event(name, props) }.
- desktop/src/preload/api-types.ts — LogBridge surfaced on CalmlyApi.
- desktop/src/preload/index.ts — wired log bridge.

CHANGED:
- desktop/src/main/index.ts:
  - crashReporter.start({ uploadToServer: false, productName, submitURL }) BEFORE app.whenReady so even early failures get dumped locally.
  - configureElectronLog() at module scope; createDesktopLogger created with ALLOW_PII = !app.isPackaged && process.env.LOG_PII === 'true' (packaged builds hard-disable PII regardless of env).

title: CAL-01: Google Calendar OAuth flow (server callback proxy + scopes + refresh token)
description:
## Goal
Implement the end-to-end Google Calendar OAuth flow so a user can connect their Google account from the desktop client and the server captures a refresh token via a callback proxy.

## Scope
- Server-side OAuth callback proxy on the sync server: `GET /oauth/google/start`, `GET /oauth/google/callback`
- Scopes: `https://www.googleapis.com/auth/calendar.readonly`, `openid`, `email`, `profile`
- PKCE + `state` (CSRF) parameters with state tied to authenticated user session
- Exchange code for tokens server-side; capture `refresh_token` (force `access_type=offline&prompt=consent` to ensure issuance)
- Hand refresh token + access token + expiry back to the client over an authenticated channel (signed short-lived bundle the client redeems via `POST /oauth/google/redeem`)
- Client-side trigger: open external browser to start URL, listen for `calmly://oauth/google/done?ticket=...` deep-link, redeem ticket, persist via F-12 secret store (real persistence in cal-2)
- Connection metadata row: `CalendarAccount(provider='google', external_account_id, email, status)`

## Files
- `server/src/routes/oauth/google.ts` — start, callback, redeem
- `server/src/services/googleOAuth.ts` — token exchange + ticket signing
- `server/src/db/migrations/00xx_calendar_account.sql` — accounts table
- `desktop/src/main/calendar/googleOAuth.ts` — open browser, deep-link handler, redeem ticket
- `desktop/src/preload/calendar.ts` — `calendar.connectGoogle()` (returns connection status)
- `shared/src/types/calendar.ts` — `CalendarAccount`, `OAuthRedeemTicket`

## Acceptance
- A user clicks "Connect Google" in Settings → Calendar (placeholder UI ok), browser opens, user consents, deep-link returns to app, refresh token is persisted via F-12, `CalendarAccount` row exists with `status='connected'`
- `state` mismatch or expired ticket returns clear error and does not persist
- Refresh token is never logged or sent to telemetry
- Forcing the consent flow guarantees `refresh_token` is present even on re-connect

## Notes
- Token storage uses the secret-store key `calendar.google.refresh_token:<account_id>` defined in F-12 — DO NOT invent a new keychain.
- Microsoft 365 lives in cal-ms-oauth and mirrors this structure.
- Display UI polish (cards, status pills, last-sync) is in cal-settings-page; this task only needs a minimal entry point.

## References
PRD §15 Calendar Integration, §22 risks (calendar OAuth edge cases), §14 (encrypted at rest).
notes: Approach: server-side OAuth proxy. (1) /oauth/google/start (auth'd) generates PKCE+state, stores in oauth_states table (10min TTL), redirects to Google with access_type=offline&prompt=consent. (2) /oauth/google/callback (public) validates state, exchanges code w/ verifier, fetches userinfo, upserts calendar_accounts row, stores tokens in oauth_tickets (5min TTL, one-shot, raw — internal-only), renders HTML that opens calmly://oauth/google/done?ticket=<jti>. (3) POST /oauth/google/redeem (auth'd) validates HMAC-signed ticket bound to user_id, returns refresh+access+expiry+account, deletes ticket row. Client persists refresh in F-12 secret store and writes a local-only calendar_accounts mirror row. Generic OAuth state/ticket helpers (oauth/state.ts, oauth/tickets.ts) — CAL-02 (microsoft) reuses them. Tradeoffs: brief window where refresh tokens sit in DB unencrypted (5 min, one-shot deletion) — acceptable for MVP, can add at-rest encryption later. NOT doing: actual calendar event fetching (CAL-04), automatic access-token refresh loop (CAL-03), settings UI polish (cal-settings-page).
close_reason: CAL-01 shipped. Server: PKCE state store, signed one-shot ticket helper, /oauth/google/start|callback|redeem, calendar_accounts upsert. Desktop: connectGoogle() (browser → deep-link → redeem → F-12 secret store → local mirror), extended deep-link parser for calmly://oauth/<provider>/done?ticket=, calendar IPC bridge. Shared types (CalendarAccount, OAuthRedeemResponse). Migrations on server (0007) + desktop (0016). 3 schema-parity allow-list entries documented. Tests: pkce, tickets (round-trip + tampered/wrong-user/replay/expired), googleProvider (auth URL + exchange + userinfo), connectGoogle orchestration (happy/timeout/browser-fail/401/network/secret-store-fail), extended deeplink parser tests. Lint + server typecheck + shared typecheck clean; desktop typecheck has 0 new errors (pre-existing pile unrelated). Routes registered only when GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID + secret configured.

title: CAL-02: Microsoft 365 Calendar OAuth flow (parallel to Google)
description:
## Goal

## Scope

- Authority: `https://login.microsoftonline.com/common/oauth2/v2.0` (multi-tenant; supports work + personal)

- Exchange code for tokens server-side; capture `refresh_token` (requires `offline_access` scope)

## Notes
- Reuse the ticket-signing helper from cal-google-oauth — do not re-invent it. If you need to refactor it into a shared service in `server/src/services/oauthTickets.ts`, do so.
- Graph API consumption (event fetching) lives in cal-import-worker.

title: CAL-03: Encrypted refresh-token storage + access-token refresh (uses F-12 secret store)
description:
## Goal
Wire calendar refresh-token persistence and retrieval through the F-12 secret store so OAuth tokens are encrypted at rest and only the main process can use them.

## Scope
- Typed accessor module: `calendarTokens.set(provider, accountId, refreshToken)`, `.get(provider, accountId)`, `.delete(provider, accountId)`
- Backed by F-12 `secretStore` with namespaced keys `calendar.<provider>.refresh_token:<account_id>`
- Access-token cache (in-memory, never written to disk) with expiry timestamp; a `getAccessToken(provider, accountId)` helper that refreshes via the provider's token endpoint when expired
- Refresh failures (revoked, invalid_grant) mark the `CalendarAccount.status = 'reauth_required'` and surface an event the renderer can subscribe to
- IPC: renderer can call `calendar.disconnect(accountId)` which clears the secret AND the account row

## Files
- `desktop/src/main/calendar/tokens.ts`
- `desktop/src/main/calendar/refresh.ts` — provider-agnostic refresh dispatcher
- `desktop/src/main/calendar/providers/google.ts`, `providers/microsoft.ts` — refresh endpoints + scopes
- Extend `desktop/src/preload/calendar.ts` with `disconnect`, `listAccounts`, `onAccountStatusChanged`

## Acceptance
- Stored refresh tokens roundtrip through encrypted storage (DB inspection shows ciphertext)
- Calling `getAccessToken` when access token is fresh returns from cache without network
- When access token is expired, refresh is called and a new access token is cached
- Revoking the token externally → next refresh returns `invalid_grant` → `CalendarAccount.status = 'reauth_required'` and renderer receives event
- `disconnect(accountId)` removes the secret AND the account row; subsequent `listAccounts` does not include it

## Notes
- DO NOT expose access tokens or refresh tokens to the renderer over IPC — only status booleans and identifiers.
- This task assumes cal-google-oauth and cal-ms-oauth have already populated the secret store on first connect; this task generalizes the read/refresh path.
- Backoff on refresh failures: exponential, capped at 5 min, halt after 5 consecutive failures and mark `reauth_required`.

## References
PRD §14 (API keys / tokens encrypted at rest), §15, §22 risks (token expiry).
notes: Approach: server-mediated refresh (path A). Desktop reads refresh_token from F-12, POSTs to server /oauth/{provider}/refresh with {account_id, refresh_token}; server has client_id+secret, exchanges via provider refresh-grant, returns {access_token, expires_in, refresh_token?}. Desktop caches access_token in-memory only and rotates the F-12 refresh entry if MS rotated it. invalid_grant → desktop marks local account 'reauth_required' and emits status event over IPC. Schema: add 'reauth_required' to calendarAccountStatuses (shared model + desktop migration + server migration — all three). New desktop modules: calendar/tokens.ts (typed F-12 accessor), calendar/refresh.ts (in-memory cache + getAccessToken with exponential backoff capped 5 min, halt after 5 consecutive failures). Server: extend google/microsoftProvider with refreshToken() helper; new generic refresh route in plugin. IPC: calendar.disconnect(accountId) + onAccountStatusChanged event. Tests: tokens roundtrip, refresh cache hit/miss, invalid_grant→reauth_required, backoff, disconnect, server refresh endpoint happy + invalid_grant + auth-fail. NOT doing: actual calendar event fetch (CAL-04), settings UI polish (cal-settings-page), token-expiry banner UI (CAL-06).
close_reason: CAL-03 shipped. Server: refresh-grant helpers (refreshGoogleAccessToken, refreshMicrosoftAccessToken) under shared OAuthRefreshError vocabulary; new POST /oauth/{provider}/refresh and /disconnect routes wired into the provider plugin. Plugin split into types.ts + connectRoutes.ts + manageRoutes.ts + 29-line plugin.ts shell to stay under 300 LOC. Schema: added 'reauth_required' to calendarAccountStatuses (shared model + desktop migration 0017 + server migration 0008). Desktop: calendar/tokens.ts (typed F-12 accessor), calendar/refresh.ts (in-memory access-token cache, 30s safety margin, exponential backoff capped at 5 min, escalates to reauth_required after 5 consecutive transient failures, surfaces invalid_grant→reauth_required immediately, persists Microsoft rotated refresh tokens, flips status back to connected on recovery), calendar/statusEvents.ts (in-process pubsub), calendar/localStore.ts extended with markStatus + delete + get. IPC: calendar:disconnect (server delete + token delete + local delete + status event; falls through on 401/network so users aren't stuck), calendar:onAccountStatusChanged via webContents.send. connectProvider.ts now uses calendarTokens helper instead of raw secretStore. Tests: 8 server refresh-grant unit tests (Google/Microsoft happy + invalid_grant + provider_error + network_error + missing fields), 11 desktop refresh tests (cache hit/miss, MS rotation, invalid_grant→event, backoff, escalation to reauth_required, no_account, short-circuit on prior reauth_required, recovery to connected, network_error), 12 calendar IPC tests (auth-fail + bad-payload + happy + server failure modes + status broadcast). All typecheck + lint clean; 0 new schema-parity drift.

title: CAL-04: Calendar import worker (periodic + on-demand, recurrence + timezones)
description:
## Goal
Implement a calendar import worker that fetches events from each connected provider on a schedule (and on demand), expands recurrences, normalizes timezones, and writes `CalendarEventImport` rows to the local cache.

## Scope
- Periodic worker in main process: every 15 min while app is running, and on-demand via `calendar.refresh(accountId?)` IPC
- Window: from `now() - 1d` to `now() + 30d` (sliding); incremental sync uses provider sync tokens where available (Google `syncToken`, Microsoft `deltaLink`)
- Recurrence: request server-expanded instances where supported (Google `singleEvents=true&timeMin=&timeMax=`, Microsoft `calendarView` endpoint) so we never expand RRULE locally
- Timezones: store all times as UTC `INTEGER` epoch ms in DB, plus original timezone string for display; convert to user's local TZ in the renderer
- Event de-duplication by `(provider, account_id, external_id)`; updates use `recurringEventId + originalStartTime` for instance-level identity
- Cancellations: provider returns `status='cancelled'` → soft-delete the row (or hard delete after 24h)
- Migration: `CalendarEventImport(id, account_id, provider, external_id, recurring_event_id, title, location, start_utc, end_utc, all_day, tz, status, etag, updated_at)` with index on `(account_id, start_utc)`
- Concurrency: only one import per account at a time; queue further requests

## Files
- `desktop/src/main/calendar/importWorker.ts`
- `desktop/src/main/calendar/providers/google.ts` — `listEvents`, `delta`
- `desktop/src/main/calendar/providers/microsoft.ts` — `calendarView`, `delta`
- `desktop/src/main/db/migrations/00xx_calendar_event_import.sql`
- `shared/src/types/calendar.ts` — extend with `CalendarEventImport`

## Acceptance
- After connecting a Google account with a recurring weekly meeting, the next 4 instances appear as separate rows in `CalendarEventImport`
- Re-running import does not duplicate rows; updated event titles are reflected
- A cancelled instance disappears from the active set
- Timezone smoke test: an event created in `Europe/London` while the user's machine is in `America/New_York` shows the correct local start time
- On-demand `calendar.refresh()` returns within ~5s for accounts with <500 events
- A token in `reauth_required` is skipped without crashing the worker

## Notes
- DO NOT implement RRULE expansion ourselves — both providers offer expanded views; use them.
- Bidirectional write-back is OUT OF SCOPE (PRD §15).
- Plan UI integration is cal-plan-display, not this task.
- All-day events: store `all_day=true` and use date-only semantics; do not apply TZ conversion.

## References
PRD §15, §22 risks (recurrence, timezones), §14 Data Model (CalendarEventImport).

Remaining children: calmly-1f0 (Google provider, P2), calmly-e68 (Microsoft provider, P2), calmly-u7h (worker + IPC + integration tests, P2). All three depend on at1. This bead stays open until all three close, then the original ta0.4 acceptance can be re-validated end-to-end.

title: CAL-06: Token-expiry handling + re-auth prompt
description:
## Goal
Detect expired or revoked calendar OAuth tokens, surface a clear re-auth prompt to the user, and complete the re-auth flow without losing imported event history or requiring full disconnect.

## Scope
- Trigger: `CalendarAccount.status` transitions to `reauth_required` (set by cal-token-storage refresh failures)
- In-app banner on Plan and Settings → Calendar: "Reconnect <provider> calendar to keep events fresh" + Reconnect button
- Settings → Calendar shows per-account status pill: Connected / Syncing / Needs reauth / Error
- Reconnect button starts the same OAuth start flow as initial connect, but reuses the existing `CalendarAccount` row (matches by `external_account_id` + provider) instead of creating a new one
- On successful re-auth, status flips back to `connected`; `lastSyncAt` is preserved; import worker resumes on next tick
- Events imported before re-auth are NOT deleted; only stale events older than the import window are pruned naturally
- Tested error paths: user denies consent on re-auth, user picks a different account on re-auth (treat as new account, do not silently rebind)

## Files
- `desktop/src/renderer/components/CalendarReauthBanner.tsx`
- `desktop/src/renderer/pages/Settings/Calendar.tsx` — extend cal-settings-page with re-auth UI states
- `desktop/src/main/calendar/reauth.ts` — orchestration
- Extend `desktop/src/preload/calendar.ts` with `reconnect(accountId)`

## Acceptance
- Manually marking an account as `reauth_required` in DB causes the banner to appear on Plan and Settings → Calendar within 5s
- Clicking Reconnect completes a new OAuth round-trip, status flips to `connected`, banner disappears
- Imported events from before the re-auth are still visible
- If the user picks a different Google/MS account during re-auth, the original account row stays in `reauth_required` and a new account row is created
- Refresh-failure backoff (5 consecutive failures) flips status correctly even if the user is offline temporarily

## Notes
- Do NOT auto-disconnect on first refresh failure — only after the backoff threshold from cal-token-storage.
- Re-auth UX must be calm and non-punishing per PRD voice; copy: "Your calendar needs to reconnect. Nothing is lost — just sign back in."
- Email-based fallback nudges are out of scope.

## References
PRD §13 Error states (calendar OAuth token expired, calendar connection fails), §15, §22 risks.

title: TG-09b: Telegram Update payload builders for integration specs
description:
## Goal
Test fixture builders that produce well-typed grammy `Update` objects for the TG-09 integration specs. The seven specs (linking, inbound text, inbound voice, /now, /today, /inbox, outbound) each need to feed canned updates through the dispatcher; without shared builders each spec re-rolls verbose Telegram payload literals.

This is independent of every handler — pure data factories — so it lands cleanly on the opus branch alongside the mock harness (TG-09a / calmly-2g0).

## Scope
- `server/src/test-utils/telegramUpdates.ts`
  - export `makeBaseUpdate(opts?: { update_id?, chat_id?, user_id?, message_id? })` returning the common shell
  - export `makeTextUpdate(text: string, opts?)` — text message Update
  - export `makeStartUpdate(code?: string, opts?)` — `/start` or `/start <CODE>` text Update
  - export `makeCommandUpdate(command: '/now' | '/today' | '/inbox', args?: string, opts?)` — slash-command text
  - export `makeVoiceUpdate(opts?: { fileId?, durationSec?, mimeType? })` — voice message Update
  - export `makePhotoUpdate(opts?)` — covers the "I only handle text and voice" branch
  - export `makeCallbackQueryUpdate(callback_data: string, opts?)` — for TG-07 outbound action button assertions
- All builders return real `Update` from `grammy/types` (not `any`) so future schema changes break compile, not runtime.
- Defaults are deterministic but distinct per type (sensible chat_id, user_id, message_id) and overridable via opts.
- Tests: `server/src/test-utils/__tests__/telegramUpdates.test.ts`
  - one test per builder asserting the shape (top-level keys, nested .message / .voice fields)
  - overrides apply (changing chat_id or fileId surfaces correctly)
  - makeStartUpdate('ABC123') -> message.text === '/start ABC123'
  - makeStartUpdate() -> message.text === '/start'
  - makeCommandUpdate('/today', 'tomorrow') -> message.text === '/today tomorrow'
  - photo update has no .text and no .voice; covers the "neither text nor voice" branch dispatcher logs

## Acceptance
- pnpm typecheck:gated passes (no new errors vs baseline)
- vitest run passes for the new suite (>= 8 tests)
- File <300 LOC (likely ~150)
- No imports from server/src/telegram/* — pure builders, no handler coupling

## Out of scope (later TG-09 children)
- Wiring updates through the real dispatcher (needs the test app builder and the actual handlers to be on the branch)
- Per-spec setup for linking/text/voice/commands/outbound
- Postgres test pool builder (a separate fixture layer)

## References
TG-09 (calmly-d0p.9), TG-09a (calmly-2g0).
notes:
Approach: thin factory module — one exported function per Update shape, all returning grammy Update typed-precisely. Deterministic defaults (chat_id=12345, user_id=67890, message_id increments) with opts override. Tests just assert structure since logic is trivial.

Tradeoffs: hand-rolling the literals vs faker — the surface is small enough that hand-rolling beats a dep. Keeping builders in test-utils/ rather than __tests__/__fixtures__/ so non-test code (e.g., dev seed scripts) could reuse later if needed.

Not doing: a full Update generator (msw-style) — overkill for seven specs. Not adding builders for inline_query, callback_query results, etc. that the bot doesn't dispatch yet.
close_reason: Closed

title: Deterministic core loop: Capture to Review (no AI/Telegram/calendar)
description:
## Goal
Ship the deterministic (no-AI, no-Telegram, no-calendar) full daily loop: a user can capture an item, triage it, plan their day, focus on a task, replan when off-track, and complete daily shutdown — all from the desktop app.

## Build order
PRD §23 step 2 (Deterministic core loop).

## Scope
- Home screen: Now, Next, Today; persistent capture bar; conditional Inbox/Triage card; Replan + Quick Plan entry points
- Capture: quick-add UI + global hotkey; persists to InboxItem
- Inbox / Triage: one-item-at-a-time UI; classify type, due-date chips, route to Today/This Week/Later; inline "break it down"; snooze/skip
- Plan: day view with manual time blocks (no calendar import yet), drag/drop reorder, simple reschedule
- Focus: current task + next step view; soft time visibility; ad-hoc focus blocks; "I'm stuck" deterministic prompts (no AI)
- Replan: push/drop/shrink/move; framed as recovery
- Review / Daily Shutdown: completed list, carry-forward, drop/move, optional one-line reflection
- Quick Plan ritual: morning confirm reorder/drop/shrink

## Out of scope (covered by other epics)
- AI suggestions of any kind (Epics 7–8)
- Calendar import (Epic 5)
- Telegram or any reminders (Epics 3–4)
- Full-text search overlay (Epic 6)

## Done when
All core-loop tasks closed AND a single user can complete the full Capture→Triage→Plan→Focus→Replan→Review loop in one day on desktop with no AI / Telegram / calendar configured.

## References
PRD §5 (Core Value Prop), §7 (MVP Scope desktop), §9 (Core Journey), §11 (Functional Requirements), §13 (Empty/Error States).
notes:
## UI design reference
Use `GUI_draft.ts` (repo root) as the visual + interaction reference for this task. It establishes the palette (stone + emerald), shapes (soft rounded — `rounded-[1.8rem]`, `rounded-[2.5rem]`), typography (serif italic hero headers, sans body), iconography (lucide-react + custom MountainClimberIcon), kanban-column layout for Inbox/Today/This Week, drag-and-drop affordances, and motion (fade-in / slide-in). Reuse its Tailwind class patterns unless there is a clear reason to deviate. Pair with the `frontend-design` skill after loading the draft.

title: CL-01: Home screen — Now/Next/Today layout + Replan + QuickPlan entry points
description:
## Goal
Build the desktop Home screen — the daily landing surface that shows Now, Next, and Today's commitments, hosts the persistent capture bar, surfaces a conditional Inbox/Triage card when items need attention, and exposes Replan + Quick Plan entry points.

## Scope
- Replace the F-06 Home placeholder with the real layout
- Three primary regions, top to bottom:
  - **Now** card — current focused task (or empty-state CTA "Start a focus block")
  - **Next** card — next scheduled commitment (task or event)
  - **Today** list — chronological list of today's planned tasks/events (read-only here; full edit in Plan)
- Persistent capture bar pinned to top or bottom of viewport (renders on every page, lives in AppShell — can land here or in CL-CAPTURE; whichever ships, the other consumes the slot)
- Conditional **Inbox / Triage** card appears when `inbox_items.resolved_at IS NULL` count > 0; shows count + "Triage now" button → routes to `/inbox`
- **Replan** button (top-right of Today region) → opens Replan UI (CL-REPLAN)
- **Quick Plan** button → opens Quick Plan ritual (CL-QUICKPLAN)
- Reads from local SQLite via the renderer→main bridge; uses a typed `window.calmly.tasks.listToday()` IPC handler

## Files
- `desktop/src/renderer/pages/Home/Home.tsx` (replace placeholder)
- `desktop/src/renderer/pages/Home/NowCard.tsx`
- `desktop/src/renderer/pages/Home/NextCard.tsx`
- `desktop/src/renderer/pages/Home/TodayList.tsx`
- `desktop/src/renderer/pages/Home/InboxTriageCard.tsx`
- `desktop/src/main/ipc/today.ts` — IPC handlers for `tasks.listToday`, `events.listToday`, `inbox.unresolvedCount`
- `desktop/src/preload/index.ts` — extend bridge

## Acceptance
- Opening the app on a day with 2 scheduled tasks renders Now (first task) + Next (second task) + Today list with 2 items
- With 0 unresolved inbox items, the Inbox/Triage card is NOT rendered
- With ≥1 unresolved inbox item, the card renders with the correct count and routing works
- Clicking Replan opens the Replan UI (a stub modal is acceptable until CL-REPLAN ships)
- Clicking Quick Plan opens the Quick Plan ritual (stub modal acceptable until CL-QUICKPLAN ships)
- E2E test: seeded DB → Home screen → assert Now/Next/Today regions render expected text

## Notes
- Empty states for the regions live in CL-EMPTYSTATES; this task can use placeholder strings.
- Capture bar implementation itself lives in CL-CAPTURE; this task only reserves the AppShell slot and consumes the count.
- No drag/drop here — Today list is read-only on Home.

## References
PRD §7 item 1 (Home), §9 Morning, §10 Screen List, §11 (general home behavior).
notes:
LANDED: vertical slice complete and tested.

Read IPC stack:
- main/today/store.ts: pure SQL helpers — listTodayTasks, listTodayEvents, countUnresolvedInbox. Each takes (db, userId, now, tzOffsetMinutes) so unit tests stay deterministic. localDayWindow handles TZ math (8 tests covering UTC, +/- offsets, range placeholders, empty results).
- main/ipc/today.ts: tasks:listToday, events:listToday, inbox:unresolvedCount handlers. Each reads currentUser; returns NotSignedIn discriminant when absent.
- preload/today.ts + extended InboxBridge: TasksBridge.listToday, EventsBridge.listToday, InboxBridge.unresolvedCount join the existing CalmlyApi.
- main/index.ts: registerTodayIpc() wired into whenReady.

UI:

title: CL-10: 'I'm stuck' deterministic guided prompts (no AI)
description:
## Goal
Implement the "I'm stuck" guided rescue inside Focus mode using a fixed, deterministic prompt sequence (no AI). One question at a time; the user can answer, skip, or exit at any step.

## Scope
- "I'm stuck" button in CL-FOCUS opens an inline overlay (does not change route)
- Fixed prompt sequence (5 prompts; user can answer in a textarea or skip):
  1. "What's the smallest next thing you could do — even something tiny?"
  2. "Is the task unclear? If so, what's the question?"
  3. "Do you need a person, an answer, or a piece of info?"
  4. "Could a 5-minute version count as done?"
  5. "Can you switch to a different task and return later?"
- One question on screen at a time; **Next** advances; **Back** goes back; **Skip** advances without saving; **End rescue** closes the overlay
- Answers (if any) saved as a single appended note on the current task — append to `tasks.notes` with format `\n\n--- Stuck rescue (ISO timestamp) ---\nQ: ...\nA: ...\n` (one block per session)
- After step 5, show outcome buttons:
  - **Continue current task** → close overlay, return to ActiveSession
  - **Switch task** → opens SwitchTaskPicker (CL-FOCUS)
  - **Take a break** → ends focus session, returns to Home
- Track each rescue session in `stuck_sessions` table (new migration `0008_stuck_sessions.sql`) — id, focus_session_id, started_at, ended_at, outcome enum

## Files
- `desktop/src/renderer/pages/Focus/StuckPrompts.tsx`
- `desktop/src/renderer/pages/Focus/StuckPromptStep.tsx`
- `desktop/src/main/db/migrations/0008_stuck_sessions.sql`
- `desktop/src/main/ipc/focus.ts` — extend with `focus.startStuckSession`, `focus.endStuckSession(outcome, answers[])`
- `shared/src/model/focus.ts` — extend with StuckSession schema

## Acceptance
- Clicking "I'm stuck" opens overlay on prompt 1
- Filling answers for prompts 1, 3 and skipping 2, 4, 5 then clicking "Continue current task" appends a notes block to the task with only the answered Qs
- Clicking "Switch task" ends the stuck_session with outcome='switch' AND opens the switch picker
- Clicking "Take a break" ends both the stuck_session AND the focus_session
- Unit test: prompts array is the source of truth; verify exactly 5 prompts in correct order
- E2E test: full flow — open, answer one, skip one, end with switch outcome — assert DB rows

## Notes
- Prompts are hardcoded in MVP. User-customizable prompt list is post-MVP.
- AI-assisted rescue is Epic 7/8 — keep this overlay strictly deterministic.
- Failure behavior (PRD §6): even if AI is later enabled, this deterministic flow remains the fallback.

## References
PRD §11 Focus ("'I'm stuck' triggers guided help, one question at a time"), §6 Failure behavior.

title: CL-11: Ad-hoc focus blocks — start focus on a not-yet-scheduled task
description:
## Goal
Allow the user to start a focus session on a task that wasn't pre-scheduled — including creating a brand-new task in the moment — so Focus is usable even when the day has no plan.

  1. **Pick from any open task** — searchable list of all tasks where status='open' (today + future + undated)
  2. **Capture & focus** — single text input "What are you focusing on?"; on submit:
     - Creates a new Task with title=text, due_at=today, source='desktop'
     - Immediately starts a focus session with `source='ad-hoc'`
     - Skips inbox/triage entirely (it's already actionable since the user is starting it)
- The ad-hoc session shows a small "Ad-hoc" pill near the title to distinguish from scheduled

title: CL-12: Replan UI — push, drop, shrink, move; reachable from Home/Plan/Focus
description:
## Goal
Build a unified Replan UI accessible from Home, Plan, and Focus that lets the user push, drop, shrink, or move tasks in bulk — framed as recovery, not failure — when the day's plan goes off track.

## Scope
- Replan trigger lives in three places: Home (button on Today region), Plan (button on day grid header), Focus (button in ActiveSession)
- Replan modal shows today's remaining (not-yet-done) tasks from now forward, in chronological order
- Per row: title, current scheduled time, four action buttons:
  - **Push** — push by 30m / 1h / 2h (segment buttons); ripples forward (subsequent tasks shift to avoid overlap)
  - **Drop** — confirms once, moves to backlog
  - **Shrink** — duration buttons 15m / 30m
  - **Move to date** — date picker; clears scheduled_*; sets due_at to selected date
- Multi-select via row checkboxes; "Apply to selected" bar appears with the same four actions for batch ops
- "Why are you replanning?" optional dropdown at the top: "Ran late" / "Got stuck" / "Priorities changed" / "Other" — saved to `replan_events` table for telemetry (see Epic 9; here just store)
- "Done — replanned" button closes the modal; changes are applied optimistically as the user makes them, Done just closes
- Reframing copy at top: "Your day shifted. Let's adjust." (no "you fell behind", no shaming language)

## Files
- `desktop/src/renderer/components/Replan/ReplanModal.tsx`
- `desktop/src/renderer/components/Replan/ReplanRow.tsx`
- `desktop/src/main/db/migrations/0009_replan_events.sql`

- `desktop/src/renderer/pages/Home/Home.tsx`, `Plan/Plan.tsx`, `Focus/Focus.tsx` — wire entry points

## Acceptance
- Pushing a 10:00 AM task by 1h moves it to 11:00 AM AND shifts the 11:00 AM task to 12:00 PM (ripple)
- Multi-selecting two tasks and clicking "Drop" moves both to backlog in a single transaction
- Reason dropdown value is persisted to `replan_events` even if the user closes without other changes
- Modal is reachable from all three entry points (Home/Plan/Focus) and shows identical state
- E2E test: open from Focus, push current task by 30m, close modal, verify Plan grid reflects change

## Notes
- AI replan suggestions are Epic 7/8 — no AI affordance here.

title: CL-13: Review / Daily Shutdown — completed list, carry-forward, reflection
description:
## Goal
Replace the F-06 Review placeholder with the Daily Shutdown ritual — show what got done today, walk unfinished items through carry-forward / drop / move, and capture an optional one-line reflection so the day ends cleanly.

## Scope
- `/review` route renders three sections, top to bottom:
  - **Completed today** — read-only list of tasks where `status='done'` AND `updated_at` is today; show count prominently ("You completed 7 things today")
  - **Unfinished today** — tasks where status='open' or 'in_progress' AND (due_at = today OR scheduled today); per-row actions:
    - **Carry forward** (default) — sets due_at to tomorrow; clears scheduled_*
    - **Drop** — sets status='dropped'
    - **Move to date** — date picker
    - **Done** — quick mark-complete in case the user forgot earlier
  - **Reflection** — optional single-line input "One word about today" or longer free-text (max 280 chars); saved to `daily_reflections` table (new migration `0010_daily_reflections.sql`)
- "Complete shutdown" button at bottom — sets `user_settings.last_shutdown_date = today`, navigates to Home, shows a calm closing toast ("Day closed.")
- "Skip shutdown" button — closes without writing reflection; does NOT mark last_shutdown_date
- Header shows date + total time focused today (sum of focus_session durations)
- Keyboard: `C` = carry forward selected, `D` = drop selected, `Enter` = complete shutdown

## Acceptance
- With 7 done today + 3 unfinished today, the screen shows "7 completed" and 3 actionable rows
- Clicking "Carry forward" on an unfinished task sets due_at=tomorrow and removes it from today's view; verify via /plan tomorrow
- Saving reflection "long day" persists a row in `daily_reflections` with date=today and text="long day"

title: CL-14: Empty states for the 5 PRD §13 states (first-open, inbox, plan, focus, review)
description:
## Goal
Implement the five PRD §13 empty states with calm, useful, ADHD-friendly copy and clear primary actions — replacing the placeholder strings left throughout Epic 2.

## Scope
The five states (PRD §13):
1. **First open with no items** — Home empty (no tasks, no inbox, no schedule)
   - Headline: "Welcome to Calmly. Capture anything to start."
   - Primary action: focus the CaptureBar (no scary onboarding wall)
   - Secondary: small link "Take the 60-second tour" (stub — full onboarding is in Epic 9; here just hide the link if the tour component doesn't exist)
2. **Empty inbox** — `/inbox` with zero unresolved items
   - Headline: "Inbox clear."
   - Sub: "Anything you capture will land here."
   - Action: Back to Home button + show the CaptureBar prominently
3. **Nothing scheduled today** — `/plan` and Home Today region with zero items
   - Headline: "Nothing on the schedule."
   - Sub: "Pick something from your backlog or capture a new task."
   - Actions: "Open backlog" + "Start ad-hoc focus"
4. **No current focus task** — `/focus` with no active session AND no candidates today
   - Headline: "No focus right now."
   - Sub: "Start an ad-hoc focus block, or pick from any open task."
   - Actions: "Start ad-hoc focus" + "Pick a task"
5. **Review with no completed items** — `/review` where today's done count is 0
   - Headline: "Some days are heavy. That's okay."
   - Sub: "You can still close out the day."
   - Action: "Complete shutdown" still available (no reflection required)

title: CL-15: Full daily-loop E2E test pass (Capture → Review)
description:
## Goal
Full daily-loop E2E test pass that exercises the deterministic core loop end-to-end: Capture → Inbox → Triage → Plan → Focus → Replan → Review. This is the MVP gating test for Epic 2 — if this passes, the deterministic shape of the product is provably working.

## Scope
- One Playwright spec `loop.spec.ts` that walks the full happy path:
  1. **Capture**: invoke global hotkey, type "buy birthday card", press Enter — verify InboxItem row created
  2. **Triage**: open `/inbox` triage focused mode → classify as task → set due_at = today → route to "Today" → next item
  3. **Plan**: navigate to `/plan` → drag the new task to the 14:00 slot → assert scheduled_at persisted
  4. **Focus**: from Home, click "Start focus" on the 14:00 task → assert FocusSession row created → click "Mark done" → assert task.status = 'done', session.ended_at set
  5. **Replan**: with one remaining unfinished task, open Replan from Focus → "Push to tomorrow" → assert due_at advanced
  6. **Review**: navigate to `/review` → assert "1 completed today" + "1 unfinished" → carry-forward unfinished → save reflection "long day" → complete shutdown → assert reflection persisted, last_shutdown_date set
- Negative-path mini-specs: capture without title (should reject), triage skip (item stays in inbox), Replan drop (task → status='dropped')
- Empty-state spec: fresh user → Home shows first-open empty state → capture flow still works
- CI integration: `e2e-core-loop` job depends on `e2e-foundations`

## Files
- `desktop/e2e/core-loop/loop.spec.ts` — the main happy-path spec
- `desktop/e2e/core-loop/negative.spec.ts`
- `desktop/e2e/core-loop/empty-state.spec.ts`
- `desktop/e2e/fixtures/seedUser.ts` — pre-signed-in fixture (reuses foundations fixture)

## Acceptance
- All three spec files pass on a clean tree
- The happy-path spec runs in under 60 seconds locally
- Each step uses semantic locators (role/name/testid), not nth-child or pixel positions
- Trace artifacts upload on failure
- Test isolation: each spec gets a fresh DB (truncate or new userData dir)
