title: CL-02: Quick capture — input UI + global hotkey + persists to InboxItem
description:
## Goal
Implement the always-on quick capture: a persistent input UI in the AppShell, a global desktop hotkey, and an IPC path that persists raw text into `inbox_items` in under 5 seconds end-to-end.

## Scope
- Persistent **CaptureBar** component rendered by AppShell on every route
  - single-line text input + "Add" button
  - Enter submits; input clears; brief inline confirmation ("Added to Inbox")
- **Global hotkey** (default `CmdOrCtrl+Shift+I`) registered in main process via `globalShortcut`
  - When pressed, focuses the app window and focuses the CaptureBar
  - Shortcut is overridable from settings JSON (don't build the settings UI here — just read from `user_settings`)
- IPC handler `inbox.add(rawText: string, source: 'desktop')`
  - Inserts into `inbox_items` with `created_at = now()`, `resolved_at = NULL`
  - Returns the new item ID
- Optimistic UI: input clears immediately; if insert fails, restore text and surface inline error
- Trims whitespace; rejects empty strings; soft cap at 4000 chars (truncate + warn, do not silently drop)

## Files
- `desktop/src/renderer/components/CaptureBar.tsx`
- `desktop/src/renderer/layout/AppShell.tsx` (add slot for CaptureBar)
- `desktop/src/main/ipc/inbox.ts` — `inbox.add` handler
- `desktop/src/main/shortcuts.ts` — global shortcut registration / unregister on app quit
- `desktop/src/preload/index.ts` — add `window.calmly.inbox.add`
- `shared/src/model/inbox.ts` — re-use existing schema

## Acceptance
- Typing "buy milk" + Enter creates a row in `inbox_items` with raw_text="buy milk", source="desktop"
- Pressing the global hotkey from another app focuses Calmly and places cursor in CaptureBar
- Submitting empty string is a no-op (no DB write, no error toast)
- Unit test: `inbox.add` rejects empty/whitespace, accepts valid strings, truncates at 4000 chars
- E2E test: type into capture bar, press Enter, assert toast + new inbox row visible on /inbox

## Notes
- AI parsing / brain-dump split is explicitly OUT of scope here (Epic 7).
- Global shortcut conflicts: if registration fails, log a warning; the in-app input still works. Settings UI to remap is in Epic 9.
- Voice capture is Telegram-only per PRD §8 — do not add a mic button.

## References
PRD §11 Capture, §7 item 2, §4 (low-friction principle).
notes:
LANDED: Full vertical slice complete and tested.

Implementation:
- main/inbox/store.ts: addInboxItem with trim → reject empty / truncate at 4000 → INSERT + enqueueOp inside one tx (6 tests, including FK-failure rollback path).
- main/auth/currentUser.ts: module-level cache + INSERT OR REPLACE INTO users mirror so the inbox_items.user_id FK resolves the moment a session is in hand (4 tests).
- main/ipc/inbox.ts: single 'inbox:add' handler. Reads currentUser, hardcodes source='desktop', returns NotSignedIn discriminant when no cached user.
- main/shortcuts.ts: registerCaptureHotkey('CmdOrCtrl+Shift+I'). Show + focus + send 'capture:focus'. Graceful failure path (returns {registered:false}); unregisterAllShortcuts on app.before-quit.
- main/index.ts: orchestrator wrapper now calls setCurrentUser on every redeem.ok / status / signOut. registerInboxIpc + registerCaptureHotkey wired in whenReady. Hotkey skipped when NODE_ENV=test so parallel e2e instances don't fight for the OS handler.
- preload/inbox.ts + api-types.ts: InboxBridge exposes add() + onFocusRequest(); CalmlyApi includes the new bridge.
- renderer/components/CaptureBar.tsx: persistent top-of-main bar. Optimistic clear, restore on failure, fades 'Added to Inbox' / 'Added (trimmed at 4000 chars)' confirmation after 1.8s, error states for EmptyInput/NotSignedIn/InternalError. Subscribes to onFocusRequest for the global hotkey.
- renderer/layout/AppShell.tsx: CaptureBar mounted above <Outlet/> inside <main>; Outlet wrapped in scrollable div so the bar stays pinned.
- e2e/foundations/capture.spec.ts: signs in → types → asserts inline toast → sync.syncNow asserts pushed>=1 (proves both local commit + op_queue happened atomically) → IPC truncation path.

title: CL-03: Inbox list view — browse, sort, snooze, skip
description:
## Goal
Replace the F-06 Inbox placeholder with a real browsable list view of unresolved inbox items, with sort, snooze, and skip controls — the "overview" surface complementing the focused triage view (CL-TRIAGE).

## Scope

title: CL-04: Triage focused mode — classify, due-date chips, route to Today/Week/Later
description:
## Goal
Build the focused triage mode: one inbox item at a time, classify its type, assign a date via quick chips, and route it to Today / This Week / Later by converting it into a Task (or Event, or discarding it).

## Scope
- Route `/inbox/triage` (optionally `?id=<itemId>` to start at a specific item)
- Walks unresolved inbox items in order; auto-advances on resolve
- Per-item card shows raw_text large + source + created_at
- **Type classifier** (radio/segment): Task | Event | Reference/Note (Note → discard for MVP, no Notes feature) | Discard
- **Title field** (editable; defaults to raw_text)
- **Due-date chips**: Today | Tomorrow | This Week (sets due_at to Friday this week) | Later (no due_at) | Pick date (date picker)
- **Route action buttons**: "Today" / "This Week" / "Later" — each creates the Task with the right due_at and sets `inbox_items.resolved_at = now()`
- For Event type: collects start_at/end_at via simple inputs and creates `events` row instead
- **Snooze** and **Skip** also available from this view (consistent with list view)
- Keyboard: 1=Task, 2=Event, 3=Discard; T=Today, W=This Week, L=Later; S=Snooze, X=Skip; Enter=Confirm
- After resolving, slide to next item; if queue empty, show "Inbox clear" celebratory state

## Files
- `desktop/src/renderer/pages/Inbox/TriageFocused.tsx`
- `desktop/src/renderer/pages/Inbox/TypeClassifier.tsx`
- `desktop/src/renderer/pages/Inbox/DueDateChips.tsx`
- `desktop/src/main/ipc/triage.ts` — `triage.resolveAsTask`, `triage.resolveAsEvent`, `triage.discard`
- `desktop/src/preload/index.ts` — extend bridge

## Acceptance
- With 3 unresolved items, opening /inbox/triage shows item 1; clicking "Today" creates a task with due_at=today, resolves item 1, advances to item 2
- Choosing "Discard" sets resolved_at without creating a task or event
- Choosing "Event" with start/end times creates a row in `events` and resolves the inbox item
- Keyboard shortcut `T` after typing in title field still routes to Today (shortcuts ignored while focus is in input — verify with E2E)
- After last item resolved, "Inbox clear" view renders with link back to Home
- Unit test: each `triage.resolve*` correctly creates the right entity and resolves the inbox item atomically (single transaction)

## Notes
- "Break it down" inline action lives in CL-BREAKDOWN — surface a placeholder "Break down" button here that CL-BREAKDOWN will wire up.
- AI suggestions for type/title/date/next-action are explicitly out (Epic 7).
- Reminder rule attachment happens in Epic 4; this task creates tasks without reminder_rules rows.

## References
PRD §11 Triage, §7 item 3, §9 Morning.
notes:
LANDED: triage focused mode — IPC + UI + tests all in place.

Store. desktop/src/main/triage/store.ts adds resolveAsTask, resolveAsEvent, discardInboxItem. All three share an atomic transaction: SELECT inbox row → INSERT task/event (skipped for discard) → UPDATE inbox.resolved_at + bump version → enqueue full-snapshot upserts for both rows. The shared loadInboxForResolve helper produces consistent NotFound vs AlreadyResolved discrimination. 10 unit tests cover empty-title rejection, NotFound, AlreadyResolved, full-snapshot enqueue contents, dueAt:null Later branch, end<start rejection on events, source='manual' on event inserts, discard skips entity creation, and InternalError on UPDATE failure.

IPC. desktop/src/main/ipc/triage.ts wires triage:resolveAsTask / triage:resolveAsEvent / triage:discard. Each guards on getCurrentUser; payload-shape validation rejects non-finite numbers and non-string ids before crossing into the store.

Bridge. preload/triage.ts + extended CalmlyApi.triage on api-types.ts surface TriageBridge.{resolveAsTask, resolveAsEvent, discard}. Wired into preload/index.ts.

UI. /inbox/triage replaces the prior stub: TypeClassifier (Task | Event | Discard radio with 1/2/3 keys), editable title field defaulting to raw_text, DueDateChips (Today | Tomorrow | This Week | Later | Pick date) for Task mode, datetime-local inputs for Event mode, primary actions (Today/This Week/Later for Task, Schedule for Event, Discard for Discard), Snooze popover (1h / Tomorrow morning / Next week) and Skip in the secondary group. Break-down placeholder surfaces but is disabled for CL-05. Keyboard model: 1/2/3 type, T/W/L date chip (Task only), S/X snooze/skip, Enter confirm primary; INPUT/TEXTAREA focus exempts shortcuts. Item card slides in via Tailwind animate-in keyframes when the cursor advances. 'Inbox clear' state celebrates with the MountainClimber icon + 'Back to today' button when the queue empties. Reuses InboxBridge.list (refresh after each resolution to slide forward) and InboxBridge.snooze/skip — no new IPC for those.

Date helpers. renderer/pages/Inbox/triageDates.ts (chipToday, chipTomorrow, chipThisWeek with Sat→next-Friday roll, endOfDay) — 7 unit tests including month-boundary crossings.

Verified: typecheck (web + node) clean, eslint clean on touched files, 135 vitest tests passing (was 118 before this bead). Full DB-seeded E2E lives in calmly-exi (CL-04-e2e, P1, depends on this + calmly-ttx for the seed fixture).

title: CL-05: Inline 'break it down' inside Triage (deterministic, no AI)
description:
## Goal
Add an inline "Break it down" action inside the focused Triage view that lets the user split a vague inbox item into a clearer next-action plus optional follow-up subtasks — fully deterministic (no AI), powered by manual user editing.

  - "Also create subtasks" repeating-row list — each row is a free-text input + remove button + "Add row" affordance

  - Creates one parent Task (the next action) with due_at from the chips
  - Creates child Tasks for each non-empty subtask row, with `parent_task_id` set to the parent and `due_at = NULL`
  - Resolves the inbox item with `source='manual-split'` recorded on each created task (use existing `source` field; add `'manual-split'` to the enum)

title: CL-06: Plan view — day grid with manual time blocks + drag/drop reorder
description:
## Goal
Replace the F-06 Plan placeholder with a real day-grid view where users can place tasks into time blocks manually and reorder them via drag/drop. No calendar import yet.

## Scope
- `/plan` route shows a single-day vertical grid (default = today; date picker for ±N days)
- Grid: 6:00 AM → 11:00 PM in 30-min slots (configurable later via settings; hardcode for MVP)
- Two columns inside the grid:
  - **Scheduled column** — placed time blocks (each block = a Task with `scheduled_start`, `scheduled_end`)
  - **Backlog column** — unplaced tasks for the selected day (Tasks with due_at on that day but no scheduled_start)
- Drag a backlog task onto a slot to place it (default 30-min duration)
- Drag a placed block to a different slot to reschedule (snaps to 15-min grid)
- Resize a block by dragging its bottom edge (15-min snap; min 15 min, max 4 h)
- Click a block to open a side panel with title, notes, due_at, scheduled_start/end editing
- Add new fields to `tasks`: `scheduled_start INTEGER NULL`, `scheduled_end INTEGER NULL` (migration `0006_task_schedule.sql`)
- Empty grid + empty backlog states placeholder ("Nothing scheduled today") — full polish in CL-EMPTYSTATES

## Files

- Dragging the block to 10:00 AM moves it; DB updated; refresh preserves the new position
- Resizing a block from 30 to 60 min updates scheduled_end correctly with 15-min snap
- Two blocks cannot occupy the exact same time range — overlap is allowed but visually flagged with a warning border

title: CL-09: Focus mode — current task + next step, soft time, mark done, switch task
description:
## Goal
Replace the F-06 Focus placeholder with a real focus mode UI: shows the current task plus its next step, exposes time as secondary info, supports mark-done, and lets the user switch tasks without leaving Focus.

## Scope
- `/focus` route renders the active focus session (if any); without a session, shows a chooser
- **Active session UI**:
  - Large current task title + parent task chain (if subtask)
  - "Next step" sub-line — for parent tasks, this is the first open child task; for leaf tasks, it's `notes` truncated to one line
  - Soft time visibility: scheduled time shown small + grey ("9:00 – 9:30"); elapsed timer optional and toggleable; no countdown by default
  - Primary action: **Mark done** — closes the task, advances to next scheduled item if any
  - Secondary actions: **Switch task** (opens picker), **I'm stuck** (opens guided prompts — CL-STUCK-PROMPTS), **End focus** (returns to Home)
- **Focus session state** persisted to `focus_sessions` table (new migration `0007_focus_sessions.sql`) — id, user_id, task_id, started_at, ended_at NULL, source ('scheduled'|'ad-hoc')
- **Switch task picker**: list of today's remaining tasks (scheduled + backlog), select one → ends current session, starts new
- Without an active session: Focus screen shows "Start focus" button + list of today's items to pick from (also handles ad-hoc — see CL-FOCUS-ADHOC)

## Files
- `desktop/src/renderer/pages/Focus/Focus.tsx` (replace placeholder)
- `desktop/src/renderer/pages/Focus/ActiveSession.tsx`
- `desktop/src/renderer/pages/Focus/SwitchTaskPicker.tsx`
- `desktop/src/main/db/migrations/0007_focus_sessions.sql`
- `desktop/src/main/ipc/focus.ts` — `focus.start(taskId, source)`, `focus.end()`, `focus.markDone()`, `focus.switch(newTaskId)`, `focus.current()`
- `desktop/src/preload/index.ts` — extend bridge
- `shared/src/model/focus.ts` — new file with FocusSession schema

## Acceptance
- Starting focus on a parent task with 2 open children renders title=parent, next-step=first child
- Mark done closes the active task (status='done') AND ends the focus session (`ended_at = now()`)
- Switch task ends current session, starts new one with a fresh started_at
- Reloading the app while a session is active resumes the same session
- Time display: scheduled time visible but small/grey; no countdown; toggle reveals elapsed timer
- E2E test: start focus, mark done, assert task status + session ended

## Notes
- "I'm stuck" prompts live in CL-STUCK-PROMPTS — surface a placeholder button here that CL-STUCK-PROMPTS will wire up.
- Ad-hoc focus blocks are CL-FOCUS-ADHOC; this task's "Start focus" picker shows only today's planned tasks.
- AI rescue suggestions are Epic 7/8.
- Notification suppression during focus (do not disturb) is Epic 4 (reminders).

## References
PRD §11 Focus, §7 item 5, §9 During the day.
notes:
LANDED CL-09a: schema + IPC for focus mode.

Schema. Desktop migration 0008_focus_sessions.sql creates a STRICT TABLE with id/user_id/task_id/started_at/ended_at/source. LOCAL ONLY — no server migration, no entry in syncTables. Side effects that DO sync (task.status='done' on markDone) flow through the regular tasks-upsert path with full-row snapshots. Two indices: partial open-sessions index for currentFocus's lookup; non-partial task_id index for cascading-delete affinity.

Shared. shared/src/model/focus.ts: FocusSourceSchema ('scheduled'|'ad-hoc') + FocusSessionSchema with end>=start refine. Re-exported from shared/src/model/index.ts.

Store. main/focus/store.ts:
- currentFocus(db, userId): single-row read of the open session.
- startFocus(db, userId, taskId, source, now): rejects unknown sources via InvalidArgs; rejects missing/non-schedulable tasks as NotFound; auto-ends prior open sessions in the same tx before INSERTing the new one.
- endFocus(db, userId, now): idempotent — returns ended:false when nothing was open.
- markDoneFromFocus(db, userId, now): in one tx — find open session, load task, UPDATE tasks.status='done' + version bump, enqueue full-snapshot tasks upsert, end the session. Returns NoActiveSession / NotFound / ok with the closed task's id.
- switchFocus(db, userId, newTaskId, source, now): end+start in one tx so the renderer never sees a 'no session' window.

13 unit tests cover currentFocus null/non-null, start with bad source / missing task / non-schedulable status / ends-prior-then-INSERTs ordering, end ended:false vs true, markDoneFromFocus NoActiveSession + happy-path with status flip + full-snapshot enqueue + session close, switchFocus bad source / missing task / ends-prior-then-INSERTs ordering.

IPC. window.calmly.focus.{current, start, end, markDone, switch} via main/ipc/focus.ts. Each guarded on getCurrentUser; payload-shape rejects bogus sources/ids before crossing into the store.

title: CAL-04d: Calendar import worker — orchestration, queue, periodic + on-demand IPC, integration tests

description:

ADD COLUMN external_ref TEXT NULL. SQLite STRICT permits a nullable TEXT add with no default. The existing source CHECK already allows 'manual-split' (added in calmly-u0u.13), so no rebuild needed for that.

ADD COLUMN external_ref text NULL. Drop + recreate inbox_items_source_check to include 'manual-split' alongside the existing four sources. Add a partial UNIQUE INDEX (user_id, external_ref) WHERE external_ref IS NOT NULL — null external_refs are the desktop path and shouldn't conflict, but two messages with the same (user_id, external_ref) MUST collide so the bot's idempotent retry path can detect a duplicate.

title: TG-03b: Telegram inbound text handler + server inbox writer + dispatcher routing + tests
description:
## Goal
Implement TG-03's runtime layer on top of TG-03a's schema foundation: when a linked Telegram user sends plain text to the bot, create an inbox_item with source='telegram-text' and ack the message. Idempotent against Telegram retry replays via inbox_items.external_ref UNIQUE.

## Scope

### Server inbox writer (`server/src/inbox/createFromTelegram.ts` or similar)
Pure pg.Pool consumer:
- captureFromTelegram(pool, { chatId, telegramMessageId, rawText, now }) -> { ok: true, inboxId, truncated, alreadyProcessed: boolean } | { ok: false, error: 'unlinked' }
- Resolves user_id from chat_id via telegram_links (JOIN, not separate query).
- external_ref = `tg:${chatId}:${telegramMessageId}`.
- ON CONFLICT (user_id, external_ref) DO UPDATE … RETURNING with a discriminator so the caller can detect 'alreadyProcessed' and reply with the original ack.
- Truncates raw_text to 4000 chars; sets a flag on the result.
- Emits version=1 + updated_at + deleted_at=NULL so sync replicates correctly.

### Bot text handler (`server/src/telegram/handlers/text.ts`)
- Filter: ignore messages whose text starts with '/' (those are slash commands handled by other beads).
- Resolve user via captureFromTelegram.
  - unlinked: reply with 'Link your account in Settings → Telegram first.' (or similar).
  - linked: reply 'Saved to inbox.' (terse per ADHD principle); if truncated, append '(trimmed at 4000 chars)'.
- Photos / files / stickers: out of scope — reply 'I only handle text and voice notes for now.'

### Dispatcher routing (`server/src/telegram/dispatcher.ts`)
Add a 'text' branch routing to the new handler. Keep the /start path that TG-02b added intact — opus's branch may not yet have it, but the merge-loop will compose them (the handlers don't share state).

### Tests (`server/src/telegram/handlers/__tests__/text.test.ts` + `server/src/inbox/__tests__/createFromTelegram.test.ts`)
Mock pg.Pool. Cover:
- Linked happy path → row inserted, ack replied
- Unlinked chat_id → no row, link-prompt reply
- Idempotent replay → second call returns alreadyProcessed:true, no duplicate row
- Slash command bypass → not treated as text capture
- Truncation → 5000-char input clipped to 4000, ack notes the trim

## Acceptance (per parent calmly-d0p.3)
- Linked user sending 'buy milk' creates one inbox_item row with source='telegram-text' and gets ack
- Re-sending the same message_id does NOT create a duplicate
- Unlinked chat_id receives the link-prompt; no inbox row created
- Slash commands are NOT treated as text capture

## Depends on
- TG-03a (schema foundation)
notes: AUDIT 2026-07-07: closed by the 2026-05 autonomous-loop state sync but the code never landed on any origin branch (lost unpushed worker session; post-crash context: calmly-3py). Scope re-filed as calmly-13d.1 — do not reopen this bead.

title: BUG: migration version-number collisions — workers don't coordinate migration numbering
description:
## Symptom
`desktop/src/main/db/migrations/` has 5 pairs of files with duplicate version numbers (0010, 0016, 0017, 0018, 0019). The migration runner uses INTEGER PRIMARY KEY on the version column, so the second migration with the same number trips the UNIQUE constraint when applied: `SqliteError: UNIQUE constraint failed: _meta_migrations.version`. The app cannot boot.

## Why this happened
Both ralph workers picked the next sequential number independently (e.g., opus did calmly-3py.4 and added 0010_drop_user_magic_link_cols; sonnet did its own work and added 0010_stuck_sessions). Neither worker rebased before numbering, so they collided.

## Tests didn't catch it
Per-worker migration tests ran against fresh DBs containing only that worker's migrations. The collision only manifests post-merge when ALL migrations are present together.

## Structural fix needed
1. Add a CI step / integration test that runs full migration sweep on a fresh DB. Fail builds if any version collides.
2. Update worker prompts: `bd create` for any new migration must include the next-available version number AS PART of the bead spec, with a check that no other in-flight bead has claimed it.
3. Long-term: switch from sequential ints to timestamp-based or hash-based migration ids that can't collide.

## Immediate workaround applied 2026-05-02
Renamed the alphabetically-second file in each colliding pair to the next free number (0020-0024). Local SQLite DB cleared so renumbered migrations apply fresh.
close_reason: Structural fix landed: migration-versions.test.ts (duplicate/gap scan) + migration-sweep.test.ts (real runMigrations() on fresh node:sqlite DB) + migration-sweep CI job in ci.yml (pinned Node 22, fails loudly if node:sqlite missing) + numbering policy in .ralph/AGENT.md. Verified locally: injected duplicate 0010 reproduces the boot-breaking UNIQUE constraint failure in both suites. (c6856ff + dcd40f8)

title: F-14d: E2E persistence.spec.ts — sign in → quit → relaunch → still signed in (encrypted store survives)
description:
## Goal
Prove the encrypted session store survives an Electron restart.

## Scope
- desktop/e2e/foundations/persistence.spec.ts.
- Steps: sign in via F-14c helper → assert signed-in → app.close() → relaunch with the SAME --user-data-dir → assert signed-in again on cold boot (no re-auth).
- Cookie jar is persisted by Electron's session.defaultSession when user-data-dir is reused; this test guards that we don't accidentally clear it.

## Acceptance
- Spec passes; cleanup tears down the user-data-dir after both runs.

## Depends on
F-14a, F-14c
notes:
DESIGN: spec at desktop/e2e/foundations/persistence.spec.ts. Approach: server fixture beforeAll → tmp userDataDir created via mkdtemp → launchElectronApp({syncUrl, userDataDir}) → signInAsTestUser → dispose (leaves userDataDir intact since helper only deletes ones it created itself, by design) → second launchElectronApp with SAME userDataDir → on cold boot the renderer asks /auth/me with the persisted cookie → AuthProvider sees signed_in immediately → AuthGate skips SignIn and renders Home directly. Assert: 'Peace, friend.' visible without re-signing AND auth.status() returns the same user.email. Self-skip without Docker (mirrors auth.spec.ts).

NOT doing: the encrypted secret-store roundtrip across restart (separate concern; safeStorage is exercised by Home's main process selfTest at boot already and there's no F-14 child for that). Just session-cookie persistence.
close_reason: Landed in 5a4530e. Spec passes in 4.3-4.9s for the full restart flow (~14.8s incl. testcontainer boot). Watchdog races Home assertion vs. SignIn-visible to fail fast on regression. Self-skips without Docker.

title: v1.0 Desktop Release: packaging, signing, auto-update, distribution pipeline
description:
## Goal
Ship Calmly v1.0 as an installable, signed, auto-updating desktop app on Windows, macOS, and Linux, with a tag-driven CI release pipeline. The MVP feature set (PRD §23 steps 1–10) is code-complete; this epic closes the gap between "runs from `pnpm dev`" and "a user can download, install, sign in, and receive updates."

## Why now
- `desktop/package.json` is version 0.0.0 with **no packager configured** — no electron-builder/forge, no installers, no auto-update, no code signing anywhere in the repo.
- `.github/workflows/release.yml` only releases the **sync server** (OSS-06). There is no desktop release path.
- Two open bugs block a credible release and are linked as blockers of this epic:
  - calmly-wv9 — migration numbering has no CI gate; a packaged app that ships colliding migrations bricks user DBs on upgrade.
  - calmly-fs7 — the magic-link email doesn't hand off to the `calmly://` protocol handler, so install → sign-in is broken outside dev-stub auth.

## Scope (children)
- REL-01 electron-builder baseline + Linux AppImage/deb
- REL-02 app icons + product identity
- REL-03 Windows NSIS target + `calmly://` protocol registration
- REL-04 macOS DMG/ZIP target + entitlements
- REL-05 code signing + notarization wiring
- REL-06 auto-update service (main process, electron-updater)
- REL-07 auto-update Settings UI
- REL-08 desktop release CI workflow (`desktop-v*` tags)
- REL-09 packaged-build smoke E2E
- REL-10 production build audit (dev-only affordances, endpoint config)
- REL-11 CHANGELOG + release-notes tooling

## Out of scope
- App-store distribution (Mac App Store, Microsoft Store, Snap/Flatpak stores)
- Delta/differential updates
- Pay-once license-key issuance/enforcement (PRD §19) — separate epic; v1.0 installers are unmetered
- Sync-server deployment changes (covered by OSS-06 pipeline)
- Native mobile anything (PRD §8)

## Done when
Pushing a `desktop-v1.0.0` tag produces a GitHub Release with installers for all three OSes plus SHA256 checksums; installing on a clean machine takes a user from download → magic-link sign-in → core capture/triage/plan loop; and a subsequent `desktop-v1.0.1` tag is surfaced in-app via the Updates UI and installs cleanly with the user's local DB intact.

## References
PRD §19 (pay-once packaging), §21 (success criteria), §26 (tensions carried forward). GUI_draft.ts for any UI surface. Existing sync-server release pipeline in .github/workflows/release.yml is the style reference for CI work.

title: REL-01: electron-builder baseline — packager config + Linux AppImage/deb
description:
## Goal
Stand up electron-builder as the packager for @calmly/desktop and produce working Linux artifacts (AppImage + deb). This is the foundation bead: Windows (REL-03), macOS (REL-04), auto-update (REL-06), and the CI pipeline (REL-08) all build on the config landed here. Linux goes first because it's verifiable in CI containers and on the dev box without signing infrastructure.

## Context
- The desktop app builds with electron-vite (`desktop/electron.vite.config.ts`) into `desktop/out/` (main/preload/renderer). There is currently NO packager: `pnpm --filter @calmly/desktop build` stops at `out/`, nothing produces an installable artifact.
- `better-sqlite3` 11.5.0 is a native module rebuilt via @electron/rebuild (see `postinstall` in desktop/package.json). It must be unpacked from asar and rebuilt against the Electron 32 ABI in the packaged app.
- This is a pnpm workspace; `@calmly/shared` is `workspace:*` and gets bundled by electron-vite, so the packaged app only needs runtime node_modules for native deps.

## Scope
- Add `electron-builder` (pin latest 25.x) to desktop devDependencies.
- Create `desktop/electron-builder.yml`:
  - `appId: com.calmly.app`, `productName: Calmly`
  - `directories: { output: release, buildResources: build }`
  - `files`: `out/**`, `package.json` (exclude sources, tests, e2e)
  - `asar: true`, `asarUnpack: "**/*.node"`
  - `npmRebuild: true` so better-sqlite3 is rebuilt for the packaged Electron; if this fights the existing electron-rebuild postinstall, document the resolution in the config comments
  - `linux: { target: [AppImage, deb], category: Utility, maintainer: ... }`
  - `protocols: [{ name: Calmly, schemes: [calmly] }]` (registration groundwork; Win/mac verification is REL-03/04)
- Add scripts to desktop/package.json: `dist` (`electron-vite build && electron-builder`), `dist:linux` (`... --linux`). Root package.json convenience script optional.
- Add `desktop/release/` to .gitignore.
- Create `desktop/build/` with a placeholder `icon.png` (512×512 minimum; REL-02 replaces it with real identity).

## Acceptance
- `pnpm --filter @calmly/desktop dist:linux` succeeds from a clean checkout and produces `desktop/release/Calmly-*.AppImage` and `.deb`.
- `xvfb-run ./release/linux-unpacked/calmly --no-sandbox` boots to the real sign-in screen (CALMLY_DEV_AUTH stub must NOT activate — it is gated on `!app.isPackaged`) and creates its SQLite DB with a full clean migration sweep in the packaged userData dir. Verify by log inspection (electron-log) and clean exit.
- better-sqlite3 loads in the packaged app (no `NODE_MODULE_VERSION` mismatch — this is the failure mode to test for).
- `pnpm typecheck` and existing vitest suites still pass (this bead should not touch src/, but the guard stands).

## Out of scope
- Windows/macOS targets (REL-03/REL-04), signing (REL-05), publish/update config beyond the protocols stanza (REL-06), icons (REL-02), CI (REL-08).

## Skills
`run` to launch and verify the packaged binary. If the packaged boot check needs automation now rather than in REL-09, `playwright-electron-debugger`.

## Notes
Known pnpm+electron-builder friction: hoisting can break electron-builder's dependency collection. If `npmRebuild` misbehaves under pnpm, prefer `electron-builder install-app-deps` in a `beforeBuild` hook or set `nodeGypRebuild: false` + explicit rebuild step, and record the decision in electron-builder.yml comments.
close_reason: electron-builder 25.1.8 + electron-builder.yml (appId com.calmly.app, asarUnpack *.node, Linux AppImage/deb, calmly:// protocol stanza), dist scripts, build/ placeholder icon. electron-vite build green; AppImage build+boot verified via desktop-release.yml CI. (f74444f)

title: REL-02: App icons + product identity (icon set, version surfacing, desktop entry)
description:
## Goal
Give the packaged app a real product identity: icon set, product naming, and version surfacing. Until this lands the installers built by REL-01/03/04 ship the default Electron icon, which reads as untrustworthy in a paid product.

## Scope
- Design a simple, calm app icon consistent with the established visual language (GUI_draft.ts): stone/warm-gray surface, emerald accent, soft rounded shape language (`rounded-[2.5rem]` feel), possibly derived from the MountainClimberIcon SVG already in GUI_draft.ts. No text in the icon.
- Produce `desktop/build/icon.png` (1024×1024 master), `icon.icns` (macOS), `icon.ico` (Windows, 256/128/64/48/32/16). Generate .icns/.ico from the master with a script (`desktop/scripts/generate-icons.mjs` using sharp or png2icons) committed alongside, so the master is the single source of truth — do not hand-maintain three binaries.
- Wire electron-builder `icon` fields for each platform in electron-builder.yml.
- Version surfacing: Settings → Account (or About section) shows `app.getVersion()` via an existing or new tiny IPC read; window title stays "Calmly" (no version in title bar — calm principle).

## Acceptance
- Packaged Linux build shows the new icon in the window/taskbar (verify via linux-unpacked run); .icns and .ico exist and are generated (not hand-edited) — regenerating from the master is byte-stable or documented as non-deterministic.
- Settings displays the app version matching package.json.
- RTL test for the version display component state (mock the IPC).

## Out of scope
- Marketing site assets, DMG background art (nice-to-have in REL-04 if trivial), notarization stapling.

## Skills
`frontend-design` — load GUI_draft.ts first per CLAUDE.md so the icon and About/version surface match the established stone+emerald language.
close_reason: Master SVG icon (stone/emerald, MountainClimber-derived) + generate-icons.mjs (sharp+png2icons) producing committed icon.png/.icns/.ico; electron-builder icon wiring; Settings shows app.getVersion() via IPC with RTL test; Linux desktop-entry config. (58d2bd6)

title: REL-03: Windows NSIS installer + calmly:// protocol registration + second-instance deep links
description:
## Goal
Windows installer: NSIS one-click, per-user install that registers the `calmly://` protocol so magic-link sign-in works on a machine where the app was installed normally (not run from a dev checkout).

## Context
- Deep-link plumbing exists (`desktop/src/main/auth/deeplink-install.ts` — see calmly-fs7 for the flow). On Windows, packaged protocol registration happens through the installer, and a second app launch delivers the URL via the `second-instance` event on the single-instance lock.
- ADHD-first posture: installation must be zero-decision. One-click, per-user (no UAC elevation), launch after finish.

## Scope
- electron-builder.yml `win` section: `target: nsis`, `nsis: { oneClick: true, perMachine: false, runAfterFinish: true, deleteAppDataOnUninstall: false }` (never delete user task data on uninstall).
- Confirm `protocols` stanza (REL-01) yields HKCU `calmly` URL-protocol registration in the NSIS installer; add explicit NSIS include only if the default doesn't.
- Verify/complete main-process handling for packaged Windows deep links:
  - single-instance lock is requested (`app.requestSingleInstanceLock()`), second-instance argv is parsed for `calmly://` URLs and routed to the same handler the dev flow uses;
  - cold-start argv (app launched BY the protocol) is also parsed on ready.
  - If any of this is missing in deeplink-install.ts, implement it here with unit tests for the argv→URL parser (mixed argv with flags, no URL, multiple URLs → first wins).
- Document a manual Windows verification checklist in docs/RELEASING.md (install, click magic link in browser, app foregrounds and signs in) — full automation of OS-level protocol dispatch is not practical in CI.

## Acceptance
- CI (windows-latest runner, wired properly in REL-08; for this bead a manual/dispatch workflow run is fine) builds `Calmly-Setup-*.exe`.
- Unit tests: argv deep-link parser covers cold-start and second-instance shapes; existing suites stay green.
- `pnpm typecheck` passes.
- docs/RELEASING.md gains the Windows manual-verify checklist (create the file if REL-05 hasn't yet).

## Out of scope
- Authenticode signing (REL-05), auto-update (REL-06), MSI/winget.

## Skills
None specific; `playwright-electron-debugger` if you end up debugging main-process second-instance behavior.
close_reason: NSIS one-click per-user config (deleteAppDataOnUninstall false), protocols registration, argv deep-link parser (cold-start + second-instance) with unit tests, Windows manual-verify checklist in docs/RELEASING.md. Installer build verified on windows-latest via desktop-release.yml. (0b39001)

title: REL-04: macOS DMG/ZIP target, hardened-runtime entitlements, open-url deep links
description:
## Goal
macOS packaging: DMG for humans + ZIP for the auto-updater, with hardened-runtime entitlements ready for signing (REL-05), and `calmly://` deep links working via the macOS `open-url` event.

## Context
- macOS delivers protocol URLs through `app.on('open-url')` — NOT `second-instance` argv like Windows/Linux. If `deeplink-install.ts` only handles argv, sign-in is silently broken on macOS. This is the highest-risk item in this bead: verify and fix.
- electron-updater requires a ZIP target on macOS in addition to DMG.
- Unsigned local builds are acceptable here; signing/notarization is REL-05.

## Scope
- electron-builder.yml `mac` section: `target: [dmg, zip]`, `category: public.app-category.productivity`, `hardenedRuntime: true`, `gatekeeperAssess: false`, `entitlements: build/entitlements.mac.plist`, `entitlementsInherit` same file.
- `desktop/build/entitlements.mac.plist`: `com.apple.security.cs.allow-jit`, `com.apple.security.cs.allow-unsigned-executable-memory` (Electron requirement), `com.apple.security.network.client`. Nothing broader — no mic/camera/location; document each entry with a plist comment.
- `CFBundleURLTypes` for `calmly` comes from the `protocols` stanza — verify it lands in the built Info.plist.
- `open-url` handling: register `app.on('open-url')` (both before-ready buffering and post-ready dispatch) routing into the same deep-link handler as other platforms. Unit-test the buffering logic (URL arrives before window exists → held and delivered after ready).
- DMG layout: default is fine; custom background art is optional polish, don't burn time.

## Acceptance
- `pnpm --filter @calmly/desktop dist -- --mac` on a macOS machine/runner produces `Calmly-*.dmg` and `Calmly-*-mac.zip` (unsigned).
- Built Info.plist contains CFBundleURLSchemes=[calmly] (assert with a small script or documented `plutil` check in docs/RELEASING.md).
- Unit tests for open-url buffering/dispatch pass on all platforms (pure logic, mocked `app`).
- `pnpm typecheck` and existing suites green.

## Out of scope
- Signing/notarization/stapling (REL-05), Mac App Store target, universal (arm64+x64 single-file) binaries — build per-arch, decide universal later.

## Skills
`playwright-electron-debugger` for main-process event debugging if needed.
close_reason: mac dmg+zip targets, hardened runtime + documented entitlements plist, CFBundleURLTypes via protocols stanza, open-url pre-ready buffering with unit tests, macOS manual checklist in docs/RELEASING.md. Build verified on macos-latest via desktop-release.yml. (d7bda53)

title: REL-05: Code signing + notarization wiring (macOS Developer ID, Windows Authenticode, graceful skip)
description:
## Goal
Wire code signing and notarization into the build so tagged releases produce artifacts that install without OS scare-screens: Developer ID + notarization on macOS, Authenticode on Windows. Everything must degrade gracefully — a contributor or CI run WITHOUT secrets still builds unsigned artifacts.

## Context
Unsigned apps are effectively broken for end users: macOS Gatekeeper blocks un-notarized apps outright on current macOS; Windows SmartScreen warns on unsigned NSIS installers. For a pay-once product (PRD §19) this is a launch blocker.

## Scope
- macOS: electron-builder signing via env (`CSC_LINK` base64 .p12 + `CSC_KEY_PASSWORD`); notarization via electron-builder `notarize: true` with `APPLE_ID`, `APPLE_APP_SPECIFIC_PASSWORD`, `APPLE_TEAM_ID` env. Hardened runtime + entitlements come from REL-04.
- Windows: Authenticode via `CSC_LINK`/`CSC_KEY_PASSWORD` (or `win.signtoolOptions` if using Azure Trusted Signing — pick based on what cert the project can actually obtain; document BOTH paths and mark the chosen one).
- Graceful-skip: builds must not fail when secrets are absent. Detect in CI (REL-08 wires the actual secrets) and log clearly "UNSIGNED build — signing secrets not configured".
- Create/extend `docs/RELEASING.md`: exact secret names, how to produce/renew each credential (Developer ID cert, app-specific password, Authenticode cert), how to verify (`codesign -dv --verbose`, `spctl -a -t exec`, `xcrun stapler validate`, `Get-AuthenticodeSignature`), and the unsigned-build fallback story.
- Verification hooks: an afterSign/afterAllArtifactBuild script that runs the codesign/notarization checks when signing was active, so a half-signed release can't slip out silently.

## Acceptance
- With dummy/absent secrets: `dist:linux` (and mac/win where runnable) completes, clearly logging unsigned status.
- With real secrets configured in repo settings (owner action — file a checklist item in the bead notes if secrets aren't available yet, do NOT block the code landing): macOS artifact passes `spctl -a` and stapler validation in the mac CI job; Windows artifact has a valid Authenticode signature.
- docs/RELEASING.md covers full credential lifecycle; no secret VALUES anywhere in the repo.
- CI changes lint clean (actionlint if configured; otherwise workflow parses and a dispatch dry-run succeeds).

## Out of scope
- Obtaining the certificates themselves (owner/business task — surface it loudly in the bead close notes if pending), Linux artifact signing (checksums from REL-08 cover integrity), cosign/SLSA provenance (the sync-server release.yml notes it as future too).

## Skills
`security-review` before landing — this bead touches credential handling in CI.
close_reason: Env-driven signing/notarization wiring (CSC_LINK/CSC_KEY_PASSWORD, APPLE_ID/APPLE_APP_SPECIFIC_PASSWORD/APPLE_TEAM_ID), graceful UNSIGNED-build skip with loud logging, afterSign/afterAllArtifactBuild verification hooks, full credential lifecycle in docs/RELEASING.md. Real signing blocked on owner obtaining certs (follow-up bead filed). (593ee76)

title: REL-06: Auto-update service — electron-updater state machine + IPC surface (main process)
description:
## Goal
Auto-update service in the main process using electron-updater against GitHub Releases: the app learns about new versions, downloads on user consent, and installs on restart. Calm posture — no modal interruptions, no auto-restart, ever.

## Context
- PRD §4 principles (calm, low cognitive load) rule out nag dialogs. Update UX is: quiet availability signal → user-initiated download → "restart when you're ready".
- REL-01 landed the packager; artifacts publish to GitHub Releases via REL-08. electron-updater consumes the `latest*.yml` feed electron-builder generates — macOS requires the ZIP target (REL-04).

## Scope
- Add `electron-updater` to desktop dependencies; add `publish: { provider: github, owner: stevensewell83, repo: calmly }` to electron-builder.yml.
- `desktop/src/main/updates/updateService.ts`:
  - state machine: `idle | checking | update-available | downloading | ready | error | disabled` with a typed snapshot (version, progress %, error code);
  - `autoDownload = false`, `autoInstallOnAppQuit = true`;
  - check on app ready (delayed ~30s so startup stays fast) and every 6h; manual `check()`;
  - entirely inert when `!app.isPackaged` (state = disabled) or when the platform build is unsigned-mac (updater will fail — surface as a distinct error, not a crash);
  - all failures (offline, GitHub 4xx/5xx, corrupt download) land in `error` state with a machine-readable code; NEVER a dialog from the main process; log via electron-log.
- IPC surface following the existing normalized-procedure pattern in `desktop/src/main/ipc/` (mirror how ai/settings handlers are registered): `updates.getStatus`, `updates.check`, `updates.download`, `updates.quitAndInstall`, plus a push channel for status changes. Types added to `desktop/src/preload/api-types.ts` using shared types per house rule (no inline string unions — see REFACTOR-AUDIT-2 precedent).

## Tests
- Unit-test the state machine against a mocked autoUpdater EventEmitter: every transition (checking→available→downloading(progress)→ready; checking→idle on no-update; each error path), the 6h re-check scheduling (fake timers), and the isPackaged gate. Target ≥ 15 tests, `updateService.ts` < 250 LOC.
- IPC handler tests in the style of `src/main/ipc/__tests__/aiSettings.test.ts`.

## Acceptance
- `pnpm typecheck` green; new suites pass; no behavior change when unpackaged (dev boots exactly as before).
- End-to-end update path is exercised for real in REL-08's post-release verification (v1.0.0 → v1.0.1 documented dry run) — not required to close this bead, but the service must log every step clearly enough that that run is debuggable.

## Out of scope
- The Settings/renderer UI (REL-07), delta updates, staged rollouts, downgrade protection beyond electron-updater defaults.

## Skills
None specific.
close_reason: updates/updateService.ts state machine (idle/checking/available/downloading/ready/error/disabled; autoDownload=false, autoInstallOnAppQuit, 30s-delayed first check + 6h interval, isPackaged gate) + normalized IPC surface + preload types from @calmly/shared. Mocked-autoUpdater suite covers all transitions. (20d837d)

title: REL-07: Auto-update Settings UI — quiet states, no-nag restart flow
description:
## Goal
Renderer surface for updates: a quiet Updates section in Settings plus a subtle "update ready" affordance, driven by the REL-06 IPC surface. Anti-nag by design.

## Context
REL-06 exposes `updates.getStatus/check/download/quitAndInstall` + a status push channel via `window.calmly.updates`. Design language: GUI_draft.ts (stone surfaces, emerald accents, soft rounded cards). PRD §4: calm, anti-shame, progressive disclosure — an update must never interrupt a Focus session or triage flow.

## Scope
- Settings → new "Updates" card (or extend About/Account section — match whichever exists after REL-02):
  - current version;
  - state-driven row: Up to date / "Check for updates" button / "Version X available — Download" / progress bar (downloading) / "Restart to update" / inline error with retry (human copy per PRD §13: what happened, what they can do, nothing is lost);
  - "Check automatically" is always-on v1 — no toggle unless trivial; do not add settings surface area.
- Global affordance: when state = ready, show a small emerald dot/pill on the Settings nav item (sidebar) — NO toast, NO modal, NO banner over content. Never render during an active Focus session view.
- All states driven by subscription to the push channel with getStatus() hydration on mount.

## Tests
- RTL component tests: one per state (disabled/dev, idle, checking, available, downloading w/ progress, ready, error+retry), mocked `window.calmly.updates`; assert the Focus-view suppression rule for the nav affordance.

## Acceptance
- `pnpm typecheck` green, RTL suite passes (≥ 8 tests), lint clean.
- In dev (state=disabled) the card shows version + "Updates are managed by the packaged app" style copy — not an error.

## Out of scope
- Release-notes rendering in-app (link to the GitHub release instead), update channels (beta/stable).

## Skills
`frontend-design` — invoke AFTER loading GUI_draft.ts, per CLAUDE.md.
close_reason: Settings Updates card (all 7 states incl. dev-disabled copy, PRD §13 error copy) + emerald ready-pill on sidebar Settings item, suppressed during Focus view; no toasts/modals. RTL tests per state + suppression rule. (184fd75)

title: REL-09: Packaged-build smoke E2E — boot, migration sweep, native module, persistence
description:
## Goal
A packaged-build smoke suite that proves the artifact users actually download boots, migrates, signs in, and persists — catching the class of bug that dev-mode E2E structurally cannot (asar paths, native-module ABI, isPackaged gates, packaged userData location).

## Context
- Existing E2E (desktop/e2e/, Playwright `_electron`) launches via electron-vite output with dev conveniences. calmly-wv9 is the cautionary tale: per-worker tests passed while the assembled app couldn't boot. The packaged artifact is a different program; test THAT.
- Playwright can't launch an AppImage directly — point `_electron.launch({ executablePath })` at `desktop/release/linux-unpacked/calmly` (the same binary the AppImage wraps). CI needs xvfb + `--no-sandbox`.

## Scope
- `desktop/e2e/packaged/` suite + separate Playwright project/config (`playwright.packaged.config.ts`) so it never runs in the default `test:e2e` (it requires a prior `dist:linux`):
  1. **boot**: fresh temp userData dir → app reaches the REAL sign-in screen (asserts CALMLY_DEV_AUTH stub is dead in packaged builds — regression guard for the REL-10 audit);
  2. **migrations**: after boot, the SQLite DB in the temp userData contains the full migration sweep with no gaps/collisions (query `_meta_migrations` directly with better-sqlite3 from the test runner); this is the packaged-side enforcement of calmly-wv9;
  3. **native module**: DB write path works (the sign-in screen rendering already exercises read; add a main-process log assertion or lightweight probe);
  4. **persistence**: relaunch with the same userData dir → still past first-run (window-state/store survive);
  5. **version**: `app.getVersion()` (via Playwright evaluate in main) matches desktop/package.json.
- `test:e2e:packaged` script; wire into REL-08's Linux release job. Also add it to ci.yml as a nightly or main-branch-only job if runtime cost allows (< ~5 min) — decide and note.

## Acceptance
- `pnpm --filter @calmly/desktop dist:linux && pnpm --filter @calmly/desktop test:e2e:packaged` green locally (container: xvfb-run, --no-sandbox) and in CI.
- Suite is hermetic: unique temp userData per test, no leakage between specs, artifacts (screenshots, main-process logs) uploaded on failure.

## Out of scope
- Packaged smoke on Windows/macOS runners (manual checklist in docs/RELEASING.md covers those until there's signal it's worth automating), full user-journey E2E (covered by existing dev-mode suites).

## Skills
`playwright-electron-debugger` — mandatory here; launching packaged Electron under Playwright has sharp edges (sandbox flags, userData override, main-process log capture).

title: REL-10: Production build audit — dev affordances dead, endpoint config, crash-report gating
description:
## Goal
Audit and harden the packaged build: every dev-only affordance provably dead, production endpoints configured at build time, crash reporting pointed somewhere real. The output is both fixes and a written config matrix.

## Context
Dev affordances found in `desktop/src/main/index.ts` today: `CALMLY_DEV_AUTH=stub` (gated `!app.isPackaged`), `LOG_PII` (gated `!app.isPackaged`), `crashReporter.start(...)` (check its submitURL — likely dev/no-op), devtools behavior. The sync-server URL the packaged app talks to must be baked for production while remaining overridable for self-hosters (docs/SELF_HOSTING.md audience, PRD §19).

## Scope
- Sweep ALL `app.isPackaged` / `isDev` / `process.env` reads across desktop/src (main + preload + renderer via import.meta.env). Produce a table in `docs/RELEASING.md` (or docs/BUILD_CONFIG.md): variable → effect → dev default → packaged behavior → override story.
- Production endpoint config: build-time define (electron-vite `define` or env at build) for the hosted sync server base URL; packaged default = production URL; explicit user-facing override for self-hosters (Settings → Account server URL if it exists, else env var documented in SELF_HOSTING.md — do not invent new UI without checking what exists).
- crashReporter: set a real (or explicitly parked-with-TODO-and-bead) submitURL strategy; MUST remain opt-in per PRD §18 (Privacy settings toggle from POL-03 governs it); verify the toggle actually gates upload, not just collection, and add a unit test.
- Add regression tests: stub-auth module refuses to activate when `app.isPackaged` is mocked true (unit level; REL-09 asserts it end-to-end); PII logging off in packaged.
- Fix anything the sweep finds that leaks dev behavior into packaged builds; file separate bugs for anything too large for this bead.

## Acceptance
- Config matrix documented; every env var / define accounted for.
- New unit tests green; `pnpm typecheck` green; existing suites green.
- REL-09's packaged boot spec still passes (it consumes this bead's guarantees).

## Out of scope
- Building the crash-ingestion backend (park behind a documented endpoint decision + follow-up bead if needed), CSP/renderer-hardening overhaul (file separately if the sweep finds gaps).

## Skills
`security-review` — this is exactly its shape: auth stubs, PII gates, endpoint config on pending changes.
close_reason: Dev-affordance sweep with config matrix in docs (CALMLY_DEV_AUTH/LOG_PII/devtools all !isPackaged-gated, regression unit tests), build-time prod sync URL define with self-host override documented, crashReporter opt-in gating verified with test; CALMLY_CRASH_INGEST_URL parked behind follow-up bead. (24d33d1)

title: REL-11: CHANGELOG (Keep-a-Changelog) + release-notes extraction script
description:
## Goal
Make release notes a mechanical byproduct of development: a Keep-a-Changelog CHANGELOG.md for the desktop app plus a script that extracts one version's section for the GitHub Release body (consumed by REL-08).

## Context
- `.github/workflows/changelog-lint.yml` already exists — READ IT FIRST and conform to whatever convention it enforces rather than inventing a parallel one. If it lints a different changelog (e.g. the sync server's), extend the same convention to the desktop app.
- Tag scheme: `desktop-v<semver>` (REL-08). The changelog is the human-readable record; the tag is the machine trigger.

## Scope
- `CHANGELOG.md` (location per existing lint convention; likely repo root with sections, or desktop/CHANGELOG.md — match the linter): `## [1.0.0] - YYYY-MM-DD` sections with Added/Changed/Fixed/Removed subsections; backfill an honest `[1.0.0] - Unreleased` section summarizing the MVP surface (PRD §7 is the checklist — capture, triage, plan, focus, review, reminders, Telegram, calendar import, search, AI, settings).
- `scripts/release-notes.mjs` (root scripts/ dir already exists): given a version, print that section's body to stdout; exit non-zero with a clear message if the section is missing or still `Unreleased` — this is the guard that stops REL-08 from tagging without notes. Node-only, no deps.
- Unit tests for the extractor (vitest at root or desktop, wherever scripts are tested today — check; if scripts/ has no test harness, a minimal one is in scope): section found, missing version, Unreleased guard, last-section-in-file boundary.
- Update changelog-lint.yml if needed so the desktop changelog is linted on PRs touching desktop/.

## Acceptance
- `node scripts/release-notes.mjs 1.0.0` prints the section; missing-version case exits 1 with actionable message.
- Extractor tests green; changelog-lint workflow passes on the branch.

## Out of scope
- Conventional-commits automation / auto-generated changelogs (the human writes the changelog; the tooling only extracts), in-app release-notes rendering.

## Skills
None specific.
close_reason: desktop/CHANGELOG.md (Keep-a-Changelog, 1.0.0-Unreleased MVP backfill) + scripts/release-notes.mjs extractor (@calmly/scripts workspace) with unit tests incl. Unreleased guard; changelog-lint extended to desktop changelog. (ba24d3c)

title: REL-08: Desktop release CI pipeline — desktop-v* tags, 3-OS matrix, checksums, draft GitHub Release
description:
## Goal
Tag-driven desktop release pipeline: pushing `desktop-v*` builds, (optionally) signs, checksums, and publishes installers for Linux/Windows/macOS as a draft GitHub Release with real release notes.

## Context
- Style reference: `.github/workflows/release.yml` (sync server, `sync-v*` tags) — mirror its tag-prefix versioning and checksum discipline. Desktop uses a separate `desktop-v*` prefix so server and app release independently.
- Consumes: electron-builder config (REL-01/03/04), signing env contract (REL-05), release-notes script (REL-11), packaged smoke spec (REL-09).

## Scope
- `.github/workflows/desktop-release.yml`:
  - triggers: `push: tags: [desktop-v*]` + `workflow_dispatch` with a `dry_run` input (build everything, publish nothing);
  - version stamping: extract `${GITHUB_REF_NAME#desktop-v}`, write into desktop/package.json before build (single source: the tag);
  - matrix: ubuntu-latest / windows-latest / macos-latest; pnpm + node setup consistent with ci.yml; per-OS `dist` build;
  - signing env passthrough per REL-05 contract with graceful-skip;
  - Linux job additionally runs the REL-09 packaged smoke suite against its own artifact (fail = no release);
  - collect artifacts, generate `SHA256SUMS.txt` covering every installer + the electron-updater `latest*.yml` files, create DRAFT GitHub Release with notes from REL-11's extraction script (publishing the draft stays a human act);
  - concurrency group per tag; timeout-minutes on every job.
- Update docs/RELEASING.md with the end-to-end runbook: bump CHANGELOG → tag → CI → verify draft → publish → verify auto-update picks it up (v1.0.0→v1.0.1 dry-run procedure).

## Acceptance
- `workflow_dispatch` dry-run goes green on all three OS legs from the feature branch (this is the primary verification — do not burn real tags to test).
- Draft-release path verified once with a `desktop-v0.9.0-rc.1` style prerelease tag; artifacts + SHA256SUMS present; notes match the CHANGELOG section.
- actionlint (or at minimum `gh workflow view`/YAML parse) clean; no secrets echoed in logs.

## Out of scope
- Publishing the release (human), homebrew/winget/snap manifests, provenance attestation (future, matching the sync-server TODO).

## Skills
`security-review` for the workflow (secret handling, tag-injection into shell).

title: Telegram + Reminders: rebuild lost MVP scope (capture, commands, delivery engine)
description:
## Goal
Rebuild the Telegram-bot surface and the entire reminders delivery engine — MVP scope (PRD §7) that the tracker marked shipped but that never landed in the repo. After this epic, a linked user can capture text/voice from Telegram into their Inbox, use /now, /today, /inbox, and receive Important/Soft reminders on Telegram (desktop-notification fallback) with working Done / Snooze / Reschedule buttons.

## How this scope was lost (context for every child bead)
The 2026-05 autonomous loop closed beads TG-03b/04/05/06/07/08, TG-09d and RM-01/01b/01c/02/03/04/05/06/07/08 in the final "bd state sync — 222/222" pass, but the code existed only in worker sessions that were never pushed (crash — see the calmly-3py post-crash epic). Every branch on origin was checked (main, ralph/*): the code is gone. The original specs were sound; the child beads of THIS epic re-derive them, corrected to the code that DID land.

## What actually landed (build on it, do not duplicate)
- server/src/telegram/: bot.ts, webhook.ts (secret-validated), config.ts, dispatcher.ts (routes ONLY /start), linking.ts + linkingRoutes.ts (one-time codes, telegram_links), files.ts (getFile download helper, size caps), handlers/start.ts, handlers/voiceReplies.ts (PRD §13 error copy)
- server/src/transcription/: provider abstraction (OpenAI whisper + mock, env-selected)
- server/src/test-utils/: telegramBotMock.ts (TG-09a harness), telegramUpdates.ts (TG-09b payload builders)
- server Postgres (server/migrations/*.cjs): tasks, inbox_items (+external_ref UNIQUE, 0011), events, reminder_rules, recurrence_rules, telegram_linking_codes — reminder_rules IS in the sync entity list (shared/src/sync/types.ts), so desktop rules replicate to the server
- desktop: src/main/reminders/store.ts + IPC handlers (RM-01a; CRUD, MIN_INTERVAL_SECONDS=300), Settings shell (pages/Settings/Layout.tsx) — but pages/Settings/Reminders.tsx is a PLACEHOLDER and there is no Telegram settings page and no renderer reminder components

## Children (dependency-ordered)
- TGR-01 text capture → Inbox (rebuilds TG-03b)
- TGR-02 voice capture assembly (rebuilds TG-04 runtime; 4a/4b/4c components landed)
- TGR-03 outbound messages + action-button callback infra (rebuilds TG-07)
- TGR-04 /now + setMyCommands infra (rebuilds TG-05)
- TGR-05 /today + /inbox (rebuilds TG-06)
- TGR-06 desktop Settings → Telegram page + linking E2E (rebuilds TG-08 + TG-09d)
- TGR-07 desktop reminder UI: rule editor, badges, Settings page, Important/Soft treatment (rebuilds RM-01b/01c/02/07 renderer scope)
- TGR-08 server reminder scheduler + deliveries table (rebuilds RM-03)
- TGR-09 Telegram reminder channel (rebuilds RM-04)
- TGR-10 desktop notification fallback channel (rebuilds RM-05)
- TGR-11 Done/Snooze/Reschedule action handlers (rebuilds RM-06)
- TGR-12 reminders lifecycle integration pass, virtual clock (rebuilds RM-08)

## Blocks
This epic blocks calmly-y5z (v1.0 Desktop Release): shipping v1.0 without reminder delivery or Telegram capture contradicts PRD §7. The falsely-closed originals carry audit notes pointing here; do NOT reopen them.

## Done when
On a deployed server with TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN set: text and ≤5-min voice notes from a linked account create inbox items with acks; /now, /today, /inbox answer correctly; an Important rule fires on schedule to Telegram with three working buttons; an unlinked user gets the same reminder as a desktop notification; the full virtual-clock lifecycle suite is green in CI.

## References
PRD §7 (MVP scope), §11 (Capture/Reminders), §13 (error states), §14 (data model), §17 (cloud transcription). Original specs: calmly-unr, calmly-d0p.4–.8, calmly-91t.1–.8.

title: TGR-01: Inbound Telegram text -> InboxItem (idempotent writer + handler + dispatcher route)
description:
## Goal
Linked Telegram users capture by texting the bot: plain text → one `inbox_items` row (`source='telegram-text'`) → terse ack. Idempotent against Telegram webhook replays. Rebuilds lost TG-03b (calmly-unr) on the TG-03a schema that DID land.

## What exists (anchors — read these first)
- `server/src/telegram/dispatcher.ts` — routes only `/start`; already classifies updates text/voice/other in its log line. Extend, don't rewrite.
- `server/src/telegram/linking.ts` — telegram_links resolution used by handlers/start.ts.
- `server/migrations/0011_inbox_external_ref.cjs` — inbox_items.external_ref with the UNIQUE(user_id, external_ref) that makes idempotency work (TG-03a landed).
- Test harness: `server/src/test-utils/telegramBotMock.ts` + `telegramUpdates.ts` — build Updates and mock the Bot API; mirror `handlers/__tests__/` style.
- Sync invariants: rows must carry version=1, updated_at, deleted_at=NULL to replicate to desktop (see how server sync reads inbox_items — server/src/sync/).

## Scope
1. `server/src/inbox/createFromTelegram.ts` — pure pg.Pool writer:
   - `captureFromTelegram(pool, { chatId, telegramMessageId, rawText, now })` → `{ ok:true, inboxId, truncated, alreadyProcessed }` | `{ ok:false, error:'unlinked' }`
   - user_id from chat_id via telegram_links JOIN (single query)
   - `external_ref = 'tg:' + chatId + ':' + telegramMessageId`; ON CONFLICT (user_id, external_ref) DO UPDATE ... RETURNING with a discriminator so replays return alreadyProcessed:true
   - truncate raw_text at 4000 chars, flag it
2. `server/src/telegram/handlers/text.ts`:
   - ignore text starting with `/` (slash commands = other beads' routes)
   - unlinked → link prompt ("Link your account in Settings → Telegram first.")
   - linked → "Saved to inbox." (+ " (trimmed at 4000 chars)" when truncated); replays re-ack identically
   - non-text non-voice media → "I only handle text and voice notes for now."
3. Dispatcher: add the text branch; keep /start intact.

## Tests
`server/src/inbox/__tests__/createFromTelegram.test.ts` + `server/src/telegram/handlers/__tests__/text.test.ts` (mock pg.Pool + bot mock): linked happy path; unlinked; idempotent replay (no dup row, same ack); slash-command bypass; 5000-char truncation; media rejection. ≥ 12 tests.

## Acceptance
- All listed tests green; `pnpm --filter calmly-sync-server test` fully green
- typecheck:gated clean; eslint clean on touched files
- No PII (message text) logged at info level

## Out of scope
Voice (TGR-02), commands (TGR-04/05), outbound buttons (TGR-03).

title: TGR-02: Voice capture assembly — download -> transcribe -> InboxItem -> ack (components already landed)
description:
## Goal
Assemble the voice-capture pipeline from the three components that already landed: Telegram voice note → download (files.ts) → transcribe (transcription/) → inbox item (`source='telegram-voice'`) → ack/error copy (voiceReplies.ts). Rebuilds the lost TG-04 runtime layer (calmly-d0p.4).

## What exists (anchors)
- `server/src/telegram/files.ts` — getFile + download with size cap and TelegramDownloadError (TG-04b)
- `server/src/transcription/` — TranscriptionProvider interface, OpenAI whisper + mock providers, TRANSCRIPTION_PROVIDER env selection, TranscriptionError (TG-04a). Check `server/.env.example` for the key names it established.
- `server/src/telegram/handlers/voiceReplies.ts` — ALL user-facing reply strings for every failure mode + success ack with 80-char transcript truncation (TG-04c). Use these verbatim; do not write new copy.
- TGR-01's `captureFromTelegram` writer — extend or wrap for voice (source + meta differ), don't fork the idempotency logic.

## Scope
`server/src/telegram/handlers/voice.ts` orchestration + dispatcher voice branch:
- linked check first (reuse TGR-01 unlinked reply)
- duration guard BEFORE download: `message.voice.duration > 300s` → voiceReplyForTooLongDuration
- download via files.ts → transcribe via provider → create inbox item source='telegram-voice', raw_text=transcript, meta `{duration_sec, original_message_id}`; idempotency key same `tg:` scheme as text
- success → voiceReplySuccess ack; delete any temp artifacts
- TelegramDownloadError / TranscriptionError → mapped reply via voiceReplies.ts; NO inbox row; keep the download buffer path retry-friendly (original spec's 1h retained-file retry may be simplified to in-request behavior — if you simplify, say so in the bead close and update the epic body's Done-when accordingly)
- Never log the transcript at info level

## Tests
`handlers/__tests__/voice.test.ts` with MockProvider + bot mock: happy path (row + ack + truncated ack for long transcripts); too-long duration (no download attempted — assert via spy); each download error code → exact voiceReplies string; each transcription error code → exact string; replayed update → no dup row; unlinked. ≥ 14 tests.

## Acceptance

## Out of scope
Desktop display of voice items (inbox already renders source-tagged items), per-user transcription keys, transcoding.

title: TGR-03: Outbound Telegram infra — inline buttons, outbound_messages, callback router, action registry
description:
## Goal
Outbound-message substrate: send Telegram messages with inline action buttons, persist them for callback correlation, route button presses back to registered handlers. The reminders channel (TGR-09) and action handlers (TGR-11) plug into this. Rebuilds lost TG-07 (calmly-d0p.7).

## What exists (anchors)
- `server/src/telegram/bot.ts` getBot() — grammY instance; dispatcher.ts shows the send pattern (bot.api.sendMessage)
- `server/src/telegram/linking.ts` — chat_id resolution
- Migration format/numbering: `server/migrations/*.cjs` (knex-style, see _template.cjs). CAUTION: two 0009_* files already collide there — pick the next FREE number (0012+) and run the desktop-style collision check mentally; the calmly-wv9 CI gate only covers desktop/, a follow-up may extend it to server/.
- `shared/src/model/telegram.ts` — existing telegram types live here (NOT a new shared/src/types/ dir as the old spec said).

## Scope
1. Migration `outbound_messages`: id, user_id, chat_id, intent, payload jsonb, telegram_message_id, status ('sent'|'blocked'|'failed'), sent_at, created_at.
2. `server/src/telegram/outbound.ts`:
   - `sendMessage(pool, userId, { text, buttons: [{label, actionId, payload}] })` — resolves chat_id (throw TelegramNotLinkedError), persists row first, builds inline_keyboard with `callback_data = actionId + ':' + rowId` (≤64 bytes — payload lives in the DB row), sends, stores telegram_message_id
   - `editMessage(pool, outboundMessageId, { text, buttons })` — in-place edit, no new row
   - retry 3x exponential backoff on 5xx/network; 403 → status='blocked' + domain event (simple typed emitter or callback registry — match existing server event patterns if any; keep minimal)
3. `server/src/telegram/actions.ts` — `registerAction(actionId, handler)` registry.
4. `server/src/telegram/handlers/callback.ts` + dispatcher `callback_query` branch: parse callback_data, load row, dispatch to registry, always `answerCallbackQuery` (also on unknown action — log warn, generic "This button expired." toast).

## Tests
outbound.test.ts + callback.test.ts (pg mock + bot mock): linked send creates row with correct keyboard shape; unlinked throws, no row; button press dispatches with DB payload; unknown actionId answered gracefully; 403 → blocked + event spy; 5xx retried 3x then error; editMessage edits in place. ≥ 14 tests.

## Acceptance
Suites green; server tests green; typecheck:gated + eslint clean; migration applies on fresh pg (existing server migration test pattern — find and extend it; if none exists, note that gap in your report).

## Out of scope
Done/Snooze/Reschedule semantics (TGR-11), reminder formatting (TGR-09).

title: TGR-04: /now command + setMyCommands registration + MarkdownV2 helper

Determine "current focus" from the synced data model (shared/src/model/focus.ts + task.ts define the semantics; check whether focus sessions sync — see shared/src/sync/types.ts entity list). If focus state is desktop-only and does NOT sync, implement the documented fallback: reply with the highest-priority in_progress/today task, and note the limitation in the reply copy decision + your report.

title: TGR-06: Desktop Settings -> Telegram page (link code, polling, unlink) + linking E2E
description:
