title: TGR-08: Server reminder scheduler — deliveries table, next-fire math, channel router, retry/dedupe
description:
## Goal
Server-side reminder scheduler: interval worker that finds due reminder_rules (synced from desktop), creates reminder_deliveries rows, dispatches through a Channel interface, dedupes, retries with backoff, stops when the task is done. Rebuilds lost RM-03 (calmly-91t.3) — its spec is preserved below with corrections.

## Corrections to the original spec
- Migrations are `server/migrations/*.cjs` knex-style (see _template.cjs), NOT .sql. Two 0009_* files already collide — take the next free number and double-check no sibling bead claimed it.
- reminder_rules columns come from the synced desktop schema (desktop/src/main/reminders/store.ts: task_id, importance, interval_seconds, escalation_json, active, version — NO start_at/last_fired_at on the rule). Next-fire derives from the rule + its deliveries history + task state; design state.ts accordingly (pure functions, unit-tested).
- Fastify plugin lifecycle: register alongside existing plugins in server/src/app.ts; interval driver default 30s tick; graceful shutdown via Fastify onClose hook (server has SIGTERM handling — check index.ts).

## Scope (from RM-03, adjusted)
- Migration: reminder_deliveries (id, rule_id, user_id, task_id, scheduled_for, fired_at, channel, status pending/sent/failed/skipped/acked/snoozed, attempt_count, last_error, outbound_message_id, created_at)
- `server/src/reminders/state.ts` — pure next-fire math (UTC): first fire = rule activation + interval; repeat every interval_seconds while task not done and rule active; dedupe window = interval/2
- `server/src/reminders/scheduler.ts` — tick: query due rules (JOIN tasks for status; skip done/archived/deleted), create delivery, ChannelRouter.pickChannel(userId) → Channel.deliver; retry ≤3 with 1m/5m/15m backoff then failed
- `server/src/reminders/router.ts` + `channels/types.ts` — Channel interface `{ deliver(delivery): Promise<{ok:boolean; fallback?:boolean}> }`; router prefers telegram when linked else desktop; LogChannel for tests until TGR-09/10 land
- Cancel endpoint: POST /reminder-deliveries/:id/cancel (auth + ownership, existing route/middleware patterns)

## Tests
scheduler.test.ts + state.test.ts with vitest fake timers + mock channels: due rule fires once; done-task rule skipped; dedupe across double tick; 3-retry → failed; fallback signal routes to second channel; SIGTERM/onClose finishes in-flight tick without duplicating on restart (persisted state assertion); 1k-rule tick < 1s. ≥ 16 tests.

## Acceptance
Server suites green; typecheck:gated + eslint clean; migration applies cleanly on fresh pg in tests.

## Out of scope
Real channels (TGR-09/10), action semantics (TGR-11), calendar-event reminders, distributed locking (document single-process assumption in scheduler.ts header).

title: TGR-09: Telegram reminder channel — Important/Soft formats + Done/Snooze/Reschedule buttons
description:
## Goal
Telegram delivery channel for reminders: format Important/Soft messages, send via TGR-03's outbound infra with Done / Snooze 10m / Reschedule buttons, signal fallback for unlinked/blocked users. Rebuilds lost RM-04 (calmly-91t.4).

## Anchors
- TGR-03: outbound.sendMessage/editMessage, TelegramNotLinkedError, blocked domain event, action registry
- TGR-08: Channel interface, reminder_deliveries rows, router fallback semantics

## Scope (from RM-04, intact)
- `server/src/reminders/channels/telegram.ts`:
  - Important: `🔔 *<task title>*\nNext: <next step or '—'>` (MarkdownV2-escaped via TGR-04's helper); Soft: plain title
  - Buttons → actionIds `reminder.done` {deliveryId, taskId}, `reminder.snooze` {deliveryId, minutes:10}, `reminder.reschedule` {deliveryId, taskId} (handlers land in TGR-11 — register nothing here)
  - TelegramNotLinkedError → {ok:false, fallback:true}; blocked (403) → same + rely on TGR-03's event; other errors → {ok:false, fallback:false} so scheduler retries
  - success → delivery status='sent', store outbound_message_id
- Extend router.ts: prefer telegram when linked

## Tests
channels/telegram.test.ts (mock outbound): Important vs Soft formatting (exact strings incl. escaping), three button payload shapes, unlinked fallback (no send), blocked fallback, retryable error, outbound_message_id persistence. ≥ 10 tests.

## Acceptance
Server suites green; typecheck:gated + eslint clean.

## Out of scope
Button press behavior (TGR-11), desktop channel (TGR-10).

title: TGR-10: Desktop notification fallback channel (sync-transport delivery + native Notification)
description:
## Goal
Desktop-notification fallback channel: when Telegram is unlinked (or signals fallback), push the reminder over the existing sync transport to the desktop client, which raises a native Notification; clicking routes into the app. Rebuilds lost RM-05 (calmly-91t.5), simplified to the transport that actually exists.

## Reality check on the old spec (read before coding)
Inspect desktop/src/main/sync/ (loop, queue) + server/src/sync/ FIRST and determine how server→desktop data flows today (pull-based sync loop vs push stream). If there is no live push stream, implement the documented pragmatic variant: deliveries for channel='desktop' are exposed via a pull endpoint (e.g. GET /reminder-deliveries/pending) that the desktop sync loop polls on its existing cadence, acking via POST. State which variant you built in your report; do NOT build a websocket layer for this bead.

## Scope
- Server: `channels/desktop.ts` (marks delivery pending-for-desktop; returns ok), pending+ack endpoints (auth + ownership), 30-min staleness window (older pending deliveries → skipped)
- Desktop main: `reminders/notifier.ts` — on fetched pending delivery: `new Notification({ title, body })`, Important = 🔔-prefixed title, Soft plain; click focuses the app window and navigates to the task (use existing deep-link/navigation IPC pattern); ack after display
- Action buttons in native notifications are platform-flaky — the bead ships CLICK-to-open only; Done/Snooze/Reschedule from desktop happen in-app (TGR-11 exposes the action endpoint the app calls). Note Windows AppUserModelID: packaged builds have appId from the release epic; in dev log-and-toast fallback.
- reminder_deliveries.desktop_acked_at column (same migration-numbering caution as TGR-08).

## Tests
Server channel + endpoints tests (staleness window, ownership); desktop notifier unit tests with mocked Notification + mocked window/navigation (display, importance prefix, ack fired, dedupe on refetch). ≥ 12 tests.

## Acceptance
Server + desktop suites green; typecheck:gated + eslint clean; `pnpm --filter @calmly/desktop build` green.

## Out of scope
OS action buttons, quiet hours/DND logic (respect OS DND implicitly), TGR-11 semantics.

title: TGR-11: Done/Snooze/Reschedule action handlers (Telegram callbacks + HTTP action endpoint, idempotent)
description:
## Goal
The Done / Snooze / Reschedule semantics, wired to BOTH surfaces: Telegram button callbacks (TGR-03 registry) and an authenticated HTTP action endpoint (desktop in-app + notification click-through). Rebuilds lost RM-06 (calmly-91t.6).

## Anchors
TGR-03 (registry, editMessage), TGR-08 (deliveries + scheduler), TGR-09 (telegram channel, message formats), TGR-10 (desktop channel + endpoint patterns). PRD §4: Done acks the REMINDER, not the task (task completion from a reminder is a setting, default OFF — check UserSettings for an existing flag; if none, hardcode reminder-only and note it).

## Scope (from RM-06, adjusted)
- `server/src/reminders/actions.ts`: handleDone (delivery→acked, rule deactivated, telegram message edited to "Done ✓ <title>" no buttons), handleSnooze (delivery→snoozed, new delivery now+minutes, edit to "Snoozed until <HH:mm> — <title>"), handleReschedule (delivery→acked; Telegram: follow-up message with date chips Today evening / Tomorrow / In 2 days / Custom-on-desktop as callback buttons that update the task's scheduled date via the synced tasks table; desktop: respond with the taskId so the client navigates)
- Register all three (+ chip actions) with TGR-03's registry; add POST /reminder-deliveries/:id/action (auth + ownership)
- Idempotency: second action on an acked delivery is a no-op returning the current state (test double-press across surfaces)
- Audit: record actor surface + timestamp on the delivery row

## Tests
Per-handler suites: state transitions, message edits (exact strings), snooze rescheduling honored by scheduler (fake-timer integration with TGR-08), reschedule chips update task date + sync fields (version bump/updated_at), idempotent double-press, endpoint authz. ≥ 16 tests.

## Acceptance
Server suites green; typecheck:gated + eslint clean.

## Out of scope
Custom date-picker inside Telegram (chips only; Custom → "Open the app to pick a date"), desktop UI for actions beyond the endpoint contract.

title: TGR-12: Reminders lifecycle integration pass — 8 virtual-clock specs, both channels (epic exit gate)
description:
## Goal
Prove the whole rebuilt engine end-to-end with a virtual clock: rule → scheduled dispatch → channel → action → rescheduled fire, on both channels. Rebuilds lost RM-08 (calmly-91t.8). This is the epic's exit gate.

## Anchors
telegramBotMock.ts + telegramUpdates.ts (TG-09a/b), fake timers precedent in TGR-08's suite, all TGR-08..11 modules. Server integration tests that need Postgres follow the existing testcontainers pattern (see the skipped docker-gated specs in server/src — mirror how they gate on Docker availability so the suite skips cleanly where Docker is absent but RUNS in CI).

## Scope — the eight lifecycle specs (from RM-08)
1. rule creation → deliveries math (next fire computed)
2. telegram dispatch: linked user, advance clock → exactly one sendMessage with three buttons
3. desktop fallback: unlinked user → desktop channel called, telegram mock untouched
4. done: callback → delivery acked, rule deactivated, no further fires on advance
5. snooze 10m: new delivery at +10m fires on advance; original edited
6. reschedule: chip callback updates task scheduled date + acks
7. important vs soft: template differences asserted
8. escalation/repeat: Important interval=10m, +30m unacked → exactly 3 dispatches, no dupes within a tick

## Files
server/src/reminders/__tests__/lifecycle.integration.test.ts (+ helpers as needed). Keep runtime <10s via fake timers.

## Acceptance
All 8 specs green locally where Docker exists and in CI; whole server suite green; typecheck:gated + eslint clean. If CI lacks a job running docker-gated server integration specs, extend ci.yml minimally (mirror existing job style) so THIS suite runs on PRs — that gap is how the original loss went unnoticed.

## Out of scope
Desktop-side E2E of native notifications; quiet hours.
